title: B3 claim comparison on real article pairs
text: B3 claim comparison on real article pairs
why: Understanding needs each new statement checked against earlier ones as agree, contradict or gap; this tests whether a small CPU cross-encoder can do it (GO.md B3)
acceptance: On real sentence pairs from different articles that share a tag, the cross-encoder's non-neutral calls agree with Clef at least 60 percent, and it finds at least 60 percent of Clef's agree or contradict pairs.
One pair takes under 50 ms on one CPU thread.
steps: Build real pairs from labelled articles
Score with cross-encoder and Clef
Score against the bars and route

text: a criterion is over 200 characters
T17 started

PREDICT + DECISION RULE (GO.md B3; tags now exist offline from T15, so real pairs can be built; no made-up pairs). METHOD: from the 1,350 labelled articles (runs/tag_head/labels.jsonl, text re-read locally, never printed or written), take Clef-accepted tags that occur in 2 or more articles; for each, take one sentence (40 to 250 chars) per article that contains the tag and pair sentences from DIFFERENT articles: 300 TAGGED pairs (sampled over tags so no tag has more than 3 pairs), plus 100 UNRELATED control pairs (random sentences from two articles that share no tag). Models: cross-encoder/nli-deberta-v3-xsmall (local cache) gives entails / contradicts / neutral, one CPU thread; local Clef (port 8018, approved) answers two narrow yes/no questions per pair, each under 160 chars, one polarity: 'Does statement B say the same thing as statement A?' (agree) and 'Does statement B say the opposite of statement A?' (contradict); Clef label = contradict if that answer is 0.5 or more, else agree if the same-thing answer is 0.5 or more, else gap. Agreement with Clef, never accuracy: no human gold. PREDICT: Clef gap share of tagged pairs 75 to 92 percent (same-tag sentences from different stories mostly say different things), agree 5 to 20, contradict under 4 percent; the cross-encoder calls neutral on 80 to 95 percent; 3-class agreement with Clef 0.70 to 0.85 (mostly the gap class); of the cross-encoder's non-neutral calls, 40 to 70 percent match Clef (precision), and it finds 30 to 60 percent of Clef's agree or contradict pairs (recall); controls: both call at least 95 percent gap; one pair 15 to 40 ms on one CPU thread. DECISION RULE written now: the cross-encoder is READY for claim comparison if precision 0.60 or more AND recall 0.60 or more against Clef on the tagged pairs, AND under 50 ms per pair. With fewer than 15 Clef contradict pairs the contradict class is reported as UNMEASURED, not passed. If it misses, record the numbers and route: a larger cross-encoder (small, base: also local) is the next single test, and the pair builder must pick sentences that make claims (not just contain the tag). Weak or split results are recorded and routed, not argued.

RESULT (claim_test.py, runs/snapshots/claim_test_nli-deberta-v3-xsmall.json; run b3-claim-test; 300 TAGGED pairs from 846 tags found in 2+ articles, 100 UNRELATED controls, Clef 0 errors; agreement with Clef, never accuracy). CLEF labels on tagged: gap 287 (95.7 percent), agree 7 (2.3), contradict 6 (2.0). CROSS-ENCODER (xsmall) on tagged: neutral 255 (85.0), contradiction 40 (13.3), entailment 5. 3-class agreement 0.847 (almost all the gap class). Non-neutral calls: 45, matching Clef 13.3 percent (PRECISION 0.133); Clef found 13 non-neutral pairs, cross-encoder matched 46.2 percent of them (RECALL 0.462; 3 of 6 contradict, 3 of 7 agree). CONTROLS (unrelated sentences): Clef gap 100 percent, cross-encoder neutral 84 percent and called 15 of 100 'contradiction'. SPEED: p50 74.5 ms, p95 93.2 ms per pair, one thread. Contradict class: 6 Clef cases, under 15, so UNMEASURED by the rule. VERDICT vs L411: NOT READY (precision 0.133 vs 0.60, recall 0.462 vs 0.60, 74.5 ms vs 50). PREDICTIONS: Clef gap 75 to 92 MISSED (95.7, higher), agree 5 to 20 MISSED (2.3), contradict under 4 HELD; cross-encoder neutral 80 to 95 HELD (85); 3-class agreement 0.70 to 0.85 HELD (0.847, edge); precision 0.40 to 0.70 MISSED (0.133); recall 0.30 to 0.60 HELD (0.46); controls 95 percent gap MISSED (cross-encoder 84; Clef 100); 15 to 40 ms MISSED (74.5). LESSONS: (1) sentences that merely contain the same tag almost never make comparable claims (96 percent gap by Clef), so random same-tag pairs mostly test 'neutral'; the pair builder must pick sentences that make a claim about the same thing. (2) The xsmall model's 'contradiction' is not trustworthy on text outside its training style: 15 percent false contradictions on unrelated pairs. (3) 74 ms already misses 50 ms; a bigger model will be slower. ROUTING per L411: one more single test, the small cross-encoder (nli-deberta-v3-small, 141.9M) on the SAME 400 pairs, only to see whether precision rises; PREDICT: precision 0.20 to 0.45, controls neutral 90 to 98 percent, p50 120 to 250 ms; DECISION: if precision stays under 0.40 or controls under 90 percent neutral, stop trying bigger NLI models on this pair builder and route to a claim-aware pair builder (similarity-filtered sentence pairs plus an ONNX int8 speed test) as a new B3b; if precision is 0.60 or more the model is accurate and only speed remains (int8, shorter inputs, run only on candidate pairs). Task stays open (not done).

RESULT of the follow-up (nli-deberta-v3-small, same 400 pairs, run b3-claim-test-small, runs/snapshots/claim_test_nli-deberta-v3-small.json). Tagged: cross-encoder neutral 233, contradiction 62, entailment 5; non-neutral calls match Clef 11.9 percent (PRECISION 0.119); finds 61.5 percent of Clef's 13 agree or contradict pairs (RECALL 0.615, up from 0.462); controls: only 74 percent neutral, 25 of 100 unrelated pairs called 'contradiction' (xsmall: 15); p50 135.5 ms, p95 167.8 ms. PREDICTION vs L412: precision 0.20 to 0.45 MISSED (0.119), controls neutral 90 to 98 MISSED (74), p50 120 to 250 ms HELD. DECISION RULE (L412): precision under 0.40 and controls under 90 percent neutral => STOP trying bigger NLI models on this pair builder; route to B3b: a claim-aware pair builder (sentence pairs picked by embedding similarity and a claim filter, so the pairs can actually agree or contradict) plus an ONNX int8 speed test. Bigger model = more false contradictions and slower, not better. Both sizes miss all three bars; T17 closed at step 3 with the verdict NOT READY, not marked done.

title: B3b claim-aware pairs and int8 speed
text: B3b claim-aware pairs and int8 speed
why: B3 failed because same-tag sentences rarely make comparable claims (96 percent gap) and the xsmall model gave false contradictions; test pairs picked by similarity and claim filter, and an int8 speed fix (GO.md B3b)
acceptance: On high-similarity claim pairs the cross-encoder's non-neutral calls match Clef at least 60 percent and find at least 60 percent of Clef's agree or contradict pairs.
On unrelated pairs at most 5 percent are called contradiction.
The int8 model takes under 50 ms a pair on one CPU thread and flips under 5 percent of labels.
steps: Build similarity-banded claim pairs
Score fp32 and int8 with Clef
Score against the bars and route

text: T18 started

PREDICT + DECISION RULE (GO.md B3b; follows L412 and L413). METHOD: claim_pairs.py. SENTENCES: from the 1,337 labelled local articles, spaCy sentences of 50 to 250 characters that make a claim (contain a verb with a subject AND a named entity or a number). PAIRING: leaf vector of every sentence (5 ms each, CPU); for each sentence the nearest sentence in a DIFFERENT article; two bands by cosine: HIGH (0.75 or more) and MID (0.55 to 0.75); sample 150 pairs per band, no article in more than 2 pairs; plus the same 100 UNRELATED controls as B3 (random sentences, no shared tag). SCORING: cross-encoder/nli-deberta-v3-xsmall in fp32 and in int8 (torch dynamic quantisation of the linear layers, one CPU thread; a simpler stand-in for ONNX int8, named as such) on the same pairs; local Clef (approved) answers the same two narrow questions as B3 (same thing / opposite) for the Clef label. Agreement with Clef, never accuracy. PREDICT: Clef non-neutral share (agree + contradict) HIGH band 20 to 45 percent (vs 4.3 percent for same-tag pairs in B3), MID band 5 to 15; Clef contradict in HIGH 2 to 8 percent; xsmall fp32 on HIGH: precision 0.35 to 0.60, recall 0.50 to 0.80; controls: false contradiction 10 to 20 percent (unchanged from B3's 15); int8: p50 25 to 50 ms (1.5 to 3 times faster than fp32 74 ms), labels flip vs fp32 on 2 to 8 percent of pairs. DECISION RULE written now: (1) the pair builder works if the HIGH band Clef non-neutral share is 20 percent or more; (2) xsmall int8 is READY as the claim comparer only if on the HIGH band precision 0.60 or more AND recall 0.60 or more AND controls false contradiction 5 percent or less AND int8 p50 under 50 ms AND flips under 5 percent. With under 15 Clef contradict pairs in HIGH the contradict class is UNMEASURED. If it misses on precision or false contradictions, record it and route: the cross-encoder is not the comparer; claim pairs found by similarity are sent to Clef offline (as now), and the CPU side does only the finding (similarity), not the verdict. Weak or split results are recorded and routed, not argued.

RESULT (claim_pairs.py, runs/snapshots/claim_pairs.json; run b3b-claim-pairs; 22,578 claim sentences from 1,335 articles; 150 HIGH pairs (cos 0.75 or more, mean 0.804), 150 MID (0.55 to 0.75, mean 0.682), 100 unrelated controls; Clef 0 errors; agreement with Clef, never accuracy). PAIR BUILDER: Clef non-neutral share HIGH 22.7 percent (29 agree, 5 contradict of 150) vs 4.3 percent for B3's same-tag pairs, about 5 times more; MID only 2.7 percent. CROSS-ENCODER xsmall on HIGH: fp32 precision 0.16, recall 0.118; int8 precision 0.24, recall 0.176; it labels only 5 (fp32) or 9 (int8) pairs 'entailment' where Clef says 29 'same thing'. FALSE CONTRADICTION: HIGH 13.3 percent, MID 12 percent, controls 9 percent (fp32), 8 percent (int8). SPEED one thread: fp32 p50 71.1 / p95 84.1 ms; int8 p50 51.4 / p95 62.5 ms; int8 flips 4.5 percent of labels vs fp32. VERDICT vs L419: builder WORKS (HIGH 22.7 percent, bar 20); cross-encoder NOT READY on precision (0.24 vs 0.60), recall (0.176 vs 0.60), false contradictions (8 percent vs 5), speed (51.4 ms vs 50, missed by 1.4); only flips passed (4.5 vs 5). Contradict class UNMEASURED (5 cases, under 15). PREDICTIONS: HIGH non-neutral 20 to 45 HELD (22.7, low edge); MID 5 to 15 MISSED (2.7); HIGH contradict 2 to 8 HELD (3.3); precision 0.35 to 0.60 MISSED; recall 0.50 to 0.80 MISSED; controls false contradiction 10 to 20 MISSED (9 and 8, a little under); int8 p50 25 to 50 MISSED (51.4); flips 2 to 8 HELD. READING: Clef's 'same thing' is looser than the NLI model's strict entailment (Clef says yes to similar-topic restatements), so part of the gap is a definition difference between the two judges, recorded not resolved; no human gold to decide which is right. ROUTING per L419: the cross-encoder is NOT the comparer. The CPU side finds candidate claim pairs by leaf similarity plus a claim filter (about 5 times richer than tag pairs); the agree / contradict verdict stays with Clef offline. Task closed at step 3, not marked done.

title: B1b tag head with context (small MLP)
text: B1b tag head with context (small MLP)
why: The linear head sees one token at a time and missed its bars (T15); a small neural head with neighbour and article context is the cheap retry named in GO.md
acceptance: Finder loose F1 is at least 0.55 and at least 0.08 above the cheap no-spaCy baseline on the same 300 held-out articles.
Head cost stays under 10 ms per article on one CPU thread.
steps: Add context head to the T15 script
Train and score on three encoders
Score against the bar and route

text: T19 started

PREDICT + DECISION RULE (cheap retry named in GO.md and L397). METHOD: tag_head2.py = tag_head.py unchanged (same 1,345 articles, same 895 train / 150 val / 300 held-out split by article, same decode, same cheap and proposer baselines, same strict and loose F1 against Clef-accepted tags) except the head: a small MLP (input = the token vector, its left and right neighbour vectors and the mean vector of the article; 4 x 384 inputs, one hidden layer of 256, class-weighted, Adam, 6 epochs, CPU, torch) in place of logistic regression. Encoders: leaf, bge-small, granite (float32). Agreement with Clef, never accuracy. BASELINES (T15 final run): cheap loose 0.564, strict 0.396; proposer loose 0.721. T15 linear finder: leaf 0.437, bge 0.556, granite 0.570. PREDICT: MLP finder loose F1 leaf 0.50 to 0.60, bge 0.58 to 0.66, granite 0.60 to 0.68 (context should lift each by 0.04 to 0.10); chance granite clears the bar (0.644 = cheap + 0.08) about 30 percent; reranker loose gain over proposer 0.00 to 0.03 (under the 0.05 bar); head cost under 5 ms per article; granite and bge still beat leaf by 0.05 or more. DECISION RULE written now: the context head is worth keeping if its best encoder has finder loose F1 of 0.55 or more AND 0.08 above the cheap baseline (same paired bootstrap, lower bound above 0) at under 10 ms per article. If it misses, STOP tuning the head: tags stay offline, the CPU engine serves Pulse, and the idea of a CPU tag finder passes to an end-to-end span model on Kaggle only if the owner wants tags at serving time (hard cost question for the owner, not tried here). Weak or split results are recorded and routed, not argued.

RESULT (tag_head2.py, runs/snapshots/tag_head2.json; run b1b-tag-head-mlp; same method and scoring as T15 except the head: MLP over token + left + right + article mean). NOTE ON COMPARABILITY: the queue cleared the text of 15 articles since T15 (1,335 usable, 885 train / 150 val / 300 test), so the held-out set is NOT the T15 set; compare only inside this run (baselines re-measured on this test set: cheap loose 0.582 / strict 0.414; proposer loose 0.722 / strict 0.613). FINDER loose/strict: leaf 0.582/0.367, bge-small 0.649/0.432, granite 0.658/0.436. RERANKER loose/strict: leaf 0.750/0.683, bge 0.755/0.688, granite 0.772/0.697. Paired bootstrap loose [95% CI]: leaf finder minus cheap -0.000 [-0.030,0.030]; leaf reranker minus proposer +0.028 [0.008,0.049]; bge minus leaf +0.067 [0.041,0.095]; granite minus leaf +0.076 [0.051,0.103] (granite and bge versus the cheap baseline were not bootstrapped; per-article scores were not saved: a gap in this script). READ against L426: FINDER bar (0.55 AND +0.08 over cheap): best is granite 0.658 = +0.076 over cheap 0.582: MISS by 0.004, inside the run-to-run spread of about 0.02 seen in T15; rule says stop, and the bar is not moved. The context lifted the best finder from 0.570 to 0.658 (+0.088 on a similar set) and every encoder gained. RERANKER (bar +0.05 over proposer, reported only): granite +0.050 on the point estimate (0.772 vs 0.722), leaf +0.028; granite's interval not computed; at the line. SPEED: the 131 to 222 ms per article in the log is NOT the head's cost (the timer includes building the context features with numpy over the whole test set); the true MLP cost is unmeasured, so the under-10-ms bar is UNMEASURED. PREDICTIONS: finder leaf 0.50 to 0.60 HELD (0.582), bge 0.58 to 0.66 HELD (0.649), granite 0.60 to 0.68 HELD (0.658); granite clears 0.644 (cheap + 0.08): MISSED by 0.004 (30 percent chance given); reranker gain 0.00 to 0.03 MISSED high for granite (+0.05), HELD for leaf (+0.028); head cost under 5 ms: UNMEASURED; granite and bge still beat leaf by 0.05 or more: HELD (+0.076, +0.067). DECISION per L426: miss => STOP tuning the head. Tags stay offline; CPU engine serves Pulse. The finding for the owner: a context head with granite is within 0.004 of the bar, so a CPU tag finder is plausible; whether to pursue tags at serving time is a cost and scope question (more tuning here, or an end-to-end span model on Kaggle GPU hours), not a method step. Task closed at step 3, not marked done.

title: Pulse end-to-end extraction rate, all six fields
text: Pulse end-to-end extraction rate, all six fields
why: Owner target 2026-11-01: get through all macro (Pulse) fields and reach a high extraction rate; the 88 percent figures rest on 84 to 96 found items, not the whole stream
acceptance: Each of the six Pulse fields shows an end-to-end rate on a sealed fresh set of 1,500 or more items, with n and a 95 percent interval.
Ready means at least 80 percent agreement with Sonnet on at least half of the stream, per the engine card rule.
No choice is made on the sealed set; it is scored once at the end.
steps: Fix the measuring stick: sealed set, end-to-end rates
Condition reach sweep (round 1)
Chain fields at scale, topic decision
Traits pilot on 1,000 items
Sealed final run and Engine card

text: steps are 1 to 4 outcomes of at most 60 characters
T20 started

PLAN (owner target 2026-11-01: Pulse first, extraction rate; Area and Understanding probes of today are parked). FACTS CHECKED on the engine card v5-leaf, agreement with Sonnet never accuracy: story type 0.911 on 1,466 of 1,466; topic top-2 0.883 and top-1 0.731 on 1,466; condition present 0.889 on 609 of 1,466 (answers 51 percent of the stream) but it finds only 10.3 percent of real conditions (reach, n 675); which condition 0.875 (CI 0.794 to 0.927) on 96 items; direction 0.917 (0.838 to 0.959) on 84; size within one 0.881 (0.795 to 0.934) on 84. So the owner's reading holds: the three 88 percent figures rest on 84 to 96 items (about 6 percent of the test set), and only on cases the engine already found. The same 1,466-item set scored v1 through v5 (13 ledger lines name it), so encoder and version choices were compared on it: it is no longer sealed. Traits (51 questions, 8 groups) not started. TARGET (to confirm): per Pulse field, the share of ALL stream items where the engine answers AND agrees with Sonnet (end to end; for the condition chain, reach x agreement), on a sealed fresh set; Ready = 80 percent agreement on at least half the stream (the card's rule). STEPS: (0) fix the stick: count Sonnet labels already held, carve a dev set and a sealed set of 1,500+ never used for choices, report every field end to end with n and interval; label cost estimate first if more labels are needed, inside the 70 USD cap, owner told; (1) condition reach, round 1: sweep threshold, per-condition cutoffs, class weights, encoder on all items, 3+ seeds, on dev; output the reach versus agreement curve (this replaces the two-tier question A2 with the real trade-off); pass: 50 percent of true conditions found at 80 percent agreement, or a measured proof the current features cannot; (2) which condition, direction and size trained and measured on 300+ found items (grows as reach grows), topic one-guess versus two-guess decision with the numbers; (3) traits pilot: 1,000 items labelled by Sonnet (cost estimate first), linear heads on the existing trunk, per-question agreement and answered share, ready groups named; (4) one sealed final run, Engine card update (cp.mjs engine), speed and memory check. Any engine change is built as a CHALLENGER version, never replacing v5-leaf without the owner's yes. LOOP: rounds, not single runs: one prediction and decision rule per round, 3+ seeds, per-item scores saved, intervals on every verdict, parallel runs on the 20 cores, wake on completion, no stop between rounds; stop only at the hard gates. PARKED with results recorded: tags (T15, T19), router (T16), claim comparison (T17, T18); they belong to Area and Understanding.

STEP 0 PREDICT + DECISION RULE (fix the measuring stick). FACTS: engine trains on Haiku labels of items dated BEFORE the last fifth of the pool; the last fifth (about 9,300 items) is the test period; Sonnet labelled 7,710 items in total, enriched for items with a condition (3,326 of 7,710) so scoring re-weights to the natural stream; the 1,466 test items are the Sonnet-labelled ones in the last fifth; the other test-period items (about 7,800) have a Haiku label, no Sonnet label, and were never used for training or choices. Sonnet batch costs 0.0015 USD per item (7,710 items = 11.36 USD). DESIGN: from the unlabelled test-period items, drop exact-text twins of training or dev items and the near-duplicate list, then draw at random, fixed seed, 4,000 items: DEV2 (2,000, labelled by Sonnet now with the frozen spec, about 3 USD, hosted, headline+description only, inside the L119 pre-authorisation of 70 USD, owner told) and SEALED (2,000, ids and a SHA-256 of the id list written to the ledger NOW, labelled by Sonnet only at step 4, so no sealed label exists while we choose anything). DEV = the old 1,466 (acknowledged as reused, condition-enriched, re-weighted) plus DEV2 (natural random). SCORER (score_end2end.py): per field the share of ALL items where the engine answers AND agrees with Sonnet, with Wilson 95 percent intervals; the chain is reach x P(which right) x P(direction right | which right) x P(size within one | which right), each factor shown. PREDICT on DEV2 (natural, v5-leaf): story type 0.89 to 0.93 on 100 percent; topic top-2 0.85 to 0.90, top-1 0.70 to 0.76; condition positives (Sonnet has a condition) 15 to 35 percent of items; condition_present agreement 0.85 to 0.92 on 40 to 60 percent answered; reach (found real conditions) 6 to 15 percent; which-condition among found 0.80 to 0.92; direction 0.85 to 0.95; size within one 0.82 to 0.92; chain end to end (found and which, direction, size all right) under 10 percent of real conditions. DECISION RULE: (1) if story type and topic top-2 on DEV2 are within 0.03 of the old 1,466 figures (0.911, 0.883) the old Pulse numbers are CONFIRMED as representative; a gap of more than 0.03 means the old set is retracted for that field and DEV2 numbers replace it on the Engine card; (2) the end-to-end rate per field becomes the number on the card from now on, next to the old per-answered figure; (3) if fewer than 150 Sonnet-condition items exist in DEV2, add a second DEV2 tranche before step 1 (cost about 3 USD per 2,000). Sealed ids and hash are written before any DEV2 label is seen.

SEALED SET LOCKED (before any DEV2 label exists). Correction to L435: the test period holds 4,954 dated items (not about 9,300), 3,488 of them unused and unlabelled by Sonnet; split: SEALED 1,500 ids (runs/pulse/sealed_ids.txt, SHA-256 39d9ecc6ceb8b45ca151401d1ab7accd3fa3b639253254d3e4357d6646bdbcd0, labelled by Sonnet only at step 4) and DEV2 1,988 ids (runs/pulse/dev2_ids.txt, labelled now). Rule: no model, threshold, feature or version is chosen using the sealed ids; their labels do not exist until the final run; any read of them before step 4 is a breach to be logged. About 22,000 undated Haiku-labelled pool items were never used in training or tests either; kept in reserve for a second, differently-distributed check.

STEP 0 FINDINGS BEFORE DEV2 (scorer score_end2end.py validated on the old 1,466; reach_pilot.py). (1) WEIGHTING: re-weighted to the natural stream, v5-leaf story type is 0.884 (CI 0.861 to 0.904) and topic top-2 0.870 (0.845 to 0.891), vs the card's 0.911 and 0.883 which are unweighted on the condition-enriched set (effective n 845 of 1,466); DEV2 (natural, unweighted) decides which is right. (2) CHAIN end to end of real conditions: found 0.103; given found: which 0.909 (n 96), direction 0.941 (n 84), size within one 0.916 (n 84); all right end to end 0.080 (CI 0.055 to 0.116) of real conditions. (3) REACH PILOT (v5-leaf): on items both teachers marked as having a condition (573) the raw classifier says yes on 46.4 percent but only 15.7 percent clear the confidence cut; Sonnet+ but Haiku- (102): says yes 21.6, found 5.9; false alarms are rare (Sonnet- and Haiku-: found 0.8 percent). So most of the missing reach is the cut, which was set for 80 percent precision; the curve of reach against agreement is the step-1 deliverable. (4) TEACHER CEILING: Haiku and Sonnet agree on condition presence on 72.3 percent of the 1,466 (Haiku marks 59.8 percent positive, Sonnet 46.0); the engine trains on Haiku and is scored against Sonnet, so an 80 percent bar on presence is above what the training teacher itself reaches. Earlier test L226: training on 6,244 Sonnet labels gave AUC 0.764 vs 0.743 (Haiku-trained), answerable at 80 percent 51 vs 40 percent, so the presence signal in these features is weak (AUC about 0.76). ROUTE: round 1 of step 1 sweeps (a) the cut/curve, (b) training target (Haiku, Sonnet, both-agree, blend), (c) encoder on every item not only the routed third, (d) per-condition heads vs one presence head, (e) head type; 3+ seeds, intervals; chosen on the old set and DEV2, never on sealed.

STEP 1 PILOTS (look before the sweep; runs/pulse/presence_pilot.json, presence_learning_curve.json; AUC of the condition-PRESENCE head against Sonnet on the old 1,466, re-weighted to the natural stream; today the presence gate uses only word and character counts, no encoder). (1) ENCODER FOR PRESENCE: sparse words+chars, Haiku-trained 0.734, Sonnet-trained 0.744, blend of both 0.755 (what the engine does); sparse + leaf vector: 0.748, 0.758, blend 0.766 (+0.011); leaf vector alone: 0.719 to 0.734. The encoder does NOT unlock presence. (2) LEARNING CURVE on Sonnet-labelled training items, sparse+leaf, 3 seeds: 750 items 0.689 (sd 0.020), 1,500 0.713, 3,000 0.744, 6,000 0.758 (one run); gain per doubling 0.024, 0.031, 0.014: it is flattening; reading the curve forward, 12,000 Sonnet labels would give about 0.77 and 24,000 about 0.78 (an extrapolation, not a measurement). 6,000 Sonnet labels beat 36,070 Haiku labels (0.758 vs 0.748), so Sonnet labels are worth much more per item (cost 0.0015 USD each, so 20,000 more is about 30 USD). (3) With Haiku and Sonnet agreeing on presence on only 72.3 percent of items (L437), the signal ceiling for any student trained on these features looks like AUC about 0.78, which keeps reach at 80 percent agreement low (10 to 20 percent). READ: the presence limit is the reader plus label noise, not the cut or the encoder. OPEN TEST (cheap, next): Sonnet self-consistency on presence (relabel about 400 DEV2 items with the same frozen spec, about 0.6 USD): if Sonnet agrees with itself on presence only about 80 percent, an 80 percent bar on presence is at the noise ceiling and the owner's rule needs a presence-specific reading; if Sonnet is stable at 92 percent or more, label noise is not the limit and a stronger reader is needed.

SETS CORRECTED (supersedes the split in L436; the sealed hash 39d9ecc6... is RETRACTED, unused, nothing was labelled from it). TWO ERRORS FOUND IN MY STEP-0 DESIGN: (1) the unlabelled remainder of the test period is not a natural sample: every item where Haiku saw a condition or the gate flagged it was already Sonnet-labelled, so the 3,488 left are Haiku-negative and unflagged; the first 378 DEV2 labels confirm it (7 of 378 = 1.9 percent have a Sonnet condition; natural weighted share on the old set is 25.9 percent). Those 378 labels (runs/pulse/dev2, 0.57 USD) are kept only as a stratum check: Sonnet-positive rate among Haiku-negative, unflagged test-period items is about 2 percent. (2) the labelling job stopped at 378 because the batch tool's worst-case price guard (0.0158 USD per item assumed vs 0.0015 actual) trimmed it to the 6 USD cap; actual spend 0.57 USD. NEW SETS from items the engine has never seen and that are later than all training and test data: the 5,504 queue items published 2026-10-29 to 2026-11-02 whose text is not in the pool (same length, category and country mix as pooled items: mean 307 vs 310 characters, general 74 percent vs 71, US/IN/WORLD/NG the top countries). Natural random draws: SEALED = 1,500 random from the latest 2,800 by publication time (ids and SHA-256 written to the ledger before any label exists; labelled only at step 4); DEVQ = 2,000 random from the earlier rest (labelled by Sonnet now, about 3 USD, worst-case guard raised to 32 USD, spend reported). Item text = title + '. ' + teaser, the same form as pool items. DECISION RULE unchanged from L435 except: the natural positive rate and the old-set weighting are now compared on DEVQ, and story/topic agreement from DEVQ replaces the card figures if it differs from the old ones by more than 0.03.

SEALED SET LOCKED (v2, before any DEVQ or SEALED label exists): runs/pulse/sealed_q_ids.txt, 1,500 queue items published 2026-10-31 00:06 to 2026-11-02 01:08 UTC, SHA-256 a455c630ce4662d0931ea6ae7196141bdd82caac1c2dce89bf8617e4eb83411f, read-only file. DEVQ: runs/pulse/devq_items.jsonl, 2,000 queue items published 2026-10-29 to 2026-10-31. Rule: no model, threshold, feature or version is chosen using the sealed items; their labels are made only at step 4; any read of them before then is a breach to be logged. Hosted spend notice: Sonnet batch labelling of 2,000 headline+teaser items now, expected about 3 USD (0.0015 per item measured), job ceiling set to 32 USD only because the tool prices the worst case at 0.0158 per item; owner pre-authorisation L119 (70 USD, stop and report at each 10 USD mark).

PREDICT + RULE: Sonnet SELF-CONSISTENCY (the noise ceiling for any student). 400 random items from the 8,088 Sonnet-labelled (stratified by presence like the old set: 200 with a Sonnet condition, 200 without), relabelled by Sonnet with the same frozen spec in a new batch (about 0.6 USD, hosted, headline+description, inside L119). PREDICT agreement of the second label with the first: story type 0.93 to 0.97, topic 0.88 to 0.94, condition presence 0.85 to 0.92, same top condition among the items both mark positive 0.75 to 0.88, direction 0.88 to 0.96. RULE: if presence self-agreement is 0.90 or more, label noise is not what limits the student and a stronger reader is the lever; if 0.85 or less the 80 percent bar on presence sits at the teacher's own noise ceiling and the owner needs a presence-specific reading (bar vs ceiling shown together); between: report both and keep step 1 as planned.

PREDICT + RULE: HAIKU SELF-CONSISTENCY on the same 400 items as the Sonnet self-consistency test (L441), same frozen Haiku spec, new batch, about 0.04 USD (Haiku measured 0.0001 per item), hosted, headline+description, inside L119. Purpose: owner asked whether Sonnet is better than Haiku as a labeller; with no human gold, stability is the one thing we can measure: a labeller that disagrees with itself is noisy whatever it is anchored to. PREDICT Haiku agrees with its own first label less than Sonnet does: story type 0.88 to 0.94, topic 0.82 to 0.90, presence 0.78 to 0.88 (Sonnet predicted 0.85 to 0.92). RULE: if Haiku's self-agreement on presence is 0.05 or more below Sonnet's (non-overlapping 95 percent intervals) Sonnet is the less noisy labeller and the extra cost (about 16 times per item) buys stability; within 0.03 the two are equally stable and their disagreement (71 percent on presence) is a difference in definition, not noise. Stability is not correctness: no human gold exists.

STEP 0 RESULT (DEVQ, v5-leaf; score_end2end.py, runs/pulse/end2end_v5-leaf_devq.json; 1,997 natural random queue items published 2026-10-29 to 10-31, after all training and test data, weight 1; agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy). STORY TYPE 0.875 (CI 0.860 to 0.889) on 100 percent of the stream. TOPIC top-2 0.896 (0.882 to 0.909), top-1 0.747 (0.727 to 0.765), 100 percent answered. CONDITION PRESENT: answers 80.3 percent of items, agrees 0.966 when it answers (mostly the no cases), end to end 0.776. NATURAL SHARE with a Sonnet condition: 11.1 percent (221 of 1,997); the old set's weighting implied 25.9 percent, which was too high. CHAIN on the 221 real conditions: found 0.199 (CI 0.152 to 0.257; the old set gave 0.103), which condition right given found 0.864 (0.733 to 0.936, n 44), direction 0.921 (n 38), size within one 0.947 (n 38); all three right end to end 0.149 (0.108 to 0.202). DECISION RULE (L435) applied: story type DEVQ 0.875 vs card 0.911 = gap 0.036, over 0.03: the card figure is replaced by 0.875; topic top-2 0.896 vs 0.883 within 0.03: confirmed. PREDICTIONS: story 0.89 to 0.93 MISSED (0.875); topic top-2 0.85 to 0.90 HELD; topic top-1 0.70 to 0.76 HELD; Sonnet-positive share 15 to 35 percent MISSED (11.1); presence agreement 0.85 to 0.92 on 40 to 60 percent answered MISSED (0.966 on 80, dominated by negatives); reach 6 to 15 percent MISSED (19.9, higher); which 0.80 to 0.92 HELD; direction 0.85 to 0.95 HELD; size 0.82 to 0.92 MISSED high (0.947, inside the interval); chain end to end under 10 percent MISSED (14.9). Chain fields now have n 38 to 44 found items: still thin. Cost of DEVQ labels about 3 USD. STRATUM CHECK (dev2, 378 Haiku-negative unflagged items): 1.9 percent Sonnet-positive.

SELF-CONSISTENCY RESULT (L441, L442; same frozen spec, same 400 items stratified 200 Sonnet-positive / 200 negative, second batch; compare_selfcons.py; agreement of a labeller with its own first label; 399 and 396 items). SONNET: story 0.992, topic 0.982, presence 0.970 (CI 0.948 to 0.983), same top condition when both positive 0.974 (n 193), direction 0.992, size 1.000. HAIKU: story 0.980, topic 0.917 (0.885 to 0.940), presence 0.838 (0.799 to 0.871; positives 0.869, negatives 0.775), same top condition 0.935 (n 232), direction 0.988, size 1.000. RULE (L442): Haiku presence self-agreement is 0.13 below Sonnet's, intervals do not overlap: SONNET IS THE LESS NOISY LABELLER, the extra cost (about 16 times per item) buys stability. RULE (L441): Sonnet presence self-agreement 0.97 is over 0.90: label noise in the TEACHER is not what limits a student scored against Sonnet; a stronger or better-fed reader is the lever. READ TOGETHER: Haiku and Sonnet agree on presence only 71 to 72 percent, Haiku agrees with itself 84 percent, Sonnet with itself 97 percent: part of the Haiku-Sonnet gap is Haiku noise (the engine trains on 36,000 Haiku labels), part is a definition difference; the owner's prompt idea (same prompt for both, so the model reads it differently) is consistent with this. PREDICTIONS: Sonnet presence 0.85 to 0.92 MISSED high (0.97); Haiku presence 0.78 to 0.88 HELD (0.838); both models more stable than predicted on story, topic and top condition. CAVEAT: stability is not correctness, and a batch rerun with the same settings may be near-deterministic for Sonnet; no human gold exists. IMPLICATION for step 1: Sonnet labels are worth more per item than Haiku labels (cost 0.0015 vs 0.0001), consistent with L438 (6,000 Sonnet beat 36,000 Haiku).
T20 step 1 Fix the measuring stick: sealed set, end-to-end rates

ROUND 1 (step 2 of T20, condition reach) PREDICT + RULE. 1a, CUT FRONTIER (no retraining, v5-leaf heads, encoder on every item, presence cut and which-condition cut swept; DEVQ 1,997 natural split in two halves at random: choose the cuts on half A, report on half B, then swap and average; old 1,466 re-weighted as a second view). Output: for each pair of cuts, CHAIN PRECISION = items where the engine emitted a condition, direction and size and all three match Sonnet / items where it emitted a chain (an emission where Sonnet has no condition counts as wrong), and CHAIN RECALL = all-right / Sonnet-positive items; frontier = best recall with precision at or above 0.80 (the card's bar), plus the recall at precision 0.70 and 0.60. PREDICT: today's cuts sit at precision about 0.9 and recall about 0.15; at precision 0.80 recall rises to 0.20 to 0.30 (the raw classifier says yes on 46 percent of items both teachers marked, L437); at precision 0.60 recall 0.35 to 0.50; the three tiers of the owner question become points on this curve. 1b, TRAINING TARGET (retrain, 3 seeds): which-condition head trained on Haiku conditions (today) vs Sonnet conditions of the 6,000 Sonnet-labelled training-period items vs both with Sonnet weighted 5 times; presence blend weights (Haiku head vs Sonnet head) 0/1, 0.5/0.5, 0.25/0.75, 0/1; PREDICT Sonnet-trained which-condition head lifts chain recall at precision 0.80 by 0.03 to 0.08 and presence blend toward Sonnet by 0.02 to 0.05. DECISION RULE written now: a change is ADOPTED as a challenger (v6-*, never replacing v5-leaf without the owner's yes) if chain recall at precision 0.80 rises by 0.05 or more on half B with interval lower bound above 0 across the two swaps; otherwise recorded as no gain and the next lever is tried (per-condition cuts, more Sonnet labels). If the frontier shows recall at precision 0.80 under 0.30 for every variant, the reach target of 50 percent is not reachable with this feature set and the finding goes to the owner with the curve.

ROUND 1a RESULT (cut frontier; frontier.py, reach_curve.py, runs/pulse/reach_frontier_v5-leaf.json, raw_v5-leaf.json; DEVQ 1,997 natural, 221 Sonnet-positive; cuts chosen on half A and reported on half B, 20 splits, plus the old 1,466 re-weighted). CHAIN = condition, direction and size all match Sonnet; a chain emitted where Sonnet has no condition counts as wrong. Half-B chain recall at chain precision target 0.80: 0.099 (CI 0.038 to 0.145) at actual precision 0.65; target 0.70: recall 0.159 (0.121 to 0.216); target 0.60: 0.223 (0.177 to 0.289). Old set: lower (0.05, 0.09, 0.16). The cuts do not reach 0.80 chain precision out of sample. PREDICTION MISSED (recall at 0.80 was 0.20 to 0.30; at 0.60 0.35 to 0.50). My reading in L437 that most missing reach was the cut was WRONG as a lever for the full chain: lowering the cut buys recall only by losing precision. STAGE DECOMPOSITION on DEVQ: PRESENCE alone at probability >= 0.60 emits 94 items, 83.0 percent are Sonnet-positive (presence precision 0.830), finds 35.3 percent of the 221 real conditions; >= 0.75: 48 emitted, precision 0.917, recall 0.199; >= 0.50: 127 emitted, precision 0.748, recall 0.430. WHICH-CONDITION (38-way) top-1 inside Sonnet's set on all 221 positives, no cut: 0.805; top-2: 0.910; it rises to 0.866 where confidence >= 0.4 (84 percent of positives) and 0.905 at >= 0.5 (71 percent). Given the right condition: direction 0.904, size within one 0.899 (n 178). So the stages multiply: 0.805 x 0.904 x 0.899 = 0.65 for the full triple even with perfect presence. ERROR TAXONOMY of the 94 emitted at presence >= 0.6, cond >= 0.2: 54 all right (57 percent), 16 Sonnet has no condition, 13 wrong condition, 7 right condition wrong direction, 4 size off by 2 or more. READING: (a) the owner's 88 to 92 percent figures are each conditional on the previous stage; the full chain is about 65 percent right when the condition is real; (b) the levers are presence recall at high precision, the which-condition head (0.805 top-1), and the definition of the chain target itself (a per-field rate versus all-three-right). NEXT: round 1b retrains the which-condition head on Sonnet conditions and the presence blend, same DEVQ and old evaluation.

ROUND 1b RESULT (round1b.py, runs/pulse/round1b.json; DEVQ 221 positives and old 675 positives; no hosted calls). WHICH-CONDITION top-1 inside Sonnet's set (C=3, sparse+leaf): Haiku rows (5,782) DEVQ 0.805 [0.748, 0.852], old 0.775 [0.742, 0.805]; Sonnet rows (3,224) DEVQ 0.805, old 0.782; Haiku + Sonnet x5 DEVQ 0.796, old 0.807 [0.776, 0.835]. All inside each other's intervals: NO GAIN from the training teacher (prediction +0.03 to +0.08 chain recall MISSED). PRESENCE (AUC DEVQ / old weighted; recall at presence precision 0.83 DEVQ / old weighted): current engine blend 0.896 / 0.755; 0.330 / 0.103. Sparse+leaf Sonnet weight 0.0: 0.920 / 0.748; 0.163 / 0.016. Weight 0.5: 0.920 / 0.766; 0.276 / 0.069. Weight 0.75: 0.907 / 0.766; 0.276 / 0.095. Weight 1.0: 0.881 / 0.758; 0.267 / 0.107. The encoder lifts AUC on the natural set by 0.024 but does NOT lift recall at 83 percent precision (the current sparse blend is best at the top end). DECISION RULE (L446): no variant raises chain recall at precision 0.80 by 0.05: nothing is adopted; no challenger version built. CORRECTION OF THE CARD: the old set is condition-enriched and its re-weighting assumed 25.9 percent positives; natural DEVQ has 11.1 percent. On natural data presence finds 33 percent of real conditions at 83 percent precision (card said reach 10 percent) and 19.9 percent at the current cut; AUC 0.896 natural vs 0.755 on the old set. The stage-level picture on natural data: given a real condition the later stages pass the card's rule (which-condition 0.866 on 84 percent of real conditions at confidence >= 0.4, direction 0.904, size 0.899); the weakness is DETECTION (presence recall at high precision) and the compounding of the stages (0.65 for the full triple).

ROUND 1c PREDICT + RULE: PER-CONDITION DETECTORS (lever d of L446). Replace the single presence gate by 38 one-vs-rest logistic heads (one per condition) trained on sparse (condition-relevant columns) + leaf vector, separately on Haiku labels (36,070 items) and on Sonnet labels (6,000 training-period items); presence score = noisy-OR and max over the 38 calibrated probabilities, also blended with the current presence score. Evaluate on DEVQ and old exactly as 1b (AUC, recall at presence precision 0.83) plus the best condition per item as a which-condition answer (argmax head) vs the 0.805 top-1 baseline. PREDICT: AUC DEVQ 0.90 to 0.93, recall at precision 0.83 on DEVQ 0.33 to 0.45 (the single gate lumps 38 different concepts); argmax head top-1 0.78 to 0.84. DECISION RULE: ADOPT as a challenger (v6-ovr, not replacing v5-leaf without the owner's yes) if recall at precision 0.83 on DEVQ rises by 0.08 or more AND the old-set weighted recall does not fall, with 200-resample bootstrap lower bound above 0; if it gains under 0.03 the single-gate design is not the limit and the finding goes to the owner (detection recall of about a third at 83 percent precision with this feature family; next levers cost money or GPU: more Sonnet labels, a stronger encoder).
T10 engine card: BitMob Expert 1 v5-leaf

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready = agreement 80% or more on 30+ items, answering half the stream or more. Partial = reaches 80% only on part of the stream, or only on cases it already found. Not yet = under 80%. Later phase = not built.

layers.name: Macro / Pulse
layers.asks: What is changing, and where? One expert reads each item once and answers all of these.

fields.label: Story type
fields.what: Fact, forecast, opinion or unclear

fields.label: Topic
fields.what: One of 49 topics, two guesses

fields.label: Condition present
fields.what: Does the story report a change in one of 38 world conditions

fields.label: Which condition
fields.what: Names it, among the items where it found one

fields.label: Direction
fields.what: Up or down

fields.label: Size
fields.what: How big, within one step of Sonnet's level

fields.label: Traits (51 questions, 8 groups)
fields.what: Movement, direction and effect, intent, risk, scale, certainty, time, importance

layers.name: Area (drill into one thing)
layers.asks: Pick something from the Pulse, such as a capability, and see what drives it, depends on it and is affected by it. Pilot done (L384): tags can be proposed on the CPU and verified by Clef, but agreement is only moderate, so the design is a hybrid.

fields.label: Things and capabilities
fields.what: Find entities, places, concepts and capabilities in the item and link each to one stable identity. Pilot: about 5 tags per full article, 3 per headline item; reading the whole article adds 56% new tags.

fields.label: Events and relations
fields.what: What happened, who took part, and how things connect. Related tags (Gaza / Gaza Strip / Palestinians) merge by similarity; identity needs entity linking.

layers.name: Understanding (downstream, does not block)
layers.asks: One consolidated explanation per capability, whoever said it, traced back to its sources. Where do new items agree, disagree or leave gaps?

fields.label: Consolidated knowledge
fields.what: How a capability works and best practice across the field, merged from many sources

fields.label: Agree, contradict, gap
fields.what: Check each new item against what we know and flag what is new or missing

fields.label: Claim, evidence, source
fields.what: Every statement traced to the source text it came from; the raw documents stay but are not the focus

next.headline: Biggest gap: finding real conditions, and the chain after it
next.body: Measured on 1,997 natural, never-seen queue items (agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy): story type 0.875 and topic (two guesses) 0.896 on every item; one topic guess 0.747. Only 11% of the stream has a condition. The engine says 'no condition' correctly on almost all of the rest (0.966 when it answers, answering 80%). Of the real conditions it finds 20% at today's cut and 33% at 83% right. Given a real condition the later fields pass: which condition 0.87 on 84% of them, direction 0.90, size 0.90, but the three together are right about 65% of the time. Earlier figures (reach 10%, story 0.911) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced. Tried and no gain so far: lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training on Sonnet instead of Haiku conditions.
next.ask: Decide: (1) which capability sources to take in; (2) condition tiers: read them from the reach-versus-right curve (T20, L447); (3) do tags run on the CPU at serving time or stay an offline Clef step.

tried_groups.name: What worked
tried_groups.summary: Word counts and static vectors for everything, a frozen small encoder on routed items (now mdbr-leaf-mt, 22.6M), and regularisation tuned on a validation slice (topic +0.02, topic overfitting gap 0.103 to 0.042).

items.what: Word counts + logistic regression alone
items.result: Story type at teacher level (0.90), topic weak (0.54)
items.outcome: Kept for story type and as the always-on path

items.what: Static word vectors (potion-8M) + logistic regression
items.result: Topic 0.62; confidence is trustworthy (calibration error 0.04)
items.outcome: Kept (the base of every version)

items.what: Frozen bge-small encoder features added
items.result: Which-condition top-1 0.704 to 0.770, top-2 0.828 to 0.905
items.outcome: Adopted, routed items only (v3)

items.what: Tuning regularisation (C) of the topic heads on a validation slice
items.result: Topic top-2 0.857 to 0.877; topic gap 0.103 to 0.059; story unchanged (best C stays 3)
items.outcome: Adopted as v3.2

items.what: Swapping the encoder bge-small for MongoDB/mdbr-leaf-mt, picked from a scan of all 215 scored models
items.result: Pulse fields tie; 95% of reads under 22.6 ms vs 36.6; 643 MB vs 724; neighbour topic agreement 0.683 vs 0.648; chunked late-passage recall 0.859 vs 0.867
items.outcome: Adopted as the trunk (all three adoption rules held)

tried_groups.name: Swapping the trunk (Granite small R2)
tried_groups.summary: Ties with bge-small on every Pulse field (short items). On whole articles a bigger window beats truncating at 512, but chunking bge-small beats one long Granite pass and costs far less CPU. Plan for long articles: bge-small chunks feeding tag-level joins.

items.what: ibm-granite/granite-embedding-small-english-r2 as the shared encoder (47.7M, Apache-2.0, 8k, ModernBERT), same heads and items
items.result: Topic top-2 0.881 vs 0.877, which-condition 0.875 vs 0.863, all inside the noise; encoder alone 23 ms; engine p95 44.5 ms vs 36.2; memory 837 MB vs 732
items.outcome: bge-small stays; revisit when Area needs token-level heads

items.what: Long-term features: joining quality and long-input cost, Granite vs bge-small
items.result: Neighbour topic agreement 0.634 vs 0.648; cluster agreement (NMI) 0.383 vs 0.408; 8,192 tokens 22 s vs about 3.9 s chunked
items.outcome: Granite not ahead; one test left (token-level tagging head, needs the Area tag labels)

items.what: Whole-article test: can a passage from the late part find its article? (1,500 long articles, median 1,078 tokens)
items.result: bge truncated 0.50; Granite whole article 0.64; bge chunked mean 0.77; bge best chunk 0.87 (recall@1, late passages)
items.outcome: Owner's logic holds (bigger window beats truncation); chunking a small model wins

tried_groups.name: Bigger or tuned neural models
tried_groups.summary: Fine-tuning, int8 and distilling the encoder were not better, or not fast enough.

items.what: Fine-tuning the encoder
items.result: First try much worse (topic top-2 0.726); corrected try +0.014 on topic but worse on which-condition
items.outcome: Rejected: frozen features beat it

items.what: int8 encoder to make it fast enough
items.result: Topic top-2 drops 0.019 against a 0.01 limit
items.outcome: Rejected; cascade instead

items.what: Distilling the encoder into static vectors
items.result: Keeps none of the encoder's lift (topic top-2 0.813 vs 0.832)
items.outcome: Rejected

tried_groups.name: Outside language models (d1, LFM3)
tried_groups.summary: d1 is a strong second opinion (topic 0.926 when combined) but needs the GPU and its licence does not fit. LFM3 is unusable.

items.what: d1-2B decision model, zero-shot, on the GPU
items.result: Alone: topic top-2 0.852. Fused with our student: topic top-2 0.926, condition top-1 0.834
items.outcome: Pipeline test only: GPU, and a licence the owner called not commercially viable

items.what: LFM3-1.7B as a JSON reader
items.result: Only 28% valid JSON; as a yes/no scorer AUC 0.54 to 0.61
items.outcome: Rejected

tried_groups.name: Teaching tricks
tried_groups.summary: Training our student on d1's soft labels gave no gain.

items.what: Training the student on d1's soft labels
items.result: Topic top-2 -0.008, story -0.006, which-condition +0.009 to +0.02
items.outcome: No gain; d1 stays a live second opinion

tried_groups.name: Free-form tags (pilot: 100 articles, 100 headline items)
tried_groups.summary: CPU proposes, Clef verifies: about 3 tags per headline item, 5.4 per full article; wording agreement about 0.5; 77% of tags occur once. Capabilities are 7% of general-news tags and 23% of tech-news tags, and almost never recur across articles: news can propose capability candidates but cannot supply the capability layer. Design: a hybrid.

items.what: Tag pilot with spaCy proposer and local Clef verifier (5 narrow yes/no questions per candidate)
items.result: 41% of 2,762 candidates accepted; kappa 0.49 to 0.53; merge at cosine 0.80 cuts distinct tags by 33% but merges related, not only identical, tags; 56% of full-article tags are absent from the short version
items.outcome: Hybrid design; capability layer needs tech sources; a token-level tag head is the serving route (the proposer takes 0.7 s per item)

text: TRAITS PILOT PREDICT + RULE (plan step 3, started early while round 1c runs; decision D6: wording tested per model before use). SPEC: specs/traits_v1_sonnet.json and traits_v1_haiku.json, identical apart from the model: the 51 draft questions of traits_v0 verbatim, each answered on the same 5-step scale (not at all, slightly, clearly, strongly, cannot tell), a guideline that says use only what the item says and answer 'cannot tell' when the item gives no basis; no few-shot examples (a pilot of the bare wording). SET: the first 150 DEVQ items (natural, headline+teaser). RUNS: Sonnet twice and Haiku twice, new batches, hosted, headline+description only, inside L119; expected cost under 2 USD in total (Sonnet 51 answers per item is about 3 times the output of the 4-field label: 0.004 USD per item assumed). MEASURE per question and per group: valid-reply rate; 'cannot tell' share; self-agreement (same answer, and within one step) for each model across its two runs; Sonnet-vs-Haiku agreement (same, within one step) on run 1. PREDICT: valid replies 97 to 100 percent; 'cannot tell' 10 to 35 percent overall; Sonnet self-agreement within one step 0.90 to 0.96, exact 0.70 to 0.85; Haiku self-agreement within one step 0.82 to 0.92; Sonnet-Haiku within one step 0.80 to 0.90; at least 8 of the 51 questions have Sonnet self-agreement within one step under 0.85 (ambiguous wording). RULE: a question is READY TO LABEL if both models answer it validly, Sonnet self-agreement within one step is 0.90 or more and Sonnet-Haiku within one step is 0.80 or more; questions failing either go back for rewording (never silently dropped), reported per group. If under 30 of 51 questions are ready, the traits wording is revised before any 1,000-item labelling spend.

ROUND 1c RESULT (per-condition detectors; round1c.py, runs/pulse/round1c.json; 38 one-vs-rest heads on sparse+leaf; DEVQ 221 positives, old 675). Recall at presence precision 0.83 on DEVQ vs the current gate's 0.330: Haiku-trained noisy-OR 0.276, max 0.244, blend with current 0.290; Sonnet-trained noisy-OR 0.244, max 0.204, blend 0.326. Bootstrap gain vs current [mean, 2.5, 97.5]: best (Sonnet blend) -0.022 [-0.135, 0.107]; every variant at or below zero. AUC DEVQ 0.88 to 0.914 (current 0.896); old weighted 0.72 to 0.76. The argmax head as which-condition answer: DEVQ top-1 0.774 (Haiku) and 0.796 (Sonnet) vs 0.805 today; old 0.776 and 0.782. PREDICTION (recall 0.33 to 0.45, +0.08 adopt rule) MISSED. DECISION RULE (L449): gain under 0.03 => the single-gate design is NOT the limit; nothing adopted, no challenger built. ROUND 1 SUMMARY: five levers tried (cut, encoder in the presence gate, Sonnet vs Haiku target for the which head, presence blend weights, 38 per-condition detectors); none moves recall at 83 percent precision above 0.33 on natural data. The limit is the reader family (word counts, static and 22M-encoder vectors with linear heads) and the 11 percent base rate. Levers left that cost money or compute: a stronger encoder or fine-tuned reader (fine-tuning was rejected in L292 to L296 on topic and condition), many more Sonnet labels (curve flattens near AUC 0.78, L438), or Clef/Jev as a second reader on flagged items (hybrid; owner wanted CPU).

TRAITS PILOT RESULT (analyze_traits_pilot.py, runs/pulse/traits_pilot_result.json; 150 DEVQ items, Sonnet x2, Haiku x2, bare wording, 0.90 USD total, valid replies Sonnet 150 and 150, Haiku 149 and 149). BY THE RULE OF L451 (Sonnet self within one step >= 0.90 and Sonnet-Haiku within one step >= 0.80): 50 of 51 questions READY; the one failing is x039 in the time group (Sonnet says 'cannot tell' on 66 percent, Sonnet-Haiku within one 0.52). Overall: Sonnet self within one 0.997, exact 0.962; Haiku self within one 0.985; Sonnet-Haiku within one 0.956; 'cannot tell' 1.6 percent (time group 19 percent); no question under 0.85 self-agreement (predicted at least 8: MISSED). HONEST READ: the rule is lenient. 71.5 percent of all answers are 'not at all'; on the items where either run says anything else, Sonnet agrees with itself exactly 0.868 (mean over questions) but Sonnet and Haiku agree exactly only 0.357: they disagree on DEGREE (slightly / clearly / strongly) even where both see the trait. Two questions are almost never active in 150 natural items (x050 importance: 0 items; x024 intent: 4). PREDICTIONS: valid replies 97 to 100 HELD; cannot-tell 10 to 35 MISSED low (1.6; time group 19); Sonnet self within one 0.90 to 0.96 MISSED high (0.997); Haiku self within one 0.82 to 0.92 MISSED high (0.985); Sonnet-Haiku within one 0.80 to 0.90 MISSED high (0.956). ROUTE: Sonnet alone is the traits teacher (stable on degree: 0.87 exact on active answers; Haiku is a different grader, as for conditions); the within-one rule is too easy to be the readiness test for the student, so the student bar is set below. Cost: about 0.0025 USD per Sonnet item (4 runs 0.90 USD).

TRAITS STEP PREDICT + RULE (plan step 3). DATA: Sonnet labels the 51 trait questions (bare wording of specs/traits_v1_sonnet.json, unchanged) on 1,500 random training-period pool items (TRAIN) and 1,000 DEVQ items from position 150 on (EVAL; the 150 pilot items, Sonnet run 1, are added, EVAL = 1,150); about 2,650 items at 0.0025 = 6.6 USD, worst-case guard raised to 25 USD, hosted, headline+description, inside L119; running total this session about 12 USD of the 70. STUDENT: one head per question on the cached leaf vector plus sparse word and character counts (linear, CPU, no new engine file), trained on TRAIN, scored on EVAL (3 bootstrap resamples for intervals). SCORE per question: exact agreement with Sonnet's grade, the majority-class baseline (always 'not at all', about 0.71), lift over it, and AUC for 'active vs not at all'. BAR set now: a question is READY for the engine if exact agreement >= 0.80 AND lift over the majority baseline >= 0.05 on EVAL. PREDICT: mean exact agreement 0.78 to 0.84, mean lift 0.03 to 0.08, 12 to 28 of the 51 questions READY, best groups direction_effect and risk (concrete, keyword-driven), weakest certainty, importance and intent. RULE: groups with at least half their questions READY go on the Engine card as 'traits: partial' with the ready list; questions that fail go back for reword or wait for more labels; the 51-question draft is not declared done on the pilot alone.

ROUND 2 PREDICT + RULE (owner challenge 2026-11-02: no visible movement on story, topic, condition, which, direction, size, traits; the page shows labelling jobs, not progress). LEVER NEVER TESTED ON STORY AND TOPIC: train them on Sonnet's labels. Today's engine learns story type and topic from 36,070 Haiku labels, and is scored against Sonnet; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story 93 percent and topic 83 to 86 percent, so a Haiku-trained student has a ceiling near those figures, while Sonnet agrees with itself 99 percent and 98 percent. We hold 6,000 Sonnet-labelled training-period items (cost to add more 0.0015 USD each). TEST (round2_story_topic.py, CPU, local): same features (word+char counts + leaf vector), same linear head, three training targets: Haiku labels (36,070), Sonnet labels (6,000), both (Haiku + Sonnet x5); scored on DEVQ (1,997 natural, Sonnet labels) with Wilson 95 percent intervals; control = the Haiku-trained row (the engine's linear path equivalent). PREDICT: story type Haiku-trained 0.86 to 0.88, Sonnet-trained 0.88 to 0.93; topic top-1 Haiku-trained 0.70 to 0.75, Sonnet-trained 0.72 to 0.80; top-2 Haiku 0.86 to 0.89, Sonnet 0.87 to 0.92. RULE: if Sonnet-trained or mixed beats the Haiku-trained control by 0.02 or more on story type or topic top-1 with intervals that do not overlap, it is a CHALLENGER (v6-sonnet-target, built as a new version, the owner told, v5-leaf stays until the owner says); if the gain is under 0.02 the Haiku ceiling is not the limit for those two fields. Cost: none (labels already held). A learning curve on Sonnet labels (1,500 / 3,000 / 6,000) is run in the same job so the value of buying more labels is read from a measured slope, not guessed.

IMPROVEMENT PATH + LOOP (owner 2026-11-02: set an improvement path and loop; make movement visible). GOAL FIELDS AND HONEST STATE on natural DEVQ (1,997 items, agreement with Sonnet): story 0.875; topic top-1 0.747, top-2 0.896; condition present 0.966 when it answers (80 percent answered); real conditions found 19.9 percent (33 percent at 83 percent right); given a real condition: which 0.866, direction 0.904, size 0.899, all three right 0.65; all-right of ALL real conditions 14.9 percent; traits: 50 of 51 questions pass the lenient pilot rule, student pending. TARGETS (to beat, written now): story 0.875 to 0.90; topic top-1 0.747 to 0.80 (top-2 stays 0.89+); real conditions found at 83 percent right 0.33 to 0.50; all-right of real conditions 0.15 to 0.40; traits per question exact agreement 0.80 and +0.05 over always-'not at all'. LEVER BACKLOG, ranked by expected gain per cost (each lever = one prediction + rule note, run on DEVQ and old with intervals, adopted only as a challenger version, v5-leaf stays until the owner says): L0 SCOREBOARD on the Engine page: per field v1 / v5 / natural-now / target / last change, plus a 'what changed' list that shows wins AND levers tried with no gain (UI, cheap, first; refreshed after every round). L1 Sonnet-target training for story and topic (running, L455 rule +0.02, learning curve gives the value of buying labels). L2 STACKED presence model: gradient-boosted trees on [presence blend, 49 topic probabilities, story probabilities, top which-condition probabilities, text length], out-of-fold on training items, Sonnet-weighted; bar: recall at 83 percent precision on DEVQ +0.08 with bootstrap lower bound above 0; CPU, free. L3 SECOND-STAGE READER on the uncertain presence band only (probability 0.3 to 0.75, about 15 percent of items): a stronger local encoder (granite-small, bge-base, gte-modernbert-base are cached) or the cross-encoder zero-shot DeBERTa; bar: recall at 83 percent precision +0.10 AND p95 of the whole engine under 50 ms on one thread (measured); CPU, free. L4 MORE SONNET LABELS (0.0015 USD each; 15,000 items about 22 USD; money, reported at each 10 USD): only after L1 and L2 show a measured slope worth buying. L5 topic encoder on every item (gate removed): bar +0.01 top-1 at p95 under 50 ms. L6 direction and size heads on Sonnet conditions: only after detection moves. L7 traits students per group (running). LOOP RULES: every tick (a) if a run finished, score it against its written bar, record the result, and update the scoreboard; (b) a WIN note ('WIN: field, before, after, interval, lever') when a bar is met, a 'NO GAIN' note when not; (c) take the next lever immediately without waiting; run up to 3 CPU jobs in parallel; (d) one prediction note per round, three or more seeds or bootstrap intervals, per-item scores saved; (e) hosted spend reported at each 10 USD of the 70 USD pre-authorisation (about 19 USD used this session so far, mostly traits and DEVQ labels); (f) STOP only at hard gates: a challenger replacing v5-leaf, money past 70 USD, deleting data, anything outward-facing; (g) the sealed 1,500 are scored once, at the end. WAKE: completion of background jobs wakes me; fallback heartbeat 20 minutes.

text: T20 engine card: BitMob Expert 1 v5-leaf

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready = agreement 80% or more on 30+ items, answering half the stream or more. Partial = reaches 80% only on part of the stream, or only on cases it already found. Not yet = under 80%. Later phase = not built.

layers.name: Macro / Pulse
layers.asks: What is changing, and where? One expert reads each item once and answers all of these.

fields.label: Story type
fields.what: Fact, forecast, opinion or unclear

fields.label: Topic
fields.what: One of 49 topics, two guesses

fields.label: Condition present
fields.what: Does the story report a change in one of 38 world conditions

fields.label: Which condition
fields.what: Names it, among the items where it found one

fields.label: Direction
fields.what: Up or down

fields.label: Size
fields.what: How big, within one step of Sonnet's level

fields.label: Traits (51 questions, 8 groups)
fields.what: Movement, direction and effect, intent, risk, scale, certainty, time, importance

layers.name: Area (drill into one thing)
layers.asks: Pick something from the Pulse, such as a capability, and see what drives it, depends on it and is affected by it. Pilot done (L384): tags can be proposed on the CPU and verified by Clef, but agreement is only moderate, so the design is a hybrid.

fields.label: Things and capabilities
fields.what: Find entities, places, concepts and capabilities in the item and link each to one stable identity. Pilot: about 5 tags per full article, 3 per headline item; reading the whole article adds 56% new tags.

fields.label: Events and relations
fields.what: What happened, who took part, and how things connect. Related tags (Gaza / Gaza Strip / Palestinians) merge by similarity; identity needs entity linking.

layers.name: Understanding (downstream, does not block)
layers.asks: One consolidated explanation per capability, whoever said it, traced back to its sources. Where do new items agree, disagree or leave gaps?

fields.label: Consolidated knowledge
fields.what: How a capability works and best practice across the field, merged from many sources

fields.label: Agree, contradict, gap
fields.what: Check each new item against what we know and flag what is new or missing

fields.label: Claim, evidence, source
fields.what: Every statement traced to the source text it came from; the raw documents stay but are not the focus

next.headline: Biggest gap: finding real conditions, and the chain after it
next.body: Measured on 1,997 natural, never-seen queue items (agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy): story type 0.875 and topic (two guesses) 0.896 on every item; one topic guess 0.747. Only 11% of the stream has a condition. The engine says 'no condition' correctly on almost all of the rest (0.966 when it answers, answering 80%). Of the real conditions it finds 20% at today's cut and 33% at 83% right. Given a real condition the later fields pass: which condition 0.87 on 84% of them, direction 0.90, size 0.90, but the three together are right about 65% of the time. Earlier figures (reach 10%, story 0.911) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced. Tried and no gain so far: lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training on Sonnet instead of Haiku conditions.
next.ask: Decide: (1) which capability sources to take in; (2) condition tiers: read them from the reach-versus-right curve (T20, L447); (3) do tags run on the CPU at serving time or stay an offline Clef step.

tried_groups.name: What worked
tried_groups.summary: Word counts and static vectors for everything, a frozen small encoder on routed items (now mdbr-leaf-mt, 22.6M), and regularisation tuned on a validation slice (topic +0.02, topic overfitting gap 0.103 to 0.042).

items.what: Word counts + logistic regression alone
items.result: Story type at teacher level (0.90), topic weak (0.54)
items.outcome: Kept for story type and as the always-on path

items.what: Static word vectors (potion-8M) + logistic regression
items.result: Topic 0.62; confidence is trustworthy (calibration error 0.04)
items.outcome: Kept (the base of every version)

items.what: Frozen bge-small encoder features added
items.result: Which-condition top-1 0.704 to 0.770, top-2 0.828 to 0.905
items.outcome: Adopted, routed items only (v3)

items.what: Tuning regularisation (C) of the topic heads on a validation slice
items.result: Topic top-2 0.857 to 0.877; topic gap 0.103 to 0.059; story unchanged (best C stays 3)
items.outcome: Adopted as v3.2

items.what: Swapping the encoder bge-small for MongoDB/mdbr-leaf-mt, picked from a scan of all 215 scored models
items.result: Pulse fields tie; 95% of reads under 22.6 ms vs 36.6; 643 MB vs 724; neighbour topic agreement 0.683 vs 0.648; chunked late-passage recall 0.859 vs 0.867
items.outcome: Adopted as the trunk (all three adoption rules held)

tried_groups.name: Swapping the trunk (Granite small R2)
tried_groups.summary: Ties with bge-small on every Pulse field (short items). On whole articles a bigger window beats truncating at 512, but chunking bge-small beats one long Granite pass and costs far less CPU. Plan for long articles: bge-small chunks feeding tag-level joins.

items.what: ibm-granite/granite-embedding-small-english-r2 as the shared encoder (47.7M, Apache-2.0, 8k, ModernBERT), same heads and items
items.result: Topic top-2 0.881 vs 0.877, which-condition 0.875 vs 0.863, all inside the noise; encoder alone 23 ms; engine p95 44.5 ms vs 36.2; memory 837 MB vs 732
items.outcome: bge-small stays; revisit when Area needs token-level heads

items.what: Long-term features: joining quality and long-input cost, Granite vs bge-small
items.result: Neighbour topic agreement 0.634 vs 0.648; cluster agreement (NMI) 0.383 vs 0.408; 8,192 tokens 22 s vs about 3.9 s chunked
items.outcome: Granite not ahead; one test left (token-level tagging head, needs the Area tag labels)

items.what: Whole-article test: can a passage from the late part find its article? (1,500 long articles, median 1,078 tokens)
items.result: bge truncated 0.50; Granite whole article 0.64; bge chunked mean 0.77; bge best chunk 0.87 (recall@1, late passages)
items.outcome: Owner's logic holds (bigger window beats truncation); chunking a small model wins

tried_groups.name: Bigger or tuned neural models
tried_groups.summary: Fine-tuning, int8 and distilling the encoder were not better, or not fast enough.

items.what: Fine-tuning the encoder
items.result: First try much worse (topic top-2 0.726); corrected try +0.014 on topic but worse on which-condition
items.outcome: Rejected: frozen features beat it

items.what: int8 encoder to make it fast enough
items.result: Topic top-2 drops 0.019 against a 0.01 limit
items.outcome: Rejected; cascade instead

items.what: Distilling the encoder into static vectors
items.result: Keeps none of the encoder's lift (topic top-2 0.813 vs 0.832)
items.outcome: Rejected

tried_groups.name: Outside language models (d1, LFM3)
tried_groups.summary: d1 is a strong second opinion (topic 0.926 when combined) but needs the GPU and its licence does not fit. LFM3 is unusable.

items.what: d1-2B decision model, zero-shot, on the GPU
items.result: Alone: topic top-2 0.852. Fused with our student: topic top-2 0.926, condition top-1 0.834
items.outcome: Pipeline test only: GPU, and a licence the owner called not commercially viable

items.what: LFM3-1.7B as a JSON reader
items.result: Only 28% valid JSON; as a yes/no scorer AUC 0.54 to 0.61
items.outcome: Rejected

tried_groups.name: Teaching tricks
tried_groups.summary: Training our student on d1's soft labels gave no gain.

items.what: Training the student on d1's soft labels
items.result: Topic top-2 -0.008, story -0.006, which-condition +0.009 to +0.02
items.outcome: No gain; d1 stays a live second opinion

tried_groups.name: Free-form tags (pilot: 100 articles, 100 headline items)
tried_groups.summary: CPU proposes, Clef verifies: about 3 tags per headline item, 5.4 per full article; wording agreement about 0.5; 77% of tags occur once. Capabilities are 7% of general-news tags and 23% of tech-news tags, and almost never recur across articles: news can propose capability candidates but cannot supply the capability layer. Design: a hybrid.

items.what: Tag pilot with spaCy proposer and local Clef verifier (5 narrow yes/no questions per candidate)
items.result: 41% of 2,762 candidates accepted; kappa 0.49 to 0.53; merge at cosine 0.80 cuts distinct tags by 33% but merges related, not only identical, tags; 56% of full-article tags are absent from the short version
items.outcome: Hybrid design; capability layer needs tech sources; a token-level tag head is the serving route (the proposer takes 0.7 s per item)

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.
