changes.text: Next levers for finding real conditions; bars written in advance (ledger L456).

text: PAGE FIX (owner 2026-11-02: two jobs were running and not on the page). Cause: I started the trait student (train_traits.py) and the topic/story test (round2_story_topic.py) without a heartbeat, against my own standing rule (GO.md: the page is the truth). Fixed in three layers: (1) both running jobs registered with their PID (t20-traits-student, t20-r2-topic-sonnet-target); the poller refreshes any heartbeat that records a pid and marks it failed if the process vanishes unreported; (2) NEW WATCHDOG kit/live/heartbeat.py watch_untracked(), called by the poller every 180 s: any python or node process whose working directory is inside knowledge_pipeline, older than 60 s, not named by any heartbeat pid, and not a known service, gets an automatic row 'UNREGISTERED: <command>' on the Live tab and is closed with 'ended; exit status unknown' when it exits (tested with a dummy 100 s job: row appeared, then closed to history); the viewer server and the poller are excluded; (3) poller restarted by verified PID (1527200 to 85033), kit/live/poller.pid updated. Starter scripts must still register why / success / next; the watchdog is the safety net, not the plan. Backups of the two edited files are in the session scratchpad. After the fix the page lists running jobs: poller, t20-r2-topic-sonnet-target, t20-traits-student.

ROUND 2, STORY TYPE RESULT (L455; round2_story_topic.py, runs/pulse/round2_story_type.json; DEVQ 1,997 natural, linear head on word+char counts + leaf vector, same learner for every row; agreement with Sonnet). Haiku-trained 36,070 labels [control] 0.877 [0.862, 0.891]; Sonnet-trained 6,000 labels 0.894 [0.880, 0.907]; Haiku + Sonnet x5 0.887 [0.873, 0.900]. LEARNING CURVE on Sonnet labels: 1,500 items 0.879, 3,000 0.886, 6,000 0.894: about +0.008 per doubling, still rising. RULE (L455): gain 0.02 or more with non-overlapping intervals => challenger; Sonnet-trained is +0.017 with overlapping intervals => by the written rule NO CHALLENGER YET (miss by 0.003 on the size and on the overlap). PREDICTION: Haiku-trained 0.86 to 0.88 HELD (0.877); Sonnet-trained 0.88 to 0.93 HELD (0.894). READ: a sixth of the data, from the better labeller, beats the Haiku bulk; the curve extrapolates (not measured) to about 0.90 at 12,000 and 0.91 at 24,000 Sonnet labels, which would cost about 9 and 27 USD of labelling. The bar is not moved. Decision parked until topic reports: if topic shows a similar slope, buying 15,000 to 20,000 Sonnet labels (lever L4, 22 to 30 USD, reported at each 10 USD) pays on story, topic and presence together.

ROUND 3 / LEVER L2 PREDICT + RULE: STACKED PRESENCE MODEL (l2_stack.py). Features per item, all produced by components that did NOT train on these items: engine Haiku-head and Sonnet-head presence logits, presence logits from sparse+leaf heads (trained on the training period), the engine's linear topic probabilities (49) and story probabilities (4), the which-condition head's top confidence and top-2 gap, text length. Stacker: gradient-boosted trees (scikit-learn HistGradientBoosting) and a logistic stack, 5-fold cross-validation over DEVQ (1,997 natural) + the old 1,466 (old items weighted to the natural stream, so the stacker is not trained on the enrichment), trained and scored out of fold; METRIC = recall of real conditions at presence precision 0.83, reported on the DEVQ items only (natural) with a 200-resample paired bootstrap against the current gate on the same items. PREDICT: current gate 0.33 on DEVQ; stacked 0.38 to 0.48 (topic and story give context: money-and-prices topics make a price condition likely, sports topics make it unlikely). RULE: ADOPT as a challenger (v6-stack; a new artefact, v5-leaf stays) if recall at precision 0.83 rises by 0.08 or more with bootstrap lower bound above 0 AND no extra encoder pass is needed (all inputs already exist on the serving path, extra cost under 1 ms); if the gain is under 0.03 the presence signal is exhausted in this feature family and the finding goes to the owner with the next options (second-stage reader L3, more Sonnet labels L4). The stacker is trained on development data only; the sealed 1,500 are not read.

L2 RESULT (stacked presence; l2_stack.py, runs/pulse/l2_stack.json; 5-fold x 3 seeds over DEVQ 1,997 + old 1,466 (old re-weighted to the natural stream), scored on DEVQ only; 221 real conditions). RECALL OF REAL CONDITIONS AT PRESENCE PRECISION 0.83: current gate 0.330; logistic stack 0.376 (gain +0.024, paired bootstrap 95 percent [-0.105, 0.172]); gradient-boosted stack 0.362 (-0.002 [-0.162, 0.155]). AUC on DEVQ: current 0.8955, logistic stack 0.9288, boosted 0.9378 (+0.033 to +0.042). PREDICTION (stacked 0.38 to 0.48) MISSED: logistic 0.376 sits just under the range. RULE (L461): gain under 0.03 => the presence signal is not exhausted in ranking terms but the recall at the operating point does not move: NO CHALLENGER. HONEST READ: AUC rises about 0.04 while recall at 83 percent precision rises 0.02 with an interval about +-0.14: with 221 positives the operating-point metric is too noisy to confirm a real but small gain; more natural positives (more labelled natural items) would resolve it, which is the same money that lever L4 spends. TOPIC CONTROL FINDING (round2_story_topic.py topic, Haiku-trained control, 36,070 labels, linear head on word+char counts + leaf vector for EVERY item; fit 1,849 s): DEVQ top-1 0.765 [0.746, 0.783], top-2 0.905 [0.892, 0.917] vs the engine's v5-leaf 0.747 / 0.896 (encoder only on routed items): +0.018 and +0.009 with overlapping intervals; this is lever L5 (encoder on every item) read early, serving cost not yet measured (the leaf encoder is 5 ms per item; the engine p95 is about 23 ms). CAP ACTIONS: trait student (59 min) and the topic test (45 min, its mixed-label fit alone would take about 30 min more) stopped by verified PID at the 1-hour rule; rerun lighter (fixed C=1, 8 parallel workers; topic Sonnet-trained rows only), registered as t20-traits-student-light and t20-r2-topic-sonnet-rows.

MORE REAL CONDITIONS FOR THE CHAIN ROWS PREDICT + RULE (owner question: why do the item counts on which / direction / size not grow). CAUSES: those rows count only items the engine already FOUND (44 of 221 real conditions in DEVQ; direction and size 38 after the right condition); every test re-scores the same 1,997 + 1,466 items; real conditions are 11 percent of the stream. SELECTION EFFECT: on the 44 found items which-condition is 0.864, but on all 221 real conditions with no gate it is 0.805 (top-2 0.910) and on the 896 untouched real conditions (221 + 675 old) about 0.78: the found slice flatters it. PLAN: (1) FREE: add rows measured on ALL real conditions ('given a real condition'), n 896 now; (2) DEVQ2 = Sonnet labels for 1,593 fresh natural queue items not in the pool, not in DEVQ, not in the sealed set (ids read only to exclude them), published 2026-10-29 to 2026-11-02, about 2.4 USD; (3) HF334 = Sonnet labels for the 334 Haiku-flagged items that were never trained on and are not yet Sonnet-labelled, about 0.5 USD, used ONLY for given-a-real-condition rates (Haiku flagging skips about 15 percent of real conditions, so it is never used for how many are found). Hosted, headline+teaser, inside L119; session spend so far about 20 USD of 70. PREDICT: DEVQ2 has 150 to 200 real conditions (11 percent), HF334 has 230 to 290 (70 to 85 percent), so real conditions in untouched development data go from 896 to about 1,300; which-condition top-1 given a real condition 0.76 to 0.80, direction given the right condition 0.88 to 0.92, size within one 0.88 to 0.92, all three together 0.62 to 0.68; the new batches agree with the DEVQ estimates within 0.03 (if not, the earlier estimates were noisy and are replaced). RULE: report the pooled given-a-real-condition rates with Wilson intervals on the page next to the found-only rows; the found-only rows stay but are marked as the easy slice. No model or threshold is chosen on the sealed set.

TRAITS STUDENT RESULT (train_traits.py light rerun, runs/pulse/traits_student.json; 51 linear heads on word+char counts + leaf vector, fixed C=1, trained on 1,500 Sonnet-graded pool items, scored on 1,150 Sonnet-graded DEVQ items; agreement with Sonnet). Overall: mean exact agreement 0.806 vs 0.753 for always answering 'not at all' (mean lift 0.053); 28 of 51 questions have exact agreement 0.80 or more, 19 have lift 0.05 or more, only 2 meet BOTH (the L454 bar): x030 (risk) 0.842, x049 (importance) 0.844. By group (exact / lift / AUC of 'active vs not at all'): movement 0.799 / 0.038 / 0.852; direction_effect 0.859 / 0.030 / 0.869; intent 0.785 / 0.051 / 0.882; risk 0.914 / 0.013 / 0.940; scale 0.700 / 0.149 / 0.891; time 0.748 / 0.066 / 0.834; certainty 0.753 / 0.056 / 0.864; importance 0.823 / 0.051 / 0.880. Active-vs-not AUC runs 0.78 to 0.975 across questions (best x025 deaths or injuries 0.975, x032 0.965, x031 environment threat 0.956). PREDICTIONS: mean exact 0.78 to 0.84 HELD; mean lift 0.03 to 0.08 HELD; READY 12 to 28 of 51 MISSED (2); strongest groups direction_effect and risk: risk strongest on exact and AUC HELD, direction_effect second on exact HELD; weakest certainty, importance, intent: certainty and intent weak HELD, importance partly (0.823). BY THE RULE: traits are NOT ready as graded answers (2 of 51). HONEST READ: most traits are rare (the typical question is active on 5 to 15 percent of items), so exact agreement is dominated by the 'not at all' majority and the lift bar is hard to clear; what the CPU does well is DETECT whether a trait is present (AUC mean about 0.87); it does not grade the degree (slightly / clearly / strongly) reliably, and even Sonnet and Haiku disagree on degree (0.36 exact). ROUTE (bar not moved): next pre-registered cut for traits = present / absent: per question precision at recall, and agreement of 'present' with Sonnet at precision 0.80; group verdicts on that cut; more graded labels for the weak groups only if the binary cut supports it. Cost so far for traits labels about 7.8 USD.

OVERNIGHT ACCELERATED-LEARNING PROGRAM (owner 2026-11-02, going to bed: loop a few times, use the local CPU and GPU, find out what works across all Pulse fields; the one-lever-per-round method is slow). OWNER AUTHORISATION recorded: local GPU (RTX 5090, about 14 GB free beside voice, Clef and the world service; never stop or disturb those) for experiments in this program only. GUARDRAILS: every job registered on the page with pid, why, success, next; no job over 1 hour (chunk longer work, arm a PID-verified stop); hosted spend inside the 70 USD pre-authorisation (about 24 used; this program adds at most 20, so at most 44 total; reported at each 10 USD mark); no engine file replaced (challengers only, owner's yes needed); sealed 1,500 never scored; no third-party code (trust_remote_code stays off); no legacy models. THE IDEA: stop testing one lever per round; build ONE results matrix, encoder x field x training target, from cached features, so the next decisions come from a table. PHASE A, CEILING PROBE (GPU, about 1 hour): embed all development and training items with 9 frozen encoders (leaf, bge-small, bge-base, bge-large, gte-small, snowflake-arctic-embed-s, gte-modernbert-base, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, Qwen3-Embedding-4B; 128 tokens, same texts), then train the same dense linear head for every encoder on story type, topic (49), condition presence, which-condition, on Haiku labels and on Sonnet labels, and score on DEVQ and the old test set. QUESTION: is the limit the size of the reader or the labels and definition? PREDICT: bigger frozen encoders add 0.01 to 0.03 on story and topic top-1 and 0.03 to 0.08 on presence recall at 83 percent precision; Qwen3-4B is best on presence but no more than 0.10 above leaf; the order by size is mostly monotone; Sonnet-trained heads beat Haiku-trained heads at equal encoder on story and presence. RULE: if some encoder beats leaf by 0.05 or more on a field with a non-overlapping interval, that field's path is DISTILLATION (fine-tune the CPU-size encoder to mimic the big one, Phase C); if no encoder beats leaf by 0.03 on presence, the limit is labels and definition, not reader size, and the path is more Sonnet labels plus a sharper condition definition. PHASE B, LABELS (hosted batch, no GPU): Sonnet labels 10,000 more random training-period items (about 15 USD) so Sonnet-labelled training data goes from 6,000 to 16,000; the measured slope (about +0.008 per doubling on story) says this is the best-priced lever. PHASE C, FINE-TUNE (GPU, about 1 hour): fine-tune leaf (22M) and bge-small (33M) with multi-task heads (story, topic, presence, which) on the Haiku + Sonnet labels, export to ONNX, and measure CPU speed; adopt as a challenger only if a field gains its bar with CPU p95 under 50 ms. MORNING DELIVERABLE: one table (encoder x field x target), the learning curve to 16,000 Sonnet labels, the fine-tune verdict, and a recommended build.

ROUND 2, TOPIC RESULT (round2_story_topic.py topic, runs/pulse/round2_topic.json; DEVQ 1,997; linear head on word+char counts + leaf vector). Haiku-trained 36,070 labels [control]: top-1 0.765 [0.746, 0.783], top-2 0.905 [0.892, 0.917]. Sonnet-trained 6,000 labels: top-1 0.705 [0.685, 0.725], top-2 0.860 [0.844, 0.875]: WORSE by 0.06 and 0.045. RULE (L455): no challenger; the Sonnet target does NOT help topic at 6,000 labels. PREDICTION (Sonnet-trained top-1 0.72 to 0.80) MISSED. READ: story type (4 classes) gains from Sonnet labels at 6,000, topic (49 classes) does not: with 49 classes 6,000 labels leave about 120 per class, and the larger Haiku set wins on coverage. The mixed row (Haiku bulk + Sonnet) was skipped for the 1-hour cap and moves into the overnight GPU matrix (target 'mixed'). The topic learning curve rows (1,500 / 3,000) were not reached; the matrix reruns topic at 6,000 and at 16,000 Sonnet labels once the tranche lands.

OVERNIGHT PHASE A RESULT: ENCODER CEILING MATRIX (ceiling_embed.py, ceiling_heads.py, runs/pulse/ceiling_heads_t6k.json; 9 frozen encoders, same dense linear head, no word counts, 128 tokens, trained on Haiku (36,070), Sonnet (6,000) or mixed (Haiku + Sonnet x5); scored on DEVQ 1,997 natural; which-condition on 896 real conditions; paired bootstrap vs leaf, MIXED target). STORY TYPE top-1: every encoder lands 0.885 to 0.900; best qwen3-4b 0.900, diff vs leaf +0.011 [-0.002, 0.021]: NOT encoder-limited. TOPIC top-1: leaf 0.750; qwen3-4b 0.790 (+0.040 [0.028, 0.054]), qwen3-0.6b 0.774 (+0.024 [0.009, 0.039]), bge-large 0.762 (+0.012 [-0.003, 0.026]), others at or below leaf; top-2 leaf 0.906, qwen3-4b 0.922. PRESENCE recall of real conditions at precision 0.83: leaf 0.240; qwen3-4b 0.394 (+0.154 [0.022, 0.315]); arctic-s 0.290 (+0.050, interval spans zero); the other encoders equal or below leaf; AUC is flat (0.897 to 0.916) for all. WHICH-CONDITION top-1: leaf 0.804; qwen3-4b 0.837 (+0.033 [0.013, 0.051]); the rest within 0.02. SIZE BOTH WAYS: only the 4B model separates from leaf; encoders from 33M to 335M (bge, gte, arctic) do not beat leaf on any field. TARGETS: Sonnet-only heads are better than Haiku-only on story (+0.01), worse on topic (-0.04 to -0.05) and on presence; MIXED is best or tied almost everywhere. PREDICTIONS: bigger encoders add 0.01 to 0.03 on story and topic top-1: story HELD (+0.011), topic MISSED high (+0.040 only for the 4B); presence +0.03 to 0.08, qwen3-4b best but no more than +0.10 above leaf: MISSED (+0.154, interval wide); order mostly monotone by size: MISSED (bge-large and gte-modernbert do not beat leaf; only qwen3 does); Sonnet beats Haiku at equal encoder on story HELD, on presence MISSED. RULE (overnight program): some encoder beats leaf by 0.05+ with a non-overlapping interval on presence (qwen3-4b) => the path for presence, and for topic and which-condition (gains +0.033 to +0.040), is DISTILLATION of the 4B reader into the CPU-size encoder (Phase C); story type is a LABELS problem (Sonnet labels +0.01, ceiling about 0.90). CAVEAT: dense-only heads (leaf 0.24 at 83 percent precision) are below the engine's sparse+dense gate (0.33): word counts matter, so the real test of any new encoder is inside the full feature set; a 4B reader cannot run on the CPU at serving (about 2 s per item).

OVERNIGHT PHASE C PREDICT + RULE: DISTILL THE 4B READER INTO THE CPU-SIZE ENCODER (finetune_distill.py, GPU, about 20 minutes per variant). STUDENT = leaf (22.6M), fine-tuned end to end with 4 linear heads on its own embedding (story 4, topic 49, presence 2, which-condition 38 on real-condition rows), 64 tokens (the length the engine uses), bf16, 3 epochs, batch 64, encoder lr 2e-5, heads 1e-3. LABELS = Sonnet's where we hold it (weight 3), else Haiku's. VARIANT A: hard labels only. VARIANT B: hard labels + soft targets (temperature 2, weight 1) from linear heads on Qwen3-Embedding-4B embeddings trained on the same labels, cross-fitted 5-fold so no soft target comes from a head that saw that item. SCORE exactly like the matrix on DEVQ (story top-1, topic top-1 and top-2, presence recall at 83 percent precision and AUC, which top-1 on 896 real conditions) vs the frozen-leaf dense baseline of the same pipeline (story 0.890, topic 0.750, presence 0.240, which 0.804) and vs the 4B teacher (0.900, 0.790, 0.394, 0.837). PREDICT: A story 0.89 to 0.91, topic 0.755 to 0.785, presence 0.24 to 0.34, which 0.80 to 0.83; B topic 0.770 to 0.800, presence 0.30 to 0.42, which 0.81 to 0.84; B recovers about half of the teacher's lead over frozen leaf. RULE: a student is a CANDIDATE if on any field it beats the frozen-leaf dense baseline by its bar (story +0.015, topic top-1 +0.02, presence recall +0.08, which +0.02) with a paired-bootstrap lower bound above 0; candidates then get (a) ONNX export and a CPU speed check (p95 of the whole engine under 50 ms on one thread) and (b) the real test inside the full feature set (word counts + student vectors, heads retrained) before any challenger version is built; no challenger replaces v5-leaf without the owner. If neither variant beats frozen leaf on any field, fine-tuning is closed for this reader size and the finding goes to the owner.

text: T20 engine card: BitMob Expert 1 v5-leaf

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready = agreement 80% or more on 30+ items, answering half the stream or more. Partial = reaches 80% only on part of the stream, or only on cases it already found. Not yet = under 80%. Later phase = not built.

layers.name: Macro / Pulse
layers.asks: What is changing, and where? One expert reads each item once and answers all of these.

fields.label: Story type
fields.what: Fact, forecast, opinion or unclear

fields.label: Topic
fields.what: One of 49 topics, two guesses

fields.label: Condition present
fields.what: Does the story report a change in one of 38 world conditions

fields.label: Which condition
fields.what: Names it, among the items where it found one

fields.label: Direction
fields.what: Up or down

fields.label: Size
fields.what: How big, within one step of Sonnet's level

fields.label: Which condition, all real cases
fields.what: Its top pick for every real condition, no confidence gate (the honest version of the row above)

fields.label: Direction, all real cases
fields.what: Up or down, once it named the right condition, over all real conditions

fields.label: Size, all real cases
fields.what: Within one step, once it named the right condition, over all real conditions

fields.label: Traits (51 questions, 8 groups)
fields.what: Movement, direction and effect, intent, risk, scale, certainty, time, importance

layers.name: Area (drill into one thing)
layers.asks: Pick something from the Pulse, such as a capability, and see what drives it, depends on it and is affected by it. Pilot done (L384): tags can be proposed on the CPU and verified by Clef, but agreement is only moderate, so the design is a hybrid.

fields.label: Things and capabilities
fields.what: Find entities, places, concepts and capabilities in the item and link each to one stable identity. Pilot: about 5 tags per full article, 3 per headline item; reading the whole article adds 56% new tags.

fields.label: Events and relations
fields.what: What happened, who took part, and how things connect. Related tags (Gaza / Gaza Strip / Palestinians) merge by similarity; identity needs entity linking.

layers.name: Understanding (downstream, does not block)
layers.asks: One consolidated explanation per capability, whoever said it, traced back to its sources. Where do new items agree, disagree or leave gaps?

fields.label: Consolidated knowledge
fields.what: How a capability works and best practice across the field, merged from many sources

fields.label: Agree, contradict, gap
fields.what: Check each new item against what we know and flag what is new or missing

fields.label: Claim, evidence, source
fields.what: Every statement traced to the source text it came from; the raw documents stay but are not the focus

next.headline: Biggest gap: finding real conditions, and the chain after it
next.body: Measured on 1,997 natural, never-seen queue items (agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy): story type 0.875 and topic (two guesses) 0.896 on every item; one topic guess 0.747. Only 11% of the stream has a condition. The engine says 'no condition' correctly on almost all of the rest (0.966 when it answers, answering 80%). Of the real conditions it finds 20% at today's cut and 33% at 83% right. Given a real condition the later fields pass: which condition 0.87 on 84% of them, direction 0.90, size 0.90, but the three together are right about 65% of the time. Earlier figures (reach 10%, story 0.911) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced. Tried and no gain so far: lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training on Sonnet instead of Haiku conditions.
next.ask: Decide: (1) which capability sources to take in; (2) condition tiers: read them from the reach-versus-right curve (T20, L447); (3) do tags run on the CPU at serving time or stay an offline Clef step.

tried_groups.summary: CPU proposes, Clef verifies: about 3 tags per headline item, 5.4 per full article; wording agreement about 0.5; 77% of tags occur once. Frozen leaf dense: story 0.890, topic 0.750, presence recall@0.83 0.240, which 0.804. Teacher qwen3-4b: 0.900, 0.790, 0.394, 0.837. A (hard labels, 3 epochs, lr 2e-5): 0.881, 0.761, 0.312, 0.797. B (distilled, 3 ep, 2e-5): 0.895, 0.766, 0.339, 0.802. B 6 epochs 2e-5: 0.905, 0.769, 0.357, 0.819. B 3 epochs 5e-5: 0.898, 0.768, 0.357, 0.820. B 6 epochs 5e-5: story 0.905, topic top-1 0.776 (top-2 0.911), presence 0.376 (AUC 0.927), which 0.831. Each run takes 40 to 90 seconds on the 5090. READ: more training and a higher learning rate help every field and have not flattened; the 22M student at 6 epochs closes about 80 percent of the gap to the 4B teacher on story and which-condition and about 60 percent on presence and topic. PRE-REGISTERED BARS (L468): story +0.015 over frozen leaf: 0.905 vs 0.890 = +0.015 (at the bar, interval pending); topic +0.02: 0.776 vs 0.750 = +0.026 (meets by point estimate); presence recall +0.08: 0.376 vs 0.240 = +0.136 (meets by point estimate, interval wide); which +0.02: 0.831 vs 0.804 = +0.027 (meets by point estimate). NOT YET A CANDIDATE: lower bounds are checked by paired bootstrap on the final setting, then the full-feature test and CPU speed. NEXT: sweep 2 (12 and 16 epochs, lr 1e-4, distillation weight 3) running; then paired bootstrap on the best setting, ONNX export, CPU p95, and the full-feature test; then rerun with the 16,000-label tranche.

METHOD FLAW FOUND AND FIXED (overnight): the fine-tuned student has a trainable 384-to-1024 projection (the encoder's Dense layer) after the transformer, and my checkpoints saved only the transformer weights. The sweep scores in finetune_distill.py were computed on the live model and are VALID; but ft_eval_stack.py (presence stack with the sparse gate: 0.434 and 0.430 vs the current 0.330) and any export would have used the ORIGINAL projection with the fine-tuned transformer, so those two stack numbers are approximate (they were within 0.02 of the in-training score, so the projection moved little). Fix: checkpoints now save the full model state (st_full); the best setting is rerun and the stack and the ONNX export are redone from the full model. Also noted: no environment has onnxscript, and the legacy ONNX exporter needs the onnx package, which only the voice and verdict environments have; the export goes through a TorchScript hand-off (trace in the embed environment, ONNX conversion in the verdict environment, same torch 2.11), without installing anything. A probe command of mine (pip download) started a network download of the onnx wheel by accident; it was cut off after one line and nothing was saved.

CHALLENGER BUILD v6-student PREDICT + RULE (overnight Phase C; builds on L468 bars, L472 sweep, L473 fix). ARTEFACT: expert1_v6_student.pkl = the v5-leaf pickle (sparse vectorisers, direction and size models) + the fine-tuned student (leaf 22.6M, B setting: 16 epochs, lr 5e-5, distilled from Qwen3-4B, trained on Sonnet-else-Haiku labels, tranche NOT included) exported to ONNX (cosine 1.0000 vs torch, 13.2 ms vs leaf 12.8 ms p50 on one thread, 92 MB) with its 4 linear heads. CONTRACT (same as v5): story type and topic (two guesses) from the student heads, always answered like v5's cuts; CONDITION PRESENT = a 2-feature logistic stack [engine sparse blend logit, student presence logit] fitted on DEVQ + old (old re-weighted to the natural stream); the yes cut is the lowest probability whose precision is 0.83 (the operating point used all day) and the no side keeps v5's cut; WHICH CONDITION from the student 38-way head with a cut set on half of the real conditions at 80 percent agreement, as v5 did; direction and size unchanged. CLEAN HOLDOUT: DEVQ2 (1,593 natural items, 166 real conditions) was not used to fit the stack or the cuts, so it is the unbiased check; DEVQ and old are scored too but the stack coefficients saw them. COMPARATOR: v5-leaf on the same items. PREDICT on DEVQ2: story 0.89 to 0.91 (v5 about 0.875), topic top-1 0.77 to 0.80 (v5 about 0.747), top-2 0.91 to 0.92 (v5 0.896); presence: real conditions found at the 0.83 cut 0.38 to 0.48 vs v5 0.20 at its cut; which given a real condition (no gate) 0.82 to 0.85 (v5 0.79); the whole engine p95 under 50 ms on one thread, within 5 ms of v5-leaf (about 22 ms). RULE: the challenger is REPORTABLE on the page next to v5-leaf if story, topic and which each gain at least their bar (+0.015, +0.02, +0.02) on DEVQ2 and the whole-engine p95 stays under 50 ms; presence gain is reported with its interval whatever it is; it is NOT adopted and does not replace v5-leaf: that is the owner's decision. Sealed 1,500 untouched.

CHALLENGER v6-student RESULT (runtime ExpertS, artefact runs/expert1/expert1_v6_student.pkl, ONNX student 92 MB; paired_engine.py, score_end2end.py, footprint.py; NOT ADOPTED, v5-leaf stays; agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy). CLEAN HOLDOUT DEVQ2 (1,593 natural never-seen items, 166 real conditions; not used to fit the stack or the cuts), paired bootstrap 400: story type 0.888 to 0.902 (+0.014 [-0.001, 0.031]); topic top-1 0.786 to 0.815 (+0.029 [0.012, 0.045]); topic top-2 0.914 to 0.922 (+0.008 [-0.005, 0.020]); REAL CONDITIONS FOUND 0.175 to 0.301 (+0.127 [0.066, 0.181]); condition, direction and size all right, of real conditions, 0.151 to 0.241 (+0.090 [0.036, 0.133]); share of items answered on presence 0.797 to 0.895 (agreement when answered 0.969 to 0.965); WHICH CONDITION given a real condition, no gate, pooled 1,176: 0.792 to 0.834 (+0.043 [0.021, 0.063]). On DEVQ (stack fitted there): story 0.875 to 0.905, topic top-1 0.747 to 0.789, found 0.199 to 0.249. SPEED AND MEMORY (footprint.py, 400 items, one thread, 3 interleaved rounds): v6-student p50 14.9 to 15.1 ms, p95 16.4 to 16.7 ms, worst single read 18 to 27 ms, 587 to 596 MB; v5-leaf p50 4.5 to 5.0 ms, p95 23.3 to 24.9 ms in two rounds (1,439 ms in the third) and a single read of 2.5 to 3.2 s in every round (the known stall); both far inside the 50 ms budget. v6's tail is tighter because every item takes the same single encoder pass. PREDICTIONS (L474): story 0.89 to 0.91 HELD (0.902); topic top-1 0.77 to 0.80 MISSED high (0.815); topic top-2 0.91 to 0.92 HELD (0.922); real conditions found at the cut 0.38 to 0.48 MISSED (0.301, higher than v5 but under the range: the cut sits at presence probability 0.741, v5's level, not at a recall-seeking point); which given a real condition 0.82 to 0.85 HELD (0.834); p95 under 50 ms and within 5 ms of v5: p95 HELD under 50, 'within 5 ms of v5' not needed (v6 is lower at p95). RULE (L474): reportable if story, topic and which each gain their bar (+0.015, +0.02, +0.02) on DEVQ2: topic +0.029 YES, which +0.043 YES (pooled), story +0.014 NO by 0.001 and its interval touches zero. So by the written rule it is reported WITH that exception named: gains proven on topic one guess, finding real conditions, all-three-right and which condition; the story gain is not proven. The 4B teacher is not needed at serving: the student was distilled from it on the GPU and runs on one CPU thread. NEXT: rerun with the 16,000-label tranche; sweep a second epoch/lr region; adoption stays the owner's decision.
T20 engine card: BitMob Expert 1 v5-leaf

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready = agreement 80% or more on 30+ items, answering half the stream or more. Partial = reaches 80% only on part of the stream, or only on cases it already found. Not yet = under 80%. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Biggest gap: finding real conditions, and the chain after it
next.body: Measured on 1,997 natural, never-seen queue items (agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy): story type 0.875 and topic (two guesses) 0.896 on every item; one topic guess 0.747. Only 11% of the stream has a condition. The engine says 'no condition' correctly on almost all of the rest (0.966 when it answers, answering 80%). Of the real conditions it finds 20% at today's cut and 33% at 83% right. Given a real condition the later fields pass: which condition 0.87 on 84% of them, direction 0.90, size 0.90, but the three together are right about 65% of the time. Earlier figures (reach 10%, story 0.911) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced. Tried and no gain so far: lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training on Sonnet instead of Haiku conditions.
next.ask: Decide: (1) which capability sources to take in; (2) condition tiers: read them from the reach-versus-right curve (T20, L447); (3) do tags run on the CPU at serving time or stay an offline Clef step.

tried_groups.name: What worked
tried_groups.summary: Word counts and static vectors for everything, a frozen small encoder on routed items (now mdbr-leaf-mt, 22.6M), and regularisation tuned on a validation slice (topic +0.02, topic overfitting gap 0.103 to 0.042).

items.what: Word counts + logistic regression alone
items.result: Story type at teacher level (0.90), topic weak (0.54)
items.outcome: Kept for story type and as the always-on path

items.what: Static word vectors (potion-8M) + logistic regression
items.result: Topic 0.62; confidence is trustworthy (calibration error 0.04)
items.outcome: Kept (the base of every version)

items.what: Frozen bge-small encoder features added
items.result: Which-condition top-1 0.704 to 0.770, top-2 0.828 to 0.905
items.outcome: Adopted, routed items only (v3)

items.what: Tuning regularisation (C) of the topic heads on a validation slice
items.result: Topic top-2 0.857 to 0.877; topic gap 0.103 to 0.059; story unchanged (best C stays 3)
items.outcome: Adopted as v3.2

items.what: Swapping the encoder bge-small for MongoDB/mdbr-leaf-mt, picked from a scan of all 215 scored models
items.result: Pulse fields tie; 95% of reads under 22.6 ms vs 36.6; 643 MB vs 724; neighbour topic agreement 0.683 vs 0.648; chunked late-passage recall 0.859 vs 0.867
items.outcome: Adopted as the trunk (all three adoption rules held)

tried_groups.name: Swapping the trunk (Granite small R2)
tried_groups.summary: Ties with bge-small on every Pulse field (short items). On whole articles a bigger window beats truncating at 512, but chunking bge-small beats one long Granite pass and costs far less CPU. Plan for long articles: bge-small chunks feeding tag-level joins.

items.what: ibm-granite/granite-embedding-small-english-r2 as the shared encoder (47.7M, Apache-2.0, 8k, ModernBERT), same heads and items
items.result: Topic top-2 0.881 vs 0.877, which-condition 0.875 vs 0.863, all inside the noise; encoder alone 23 ms; engine p95 44.5 ms vs 36.2; memory 837 MB vs 732
items.outcome: bge-small stays; revisit when Area needs token-level heads

items.what: Long-term features: joining quality and long-input cost, Granite vs bge-small
items.result: Neighbour topic agreement 0.634 vs 0.648; cluster agreement (NMI) 0.383 vs 0.408; 8,192 tokens 22 s vs about 3.9 s chunked
items.outcome: Granite not ahead; one test left (token-level tagging head, needs the Area tag labels)

items.what: Whole-article test: can a passage from the late part find its article? (1,500 long articles, median 1,078 tokens)
items.result: bge truncated 0.50; Granite whole article 0.64; bge chunked mean 0.77; bge best chunk 0.87 (recall@1, late passages)
items.outcome: Owner's logic holds (bigger window beats truncation); chunking a small model wins

tried_groups.name: Bigger or tuned neural models
tried_groups.summary: Fine-tuning, int8 and distilling the encoder were not better, or not fast enough.

items.what: Fine-tuning the encoder
items.result: First try much worse (topic top-2 0.726); corrected try +0.014 on topic but worse on which-condition
items.outcome: Rejected: frozen features beat it

items.what: int8 encoder to make it fast enough
items.result: Topic top-2 drops 0.019 against a 0.01 limit
items.outcome: Rejected; cascade instead

items.what: Distilling the encoder into static vectors
items.result: Keeps none of the encoder's lift (topic top-2 0.813 vs 0.832)
items.outcome: Rejected

tried_groups.name: Outside language models (d1, LFM3)
tried_groups.summary: d1 is a strong second opinion (topic 0.926 when combined) but needs the GPU and its licence does not fit. LFM3 is unusable.

items.what: d1-2B decision model, zero-shot, on the GPU
items.result: Alone: topic top-2 0.852. Fused with our student: topic top-2 0.926, condition top-1 0.834
items.outcome: Pipeline test only: GPU, and a licence the owner called not commercially viable

items.what: LFM3-1.7B as a JSON reader
items.result: Only 28% valid JSON; as a yes/no scorer AUC 0.54 to 0.61
items.outcome: Rejected

tried_groups.name: Teaching tricks
tried_groups.summary: Training our student on d1's soft labels gave no gain.

items.what: Training the student on d1's soft labels
items.result: Topic top-2 -0.008, story -0.006, which-condition +0.009 to +0.02
items.outcome: No gain; d1 stays a live second opinion

tried_groups.name: Free-form tags (pilot: 100 articles, 100 headline items)
tried_groups.summary: CPU proposes, Clef verifies: about 3 tags per headline item, 5.4 per full article; wording agreement about 0.5; 77% of tags occur once. Capabilities are 7% of general-news tags and 23% of tech-news tags, and almost never recur across articles: news can propose capability candidates but cannot supply the capability layer. Design: a hybrid.

items.what: Tag pilot with spaCy proposer and local Clef verifier (5 narrow yes/no questions per candidate)
items.result: 41% of 2,762 candidates accepted; kappa 0.49 to 0.53; merge at cosine 0.80 cuts distinct tags by 33% but merges related, not only identical, tags; 56% of full-article tags are absent from the short version
items.outcome: Hybrid design; capability layer needs tech sources; a token-level tag head is the serving route (the proposer takes 0.7 s per item)

changes.title: Challenger v6-student: waiting for your yes (v5-leaf unchanged)
changes.text: A 22M student fine-tuned from the leaf encoder, taught by a 4B reader (on the GPU only), one CPU pass per item. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: real conditions found 17.5% to 30.1% (+12.7 points, interval 6.6 to 18.1), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 24.1%, topic one guess 78.6% to 81.5% (+2.9), which condition 79.2% to 83.4% (+4.3, 1,176 cases). Story type +1.4 points is NOT proven (interval touches zero). Speed 15 ms typical, 16.5 ms at 95%, 590 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy.

changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory

changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.title: Real conditions: counts
changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

text: TRANCHE DONE: Sonnet labelled 9,994 more training-period items (4 chunks, no errors); Sonnet-labelled training data is now about 16,000. Hosted spend this session: traits 7.8, DEVQ 3.0, DEVQ2+HF334 about 3.0, self-consistency 0.6, small tests 1.5, tranche about 14 = about 30 USD of the 70 USD pre-authorisation (10, 20 and 30 USD marks passed; reported). Rerunning the ceiling matrix (--tranche) and the student (--tranche, 16 and 24 epochs, tags _t16e16lr5 and _t16e24lr5) now.

16,000-LABEL RESULTS (ceiling_heads.py --tranche, finetune_distill.py --tranche; labels = Sonnet's where held (about 16,000) else Haiku's; DEVQ 1,997). FROZEN HEADS, Sonnet-only target, leaf: story 0.905 (was 0.890 at 6,000), topic 0.760 (was 0.706), presence 0.258, which 0.779; qwen3-4b Sonnet-only: story 0.915, topic 0.801, presence 0.448, which 0.823. At 16,000 labels the Sonnet target now beats the Haiku target on story (+0.025), topic (+0.008) and presence (+0.027); at 6,000 it lost on topic and presence: the label slope pays. STUDENT (leaf, distilled, 16 epochs, lr 5e-5): story 0.919 (6k: 0.907), topic 0.790 (0.788), presence 0.407 (0.412), which 0.824 (0.831); 24 epochs: 0.913, 0.786, 0.412, 0.824. Gains from the extra labels sit in story type (+0.012); topic, presence and which are within noise because the student already equals its 4B teacher on them (teacher at 16k: topic 0.800, presence 0.443, which 0.831). READ: story type is a labels problem (it kept rising: 0.881 Haiku-only, 0.907 at 6k, 0.919 at 16k); topic, presence and which are now limited by the teacher's reader size and by how many real conditions we have, so the next lever there is a stronger teacher or an ensemble of readers, not more of the same labels. Next: export the 16k student, build it as challenger v6b-student, and compare it with v5-leaf and v6-student on the DEVQ2 holdout.

CHALLENGER v6b-student RESULT (student fine-tuned on about 16,000 Sonnet labels + Haiku, distilled from Qwen3-4B, 16 epochs lr 5e-5; artefact runs/expert1/expert1_v6b_student.pkl; presence stack coefficients [0.150 sparse, 0.816 student, -0.247], yes cut 0.752; fitted on DEVQ + old only; NOT ADOPTED). CLEAN HOLDOUT DEVQ2 (1,593 natural never-seen items, 166 real conditions), paired bootstrap 400 vs v5-leaf: STORY TYPE 0.888 to 0.918 (+0.030 [0.015, 0.045]); TOPIC top-1 0.786 to 0.819 (+0.033 [0.016, 0.050]); top-2 0.914 to 0.925 (+0.011 [-0.003, 0.023]); REAL CONDITIONS FOUND 0.175 to 0.325 (+0.151 [0.090, 0.211]); condition + direction + size all right of real conditions 0.151 to 0.259 (+0.108 [0.054, 0.151]); presence answered share 0.797 to 0.897; WHICH CONDITION given a real condition pooled 1,176: 0.792 to 0.827 (+0.036 [0.014, 0.058]). vs the 6k-label challenger v6-student on DEVQ2: story 0.901 to 0.918, topic 0.815 to 0.819, found 0.301 to 0.325, all-right 0.241 to 0.259. RULE (L474): story +0.030 (bar 0.015, lower bound above 0), topic +0.033 (bar 0.02), which +0.036 (bar 0.02) all met: REPORTABLE as a challenger with no exception; adoption is the owner's decision (v5-leaf unchanged). Speed and memory in the next line. LESSON: the label slope measured at 6,000 (story +0.008 per doubling) held at 16,000 (0.907 to 0.919), so story type was a labels problem; topic, presence and which were reader-limited and the distilled student already reaches its 4B teacher on them.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

text: ROUND (overnight) PREDICT + RULE: STRONGER TEACHER BY ENSEMBLE. The student already equals its 4B teacher on topic, presence and which-condition (L478), so further gains there need a stronger teacher. TEST (GPU, minutes): concatenate the L2-normalised embeddings of five frozen readers already computed (qwen3-4b, qwen3-0.6b, bge-large, gte-modernbert, leaf) into one 'ens' reader and train the same dense head as the matrix (16,000-label target, mixed), scored on DEVQ vs qwen3-4b alone (story 0.909, topic 0.800, presence 0.443, which 0.831 mixed). PREDICT: ens beats qwen3-4b by 0.005 to 0.02 on topic and which and by 0.02 to 0.08 on presence recall at 83 percent precision. RULE: if ens beats qwen3-4b by 0.02 or more on topic top-1, or 0.05 on presence, with a paired-bootstrap lower bound above 0, distil the ensemble into the leaf student (finetune_distill.py with the ensemble as teacher) and rebuild the challenger as v6c-student; if not, the teacher is saturated at this reader family and the remaining lever is labels (more real conditions) and the definition of a condition.

ENSEMBLE TEACHER RESULT (ceiling_heads.py ENCS=leaf,qwen3-4b,ens --tranche, mixed target, DEVQ): ens (five readers concatenated, 6,400 dims): story 0.917, topic 0.791, presence 0.403, which 0.828; qwen3-4b alone: 0.909, 0.800, 0.443, 0.831; leaf: 0.900, 0.760, 0.249, 0.809. NO GAIN over the 4B reader on topic (-0.009), presence (-0.040), which (-0.003); story +0.008. PREDICTION (ens +0.005 to +0.02 on topic and which, +0.02 to +0.08 on presence) MISSED. RULE (L481): the teacher is saturated at this reader family (frozen embeddings + linear head); no ensemble distillation. NEXT TWO LEVERS for the weakest field (finding real conditions, 32.5 percent): (1) FINE-TUNED TEACHER: fine-tune Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B end to end on the 16,000 Sonnet labels (supervised, GPU) and test whether it beats the frozen 4B reader (topic 0.800, presence 0.443, which 0.831); if yes, distil it. PREDICT: topic 0.80 to 0.83, presence 0.45 to 0.55, which 0.83 to 0.86; RULE: beats frozen 4B by 0.02 topic or 0.05 presence with lower bound above 0 => distil into leaf (v6c). (2) ACTIVE LABELLING: the 16,000 Sonnet labels are random items, only 11 to 15 percent contain a condition; spend a second tranche (10,000 items, about 14 USD, total this session then about 44 of 70) on the items the current student is most unsure about or most suspects are real conditions (6,000 highest presence score + 4,000 from the 0.15 to 0.85 band among unlabelled training-period items); PREDICT: Sonnet-labelled real conditions in training go from about 1,700 to about 5,000; presence recall at 83 percent precision of the retrained student +0.03 to +0.08 over v6b, which-condition +0.01 to +0.03; RULE: adopt into a v6c challenger only with a paired-bootstrap lower bound above 0 on DEVQ2.

ACTIVE LABELLING CANCELLED BEFORE ANY SPEND (select_active.py): the 19,708 unlabelled training-period items are the Haiku-negative, gate-unflagged remainder (same selection effect as the first DEV2 set, L439): on those the v6b student's presence probability tops out at 0.045 for the 6,000th item and the 0.15 to 0.85 band is EMPTY, so a second tranche from the pool would buy almost no real conditions. NO HOSTED SPEND; label_tranche2.py and runs/pulse/tranche2 item files exist but are not run. FINDING: the pool's supply of real conditions is exhausted (every Haiku-positive and gate-flagged item was already Sonnet-labelled); real conditions in Sonnet-labelled training data stay at about 3,600. The only new supply is the live queue: about 1,300 new items a day, about 11 percent contain a condition (about 145 a day), at about 2 USD a day to label; a standing daily labelling of new queue items (kept apart from the sealed 1,500 and from the dev sets) is the sustainable way to grow real-condition data: a week adds about 1,000. This is a proposal for the owner (recurring hosted spend), not started.

FINE-TUNED TEACHER TEST (lever 1 of L482; GPU, about 10 minutes): fine-tune Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (0.6B, fp32 weights, bf16 autocast, 64 tokens, batch 32, 3 epochs, lr 2e-5, the 4 multi-task heads, hard labels only = variant A, 16,000-label set) and score it exactly like the matrix on DEVQ vs the FROZEN 4B reader (16k mixed: story 0.909, topic 0.800, presence 0.443, which 0.831) and the v6b student (story 0.919, topic 0.790, presence 0.407, which 0.824). PREDICT: topic 0.80 to 0.83, presence 0.45 to 0.55, which 0.83 to 0.86, story 0.92 to 0.93. RULE: if it beats the frozen 4B by 0.02 on topic or 0.05 on presence with a paired lower bound above 0 (checked after, from saved per-item results), a distillation into leaf is worth building (v6c) with cross-fitted soft targets from a 5-fold fine-tune; otherwise the supervised ceiling for this reader size is already reached by the 4B frozen teacher and the student. GPU memory is the risk (about 11 GB of the 14 GB free): if it runs out, batch 16 once; no other service is touched.

FINE-TUNED TEACHER RESULT, 3 EPOCHS (finetune_distill.py A, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, 16k labels, hard labels, DEVQ): story 0.910, topic top-1 0.767 (top-2 0.873), presence recall@0.83 0.285 (AUC 0.908), which 0.729. vs frozen 4B reader: 0.909, 0.800, 0.443, 0.831; vs v6b student 0.919, 0.790, 0.407, 0.824. WORSE than the frozen 4B on topic (-0.033), presence (-0.158) and which (-0.102); training loss still falling (12.97, 6.80, 5.33). PREDICTION (topic 0.80 to 0.83, presence 0.45 to 0.55, which 0.83 to 0.86) MISSED. RULE: not better than the frozen 4B => no distillation from this checkpoint. One longer run (8 epochs, lr 3e-5, about 18 minutes) is started because the student's own curve kept rising to 16 epochs; same rule applies, and nothing hosted is spent.

CONDITION TIERS READ FROM THE CURVE (tiers_curve.py, runs/pulse/tiers_curve.json; clean holdout DEVQ2, 1,593 natural items, 166 real conditions; presence-level precision = share of 'yes' calls that are real conditions per Sonnet; found share = real conditions found; bootstrap 400). v5-leaf: precision 0.95 finds 0.133 [0.051, 0.264] (14 yes calls per 1,000 items); 0.90 finds 0.223 [0.066, 0.333]; 0.83 finds 0.283 [0.162, 0.384]; 0.75 finds 0.331 [0.231, 0.480]; 0.60 finds 0.584 [0.345, 0.685] (101 yes calls per 1,000). v6b-student: 0.95 finds 0.313 [0.160, 0.414] (34 per 1,000); 0.90 finds 0.361 [0.264, 0.455]; 0.83 finds 0.392 [0.308, 0.600]; 0.75 finds 0.554 [0.364, 0.672]; 0.60 finds 0.711 [0.582, 0.802] (123 per 1,000). v6b is ahead at every precision level by 11 to 22 points (intervals overlap at single levels because there are only 166 real conditions). READ: the owner's two-tier question (L-earlier: 81 percent right finds 10 percent; 56 percent right finds 33 percent) is superseded by a curve; for v6b a CONFIDENT tier at about 90 percent right finds about 36 percent of real conditions (41 calls per 1,000 items) and a POSSIBLE tier at about 60 percent right finds about 71 percent (123 calls per 1,000). The tier choice is still the owner's (it changes the output contract).

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready = agreement 80% or more on 30+ items, answering half the stream or more. Partial = reaches 80% only on part of the stream, or only on cases it already found. Not yet = under 80%. Later phase = not built.

layers.name: Macro / Pulse
layers.asks: What is changing, and where? One expert reads each item once and answers all of these.

fields.label: Story type
fields.what: Fact, forecast, opinion or unclear

fields.label: Topic
fields.what: One of 49 topics, two guesses

fields.label: Condition present
fields.what: Does the story report a change in one of 38 world conditions

fields.label: Which condition
fields.what: Names it, among the items where it found one

fields.label: Direction
fields.what: Up or down

fields.label: Size
fields.what: How big, within one step of Sonnet's level

fields.label: Which condition, all real cases
fields.what: Its top pick for every real condition, no confidence gate (the honest version of the row above)

fields.label: Direction, all real cases
fields.what: Up or down, once it named the right condition, over all real conditions

fields.label: Size, all real cases
fields.what: Within one step, once it named the right condition, over all real conditions

fields.label: Traits (51 questions, 8 groups)
fields.what: Movement, direction and effect, intent, risk, scale, certainty, time, importance

layers.name: Area (drill into one thing)
layers.asks: Pick something from the Pulse, such as a capability, and see what drives it, depends on it and is affected by it. Pilot done (L384): tags can be proposed on the CPU and verified by Clef, but agreement is only moderate, so the design is a hybrid.

fields.label: Things and capabilities
fields.what: Find entities, places, concepts and capabilities in the item and link each to one stable identity. Pilot: about 5 tags per full article, 3 per headline item; reading the whole article adds 56% new tags.

fields.label: Events and relations
fields.what: What happened, who took part, and how things connect. Related tags (Gaza / Gaza Strip / Palestinians) merge by similarity; identity needs entity linking.

layers.name: Understanding (downstream, does not block)
layers.asks: One consolidated explanation per capability, whoever said it, traced back to its sources. Where do new items agree, disagree or leave gaps?

fields.label: Consolidated knowledge
fields.what: How a capability works and best practice across the field, merged from many sources

fields.label: Agree, contradict, gap
fields.what: Check each new item against what we know and flag what is new or missing

fields.label: Claim, evidence, source
fields.what: Every statement traced to the source text it came from; the raw documents stay but are not the focus

next.headline: Decision for you: adopt the v6b-student challenger?
next.body: Measured on 1,593 fresh natural items the engine never saw: story type +3.0 points, topic one guess +3.3, real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5%, all three of condition-direction-size right 15% to 26%, which condition +3.6 (all with intervals above zero). Speed stays inside the budget (15 ms typical, 17 ms at the slow end). Still weak: with one topic guess 82% and only 33% of real conditions found, condition detection remains the weakest field. Adoption replaces v5-leaf on the page and in the service; nothing has been replaced yet.

text: FINE-TUNED TEACHER RESULT, 8 EPOCHS (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, lr 3e-5, hard labels, 16k set, DEVQ): story 0.897, topic top-1 0.780 (top-2 0.874), presence recall@0.83 0.443 (AUC 0.915), which 0.782; training loss 0.74 (it is overfitting). vs frozen 4B reader 0.909, 0.800, 0.443, 0.831. Only presence ties (0.443 vs 0.443); topic -0.020, story -0.012, which -0.049. RULE (L485): not better than the frozen 4B by 0.02 topic or 0.05 presence => NO distillation from a fine-tuned 0.6B. TEACHER LEVERS CLOSED at this size: frozen readers (9 encoders), ensemble (no gain), fine-tuned 0.6B (no gain over frozen 4B). What remains for the weakest field is more real conditions (daily queue labelling) and the definition of a condition, not reader size.

TRAITS PRESENT/ABSENT READOUT PREDICT + RULE (the next cut named in L464; GPU heads, minutes). For each of the 51 questions, present = Sonnet grade above 'not at all' ('cannot tell' excluded); the same dense GPU head as the matrix on frozen embeddings of leaf, qwen3-4b and the five-reader ensemble, trained on the 1,500 Sonnet-graded training items, scored on the 1,150 Sonnet-graded DEVQ items. PER QUESTION: AUC of present vs absent, and the share of present cases found at precision 0.80 on those 1,150 items. A question is READY as a present/absent flag if it finds at least 50 percent of present cases at precision 0.80 and has at least 20 present cases in the eval items. PREDICT: leaf mean AUC 0.86 to 0.88 (the sparse+leaf head gave 0.87), qwen3-4b 0.88 to 0.92; READY questions: leaf 12 to 22 of 51, qwen3-4b 16 to 28; best groups risk and direction_effect (concrete events); weakest certainty and importance. RULE: group verdicts go on the Engine card as 'traits: partial' with the ready list if at least half of a group's questions are ready; a stronger reader raising AUC by 0.03 or more means the traits student should be distilled like the main fields; otherwise traits need more graded labels, not a bigger reader.

TRAITS PRESENT/ABSENT RESULT (traits_binary.py, runs/pulse/traits_binary.json; frozen embeddings, dense GPU head, trained on 1,500 Sonnet-graded items, scored on 1,150; present = any grade above 'not at all'; agreement with Sonnet). MEAN AUC: leaf 0.877, qwen3-4b 0.889 (+0.012), five-reader ensemble 0.898 (+0.021). READY QUESTIONS (find 50 percent or more of present cases at precision 0.80 and at least 20 present cases): leaf 24 of 51, qwen3-4b 30 of 51, ensemble 28 of 51. BY GROUP (ready of questions, leaf / qwen3-4b / ensemble; AUC of leaf): scale 6/6, 6/6, 6/6 (0.888); intent 5/8, 6/8, 6/8 (0.880); risk 3/8, 4/8, 3/8 (0.941, the best AUC); movement 3/8, 3/8, 3/8 (0.849); certainty 3/5, 3/5, 3/5 (0.856); importance 2/4, 2/4, 2/4 (0.875); direction_effect 1/8, 4/8, 3/8 (0.868); time 1/4, 2/4, 2/4 (0.823, the weakest). PREDICTIONS: leaf AUC 0.86 to 0.88 HELD; qwen3-4b 0.88 to 0.92 HELD (0.889); READY leaf 12 to 22 MISSED high (24), qwen3-4b 16 to 28 MISSED high (30); risk best group HELD; weakest groups certainty and importance MISSED in part (time is weakest, certainty second). RULE (L489): groups with at least half their questions ready on the CPU-size reader (leaf): scale, intent (5 of 8), certainty, importance (2 of 4) => 'traits: partial' with the ready list; a stronger reader adds only +0.012 AUC (below the 0.03 distillation trigger) => traits need more graded labels, not a bigger reader. engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.

next.headline: Decision for you: adopt v6b-student? It is the first version that passes the Ready rule on story type.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

fitness.name: Field fitness screen v1
fitness.clef: Presence, 7,710 items: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and Haiku 63%; Sonnet and Haiku agree 71% (Clef was asked a different wording)
notes: Sample is 395 items with about half real conditions, so guess rates differ from the natural stream.
Story type: voters agree 92% but α reads 0.70 because 93% of answers are 'fact'. α under-rates a skewed field.
Verdict cut-offs (α 0.8 build, 0.4 drop) are published rules of thumb, not proof.
Surface / mixed / implied is read from Sonnet-vs-Haiku agreement (≥90 / 75–90 / under 75); that cut-off is our own.

text: SCORE of L499 (Field Fitness Screen v1, projects/world-state/fitness_screen.py -> runs/pulse/fitness_screen_v1.json, 395 items x 4 same-spec labels). Called right: topic Build, condition present Rework, which-condition Build, direction Build (4 of 6). Wrong: story type predicted Build, got Rework (agree 92% but alpha 0.70 because 93% of answers are 'fact'; alpha under-rates skewed fields); size predicted Rework, got Build (interval alpha 0.83; exact-level cross-model only 74%, so alpha flatters it). Traits: 15 Build, 29 Rework, 4 Don't build, 3 Wait of 51, so fewer passes than 'about half'. Clef on presence (7,710 items): agrees with Sonnet 63%, Haiku 63%; Sonnet-Haiku 71%. Engine page now has Field|Status|Now->target|Working|Not working|Next step, a fitness section and hover glossary (card at next ledger line). No installs, no hosted calls.

PREDICTION (before run): rescore v5-leaf and v6b-student on the 395 dev2 items against the 4-voter CONSENSUS (Sonnet x2, Haiku x2) instead of Sonnet alone. Items split 2-2 or worse are excluded and reported as contested (expect story 7%, topic 9%, presence 23% from the fitness screen). Expect: engine agreement on non-split items 1 to 4 pts higher than against Sonnet alone for story type and topic; condition-present reach about the same (v5-leaf ~20%, v6b ~33%); v6b still ahead of v5-leaf on story type, topic and which-condition. Set is stratified (about half real conditions), so compare the two engines on the same set, not against the DEVQ figures. CPU only, no hosted calls, under 10 min.

SCORE of L502 (consensus rescore, projects/world-state/consensus_rescore.py, runs/pulse/consensus_*.json). FIRST RUN WAS CONTAMINATED: the 395 dev2 items include 309 dated before the 2026-10-25 training cutoff, so v5-leaf scored story 98.4% / topic 96.6% against consensus (DEVQ says 87.5 / 89.6); discard those figures. Clean rerun on the 86 items dated after the cutoff (runs/pulse/consensus_*_clean.json, selfcons_clean_ids.json): contested (voters split) story 7%, topic 9%, presence 22%. Against consensus on non-split items: story v5-leaf 92.5% [84.6,96.5] v6b 95.0% [87.8,98.0] vs always-fact 90.0%; topic v5-leaf 93.6% v6b 94.9% (top-2; guess 15.4%); presence right v5-leaf 26.9% v6b 46.3% vs always-yes 68.7% (set is 69% real, stratified); finds real v5-leaf 10.9% v6b 32.6%; which-condition of real v5-leaf 8.7% v6b 23.9%. Direction/size n<12, not scored. Prediction: story/topic 1-4 pts above Sonnet-only (story +1.8 / +0.8 ok; topic v5 +5.2 high); reach v6b ~33% hit, v5-leaf 11% vs ~20% predicted (low); v6b ahead everywhere (hit). LESSON: dev2 is not a clean held-out set; filter by date >= test_start before scoring any engine on it. n=86 means wide ranges; this checks direction, not a verdict.

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

items.what: Word counts + logistic regression alone
items.result: Story type at teacher level (0.90), topic weak (0.54)
items.outcome: Kept for story type and as the always-on path

items.what: Static word vectors (potion-8M) + logistic regression

items.what: Frozen bge-small encoder features added
items.result: Which-condition top-1 0.704 to 0.770, top-2 0.828 to 0.905
items.outcome: Adopted, routed items only (v3)

items.what: Tuning regularisation (C) of the topic heads on a validation slice

items.what: Swapping the encoder bge-small for MongoDB/mdbr-leaf-mt, picked from a scan of all 215 scored models
items.result: Pulse fields tie; 95% of reads under 22.6 ms vs 36.6; 643 MB vs 724; neighbour topic agreement 0.683 vs 0.648; chunked late-passage recall 0.859 vs 0.867
items.outcome: Adopted as the trunk (all three adoption rules held)

tried_groups.name: Swapping the trunk (Granite small R2)
tried_groups.summary: Ties with bge-small on every Pulse field (short items). On whole articles a bigger window beats truncating at 512, but chunking bge-small beats one long Granite pass and costs far less CPU. Plan for long articles: bge-small chunks feeding tag-level joins.

items.what: ibm-granite/granite-embedding-small-english-r2 as the shared encoder (47.7M, Apache-2.0, 8k, ModernBERT), same heads and items
items.result: Topic top-2 0.881 vs 0.877, which-condition 0.875 vs 0.863, all inside the noise; encoder alone 23 ms; engine p95 44.5 ms vs 36.2; memory 837 MB vs 732
items.outcome: bge-small stays; revisit when Area needs token-level heads

items.what: Long-term features: joining quality and long-input cost, Granite vs bge-small
items.result: Neighbour topic agreement 0.634 vs 0.648; cluster agreement (NMI) 0.383 vs 0.408; 8,192 tokens 22 s vs about 3.9 s chunked
items.outcome: Granite not ahead; one test left (token-level tagging head, needs the Area tag labels)

items.what: Whole-article test: can a passage from the late part find its article? (1,500 long articles, median 1,078 tokens)
items.result: bge truncated 0.50; Granite whole article 0.64; bge chunked mean 0.77; bge best chunk 0.87 (recall@1, late passages)
items.outcome: Owner's logic holds (bigger window beats truncation); chunking a small model wins

tried_groups.name: Bigger or tuned neural models
tried_groups.summary: Fine-tuning, int8 and distilling the encoder were not better, or not fast enough.

items.what: Fine-tuning the encoder
items.result: First try much worse (topic top-2 0.726); corrected try +0.014 on topic but worse on which-condition
items.outcome: Rejected: frozen features beat it

items.what: int8 encoder to make it fast enough
items.result: Topic top-2 drops 0.019 against a 0.01 limit
items.outcome: Rejected; cascade instead

items.what: Distilling the encoder into static vectors
items.result: Keeps none of the encoder's lift (topic top-2 0.813 vs 0.832)
items.outcome: Rejected

tried_groups.name: Outside language models (d1, LFM3)
tried_groups.summary: d1 is a strong second opinion (topic 0.926 when combined) but needs the GPU and its licence does not fit. LFM3 is unusable.

items.what: d1-2B decision model, zero-shot, on the GPU
items.result: Alone: topic top-2 0.852. Fused with our student: topic top-2 0.926, condition top-1 0.834
items.outcome: Pipeline test only: GPU, and a licence the owner called not commercially viable

items.what: LFM3-1.7B as a JSON reader
items.result: Only 28% valid JSON; as a yes/no scorer AUC 0.54 to 0.61
items.outcome: Rejected

tried_groups.name: Teaching tricks
tried_groups.summary: Training our student on d1's soft labels gave no gain.

items.what: Training the student on d1's soft labels
items.result: Topic top-2 -0.008, story -0.006, which-condition +0.009 to +0.02
items.outcome: No gain; d1 stays a live second opinion

tried_groups.name: Free-form tags (pilot: 100 articles, 100 headline items)
tried_groups.summary: CPU proposes, Clef verifies: about 3 tags per headline item, 5.4 per full article; wording agreement about 0.5; 77% of tags occur once. Capabilities are 7% of general-news tags and 23% of tech-news tags, and almost never recur across articles: news can propose capability candidates but cannot supply the capability layer. Design: a hybrid.

items.what: Tag pilot with spaCy proposer and local Clef verifier (5 narrow yes/no questions per candidate)
items.result: 41% of 2,762 candidates accepted; kappa 0.49 to 0.53; merge at cosine 0.80 cuts distinct tags by 33% but merges related, not only identical, tags; 56% of full-article tags are absent from the short version
items.outcome: Hybrid design; capability layer needs tech sources; a token-level tag head is the serving route (the proposer takes 0.7 s per item)

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: waiting for your yes (v5-leaf unchanged)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

T20 engine card: BitMob Expert 1 v5-leaf

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

layers.name: Area (drill into one thing)
layers.asks: Pick something from the Pulse, such as a capability, and see what drives it, depends on it and is affected by it. Pilot done (L384): tags can be proposed on the CPU and verified by Clef, but agreement is only moderate, so the design is a hybrid.

fields.label: Things and capabilities
fields.what: Find entities, places, concepts and capabilities in the item and link each to one stable identity. Pilot: about 5 tags per full article, 3 per headline item; reading the whole article adds 56% new tags.

fields.label: Events and relations
fields.what: What happened, who took part, and how things connect. Related tags (Gaza / Gaza Strip / Palestinians) merge by similarity; identity needs entity linking.

layers.name: Understanding (downstream, does not block)
layers.asks: One consolidated explanation per capability, whoever said it, traced back to its sources. Where do new items agree, disagree or leave gaps?

fields.label: Consolidated knowledge
fields.what: How a capability works and best practice across the field, merged from many sources

fields.label: Agree, contradict, gap
fields.what: Check each new item against what we know and flag what is new or missing

fields.label: Claim, evidence, source
fields.what: Every statement traced to the source text it came from; the raw documents stay but are not the focus

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.
next.ask: adopt v6b-student (sealed check first) · capability sources · tags at serving
