fit.why: Models agree on the exact step only 74% of the time; 'major' only 66%; 11% of items split.
fit.fix: Define each size step more tightly, then switch to the exact-step measure (needs your yes).

fields.label: Traits (51 questions, 8 groups)
fields.what: 51 questions in 8 groups. Not built into the engine yet. Tested on the CPU reader as present/absent flags: 24 of 51 questions usable (find half of present cases at 80% right); strongest groups scale (6 of 6) and intent (5 of 8). Graded answers (slightly / clearly / strongly) are not ready: 2 of 51.

layers.name: Area (drill into one thing)
layers.asks: Pick something from the Pulse, such as a capability, and see what drives it, depends on it and is affected by it. Pilot done (L384): tags can be proposed on the CPU and verified by Clef, but agreement is only moderate, so the design is a hybrid.

fields.label: Things and capabilities
fields.what: Find entities, places, concepts and capabilities in the item and link each to one stable identity. Pilot: about 5 tags per full article, 3 per headline item; reading the whole article adds 56% new tags.

fields.label: Events and relations
fields.what: What happened, who took part, and how things connect. Related tags (Gaza / Gaza Strip / Palestinians) merge by similarity; identity needs entity linking.

layers.name: Understanding (downstream, does not block)
layers.asks: One consolidated explanation per capability, whoever said it, traced back to its sources. Where do new items agree, disagree or leave gaps?

fields.label: Consolidated knowledge
fields.what: How a capability works and best practice across the field, merged from many sources

fields.label: Agree, contradict, gap
fields.what: Check each new item against what we know and flag what is new or missing

fields.label: Claim, evidence, source
fields.what: Every statement traced to the source text it came from; the raw documents stay but are not the focus

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.
next.ask: adopt v6b-student (sealed check first) · capability sources · tags at serving

tried_groups.name: What worked
tried_groups.summary: Word counts and static vectors for everything, a frozen small encoder on routed items (now mdbr-leaf-mt, 22.6M), and regularisation tuned on a validation slice (topic +0.02, topic overfitting gap 0.103 to 0.042).

items.what: Word counts + logistic regression alone
items.result: Story type at teacher level (0.90), topic weak (0.54)
items.outcome: Kept for story type and as the always-on path

items.what: Static word vectors (potion-8M) + logistic regression
items.result: Topic 0.62; confidence is trustworthy (calibration error 0.04)
items.outcome: Kept (the base of every version)

items.what: Frozen bge-small encoder features added
items.result: Which-condition top-1 0.704 to 0.770, top-2 0.828 to 0.905
items.outcome: Adopted, routed items only (v3)

items.what: Tuning regularisation (C) of the topic heads on a validation slice
items.result: Topic top-2 0.857 to 0.877; topic gap 0.103 to 0.059; story unchanged (best C stays 3)

items.what: Swapping the encoder bge-small for MongoDB/mdbr-leaf-mt, picked from a scan of all 215 scored models

items.outcome: Adopted as the trunk (all three adoption rules held)

tried_groups.name: Swapping the trunk (Granite small R2)
tried_groups.summary: Ties with bge-small on every Pulse field (short items). On whole articles a bigger window beats truncating at 512, but chunking bge-small beats one long Granite pass and costs far less CPU. Plan for long articles: bge-small chunks feeding tag-level joins.

items.what: ibm-granite/granite-embedding-small-english-r2 as the shared encoder (47.7M, Apache-2.0, 8k, ModernBERT), same heads and items
items.result: Topic top-2 0.881 vs 0.877, which-condition 0.875 vs 0.863, all inside the noise; encoder alone 23 ms; engine p95 44.5 ms vs 36.2; memory 837 MB vs 732
items.outcome: bge-small stays; revisit when Area needs token-level heads

items.what: Long-term features: joining quality and long-input cost, Granite vs bge-small
items.result: Neighbour topic agreement 0.634 vs 0.648; cluster agreement (NMI) 0.383 vs 0.408; 8,192 tokens 22 s vs about 3.9 s chunked
items.outcome: Granite not ahead; one test left (token-level tagging head, needs the Area tag labels)

items.what: Whole-article test: can a passage from the late part find its article? (1,500 long articles, median 1,078 tokens)
items.result: bge truncated 0.50; Granite whole article 0.64; bge chunked mean 0.77; bge best chunk 0.87 (recall@1, late passages)
items.outcome: Owner's logic holds (bigger window beats truncation); chunking a small model wins

tried_groups.summary: Fine-tuning, int8 and distilling the encoder were not better, or not fast enough.

items.what: Fine-tuning the encoder
items.result: First try much worse (topic top-2 0.726); corrected try +0.014 on topic but worse on which-condition
items.outcome: Rejected: frozen features beat it

tried_groups.name: Free-form tags (pilot: 100 articles, 100 headline items)
tried_groups.summary: CPU proposes, Clef verifies: about 3 tags per headline item, 5.4 per full article; wording agreement about 0.5; 77% of tags occur once. Capabilities are 7% of general-news tags and 23% of tech-news tags, and almost never recur across articles: news can propose capability candidates but cannot supply the capability layer. Design: a hybrid.

items.what: Tag pilot with spaCy proposer and local Clef verifier (5 narrow yes/no questions per candidate)
items.result: 41% of 2,762 candidates accepted; kappa 0.49 to 0.53; merge at cosine 0.80 cuts distinct tags by 33% but merges related, not only identical, tags; 56% of full-article tags are absent from the short version
items.outcome: Hybrid design; capability layer needs tech sources; a token-level tag head is the serving route (the proposer takes 0.7 s per item)

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: waiting for your yes (v5-leaf unchanged)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.title: Real conditions: counts
changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

changes.title: Traits: first results
changes.text: Sonnet graded 2,650 items on 51 questions (agrees with itself 87% on active answers). On the CPU reader, 24 of 51 questions work as present/absent flags; a 4B reader adds only a little (30 of 51). Next: build the flags into the engine, or label more graded examples.

fitness.name: Field fitness screen v1
fitness.clef: Presence, 7,710 items: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and Haiku 63%; Sonnet and Haiku agree 71% (Clef was asked a different wording)
notes: Sample is 395 items with about half real conditions, so guess rates differ from the natural stream.
Story type: 'fact' labels agree 97%, but opinion (61%) and unclear (52%) do not. That, not just the 93% share of 'fact', is why α is 0.70.
Surface / mixed / implied is read from Sonnet-vs-Haiku agreement (≥90 / 75–90 / under 75); that cut-off is our own.
These six questions and their pass bars are PROPOSED. They are not yet confirmed by the owner.
fitness.legend: Status: does the engine meet the bar today? Fit: are the labels clean enough to train on? Rework means the definition needs fixing first; more training will not help.

questions.q: Is the answer stated in the text, or does it take judgment?
How many items have no majority?
questions.m: Share of items where the voters split

questions.q: Does the same model give the same answer twice?
Do they agree on each answer, rare ones too?
Can a small CPU model beat always-guessing?
questions.m: Best engine's low end vs the guess rate

fitness.rule: Fit uses the first five checks. Build: Definition passes, nothing fails, at most one is partly. Don't build: Definition fails. Otherwise Rework. Learnable is the model's check and feeds Status.

notes: Only items dated after the 2026-10-25 training cutoff are scored. The first run on all 395 items was contaminated (story type 98%) and was discarded.
86 items means wide ranges (story type v5-leaf 85 to 97%). This shows direction, not a verdict.
Set is 69% real conditions, so Condition present: right is judged against always-yes.
Direction and size have under 12 scorable items and are not scored.

text: FIELD QUALIFICATION MATRIX (owner: could not tell a good field from a bad one; the screen's questions were never put to them). Engine tab now opens with 'Field qualification' (Define stage): six questions per field with pass bars, one row per field, with the verdict rule shown. Questions: 1 Definition (alpha 0.8+), 2 Evidence in text (Sonnet vs Haiku 75%+), 3 Contested (split 10% or less), 4 Consistency (same voter twice 90%+), 5 Every answer (lowest per-answer agreement 70%+), 6 Learnable (an engine beats always-guess; feeds Status not Fit). Q5 replaces 'voter risk' from my earlier list because it explains the failures; voter-vs-others rates stay in fitness_screen_v1.json. Fit rule: Build = Definition passes, nothing fails, at most one partly; Dont build = Definition fails; else Rework. RULE CHANGED AFTER SEEING RESULTS: Size moves Build -> Rework (3 partly: evidence 74%, contested 11%, 'major' 66%). All bars are PROPOSED, marked on the page as not yet confirmed by the owner. Layout fix: the table no longer collapses by viewport width (that hid the headers and crushed the text columns); it now stacks with labels by card width, and text uses text-wrap:pretty, no mid-phrase breaks. Not verified in a browser (none available here).

Rework cause (395 items, 4 same-spec voters): splits are model bias, not noise. Presence: Haiku says yes 67% vs Sonnet 49%, and 114 of 162 split items are Haiku-yes/Sonnet-no. Size: Haiku calls minor 121 times vs Sonnet 62, Sonnet calls major 56 vs Haiku 34. Story type: Haiku says opinion 19-23 vs Sonnet 8 and forecast 28 vs 15. Each model is self-consistent at 90-99%, so the definitions lack a boundary rule; proposed fix is a boundary test plus one anchored example per answer then a re-vote of 395 items at about 0.65 USD inside D12, not run, wording awaits owner.

RESEARCH on field fit and label consensus saved to projects/world-state/FIT_RESEARCH.md (5 searches, summaries only, no source opened). Supported: Krippendorff alpha 0.800 reliable / 0.667 lowest (2004 p.241); the prevalence paradox (Feinstein and Cicchetti 1990) and its fix, separate positive and negative agreement per answer, which is our per-answer check; CIs for that agreement fine from n 200 (Graham and Bull 1998); pilot-and-fix-guideline MAMA cycle; Plank 2022 says disagreement can be signal. NOT found: any published bar for minimum real cases, contested share, self-consistency or cross-family agreement, or a named field-fit test; those bars in fitness_screen.py are ours, unvalidated. Owner asked for sourced checks after the Fit column was found to be my design.

RESEARCH consensus side added to projects/world-state/FIT_RESEARCH.md (5 searches, summaries only). Supported: use different model families (Verga 2024 PoLL); stability is not correctness (arXiv 2609.15194, 2601.02370); weighted aggregation exists (Dawid-Skene 1979, MACE 2013) while ours is plain 3-of-4 majority; soft labels beat majority vote and dropping contested items sits between (Wu 2023 and others). Not found: any bar for the 3-of-4 rule, voter count or cross-family agreement. Consequence: consensus_rescore.py excludes split items, the hard ones, so its scores overstate; flagged for the page.

PREDICTION (before run) of sourced-check tests, script projects/world-state/sourced_checks_test.py. A prevalence paradox (Feinstein and Cicchetti 1990): story type cross-family raw agreement 90 percent or more but kappa 0.5 or less and Gwet AC1 0.85 or more (skew artifact); condition present raw about 68 percent with AC1 0.5 or less (real disagreement, not skew). C Dawid-Skene vs plain majority on the 395 items: changes the label on 5 percent or fewer of story-type items; on contested presence items neither method agrees with Clef (third system, noul over 0.5) better than 60 percent. B no new run: compare existing rescore rates with and without contested items.

SCORE of L514 (sourced_checks_test.py -> runs/pulse/sourced_checks_test.json, 395 items, cross-family pairs n=790). A story type raw 92.2 percent, kappa 0.583 (predicted 0.5 or less: MISSED, moderate), AC1 0.916 (hit): skew inflates the kappa gap but opinion specific agreement is 0.48, so the real weakness stays. Presence raw 68.1, kappa 0.365, AC1 0.378 (hit): no skew artifact, the disagreement is real. C Dawid-Skene differs from clear majority on 1 of 395 items for both fields (hit); on the 162 split presence items Clef agrees with Dawid-Skene 55.6 and with majority 57.4 percent (hit, both under 60): Clef cannot arbitrate, those items are truly ambiguous. D-S rates Sonnet reliable 1.0 and Haiku 0.86 only because Sonnet is stricter; no ground truth, so that is not evidence Sonnet is right. B from existing rescore: dropping split items lifts story type 95.0 vs 94.2 and topic 94.9 vs 94.2 (under 1 point); presence not comparable, untested. So L513 'scores overstate' is true in direction but small where measurable.

VALIDATION 1 of the sourced checks: alpha() in fitness_screen.py:19-33 against Krippendorff's definition. MM3-0570 (quick, 9 questions): all three concerns pass (correctness 0.95-0.97, input 0.94-0.96, design 0.85-0.98), goal 0.93, route ship 0.81; severity unsure (top none, p 0.39) and scope unsure (enough 0.65), overall gate unsure, consensus STRONG, not a found defect. Independent fixtures (own script, no krippendorff package installed): perfect agreement 1.0; hand case 4 AA 4 BB 2 AB gives 0.62 = hand value 1-0.2/(200/380); independent random labels 0.008; single answer None; interval ordering correct. One fixture failed: always-opposite gave -0.9 while I expected -1.0; hand calculation gives -0.9 (finite n), so my expectation was wrong, not the code. Lean 4 install was blocked by the auto-mode permission check (external installer code); licences read: Lean 4 Apache-2.0, elan Apache-2.0 or MIT; owner must allow or run the install.

PREDICTION (before run) Lean 4.35.0 proofs, file projects/world-state/lean/FitChecks.lean, no Mathlib. P1 vote-status rule: for every 4-vote vector over 4 answers, status is 'majority' exactly when some answer has 3 votes and 'split' exactly when none has 3 (proved by exhaustive decide; expect it to compile). P2 binary two-coder alpha as exact rationals: alpha <= 1 always, alpha = 1 exactly when no disagreements, and the 4/4/2 case equals 31/50 = 0.62, the value the Python alpha returned (expect compile; the general inequality may need a lemma I cannot finish without Mathlib, in which case I report it as unproved). Limits: this proves the maths model, not that fitness_screen.py matches; the shared worked example is the only link.

SCORE of L517 (Lean 4.35.0, projects/world-state/lean/FitChecks.lean): all four theorems compile with no sorry (prediction: compile, general inequality might fail; it compiled). Proved: status_rule (for all 256 combinations of 4 votes over 4 answers: majority iff some answer has exactly 3, split iff none has 3 or more, unanimous iff one has 4); alpha_le_one (binary two-coder alpha never exceeds 1); alpha_one_iff (with at least 2 values alpha equals 1 exactly when no disagreements); alpha_worked_case (4 AA, 4 BB, 2 AB gives 31/50 = 0.62, the value Python returned). Controls: print axioms shows only the standard propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; two false claims (majority iff top >= 2; 30/50) were rejected by decide. Limits: proves the maths model, not fitness_screen.py; only link is the shared worked example. Not yet covered: general n coders, interval alpha, per-answer agreement, kappa/AC1, soft labels.

PREDICTION (before run) MUTATION TEST of the verification layers (owner 2026-11-02: have MM3 partner on proofs, find shortcuts, see if it saves time). Plant 7 bugs in alpha() (pair weight 1/m, expected-disagreement n*n, sign flip, n+=1, rounded to 1 digit, skip rule m<3, nominal difference inverted) and 1 in status() (majority uses >= half). Methods: F = existing 6 hand fixtures; O = Lean-computed exact oracle vs Python on 300 random binary two-coder cases plus all 256 status vectors; M = MM3 quick class (9 questions) on each mutant. Predict: F catches 5 or more of 7 alpha bugs and 0 of 1 status bug; O catches every alpha bug that shows in the binary two-coder shape and the status bug; M catches 5 or more of 8 but misses the rounding bug; all three together catch 8 of 8. Also record wall time and MM3 cost per method.

SCORE of L519 mutation test (lean/mutation_test.py -> runs/pulse/mutation_FO.json; MM3-0571 to 0580). Planted bugs: alpha m1 pair weight 1/m, m2 n*n, m3 sign flip, m4 n+=1, m5 round 1 digit, m6 skip rule m<3, m7 nominal difference inverted; status m1 majority uses >= half. RESULTS. Hand fixtures F: caught 7 of 7 alpha bugs, 0 of 1 status (no status fixtures existed); clean code passes. Lean oracle O (300 random binary two-coder cases + all 256 status vectors, 5.3 s, free): caught 8 of 8, clean passes. MM3 quick class, 9 questions, one run per file (cost under 0.01 USD each, budget still 5.00 at 2 decimals): hard catch 1 of 8 (m3 sign flip, MM3-0574: goal fail 0.26, q2 0.32). Weak signals only: m1 q3 0.77 (MM3-0572, base 0.95), m6 q1 0.77 (MM3-0577), status m1 goal 0.67 unsure vs base 0.77 pass (MM3-0580 vs 0579). Missed outright: m4 (MM3-0575), m5 rounding (MM3-0576, predicted), m7 (MM3-0578): q6 asked directly whether different values count as 1 and equal as 0 and answered 0.92 yes on code that does the reverse. The clean status base itself scored q3 0.84 and goal 0.77, so MM3 on small numeric code is noisy. Prediction 'MM3 catches 5 or more of 8' MISSED (1 of 8). Predictions hit: F 5+ of 7 alpha and 0 of 1 status; O catches all; all three together 8 of 8 (carried by F and O); MM3 misses rounding. Lesson: for numeric code the Lean-computed oracle is the strong verifier; MM3 reading the code is a weak numeric checker and should be used for spec-level questions (claim matches source, scope, design). Thresholds on weak signals were read after seeing results, not pre-registered.

PREDICTION (before run) REPLICATION of the mutation test (owner 2026-11-02: prove the statements, record learning, state assumptions). Change from L519: mutants are generated mechanically (operator swaps, constant plus or minus 1, sign flips), not hand-picked, on two functions: alpha() and pair_stats() (kappa, AC1, PABAK, per-answer agreement; sourced_checks_test.py). Equivalent mutants (same output on 5,000 random inputs) are excluded and listed. Methods: F hand fixtures (pair_stats gets 2 hand-computed cases: 85/5/5/5 skewed and 40/40/10/10), O Lean exact oracle (300 random binary two-coder cases per function), M MM3 quick class on a random 10 of the pair_stats mutants. Predict: O kills 90 percent or more of non-equivalent mutants on BOTH functions; F kills 80 percent or fewer on pair_stats (only two fixtures); M kills 2 or fewer of 10. If O falls under 90 percent on either, the claim 'the oracle is the strong verifier' is not supported and I say so. ASSUMPTIONS in force: (A1) the 395-item four-voter sample is representative of the news pool beyond stratification; (A2) Sonnet and Haiku r1/r2 are independent enough to count as four voters (same prompt, two families); (A3) Krippendorff 0.8/0.667 and the 1990 per-answer agreement are the right bars for LLM voters, not only for human coders; (A4) Lean models cover binary two-coder shapes while the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers; (A5) mutation kill rate on seeded bugs predicts catching real future bugs; (A6) MM3 results from the quick 9-question form say nothing about thorough depth; (A7) search summaries, not the papers, were read.

SCORE of L521 (lean/replication_test.py -> runs/pulse/replication_FO.json), mechanical mutants, equivalents removed. alpha(): 28 non-equivalent; hand fixtures killed 24 (86 percent), Lean oracle killed 21 (75 percent). pair_stats(): 48 non-equivalent; fixtures killed 43 (90 percent), oracle killed 36 (75 percent). PREDICTION MISSED: 'oracle kills 90 percent or more on both' is false (75 and 75), and 'fixtures 80 percent or fewer on pair_stats' is false (90). The L520 conclusion 'the Lean oracle is the strong verifier' is NOT supported: every mutant the oracle killed the fixtures also killed, so the oracle added nothing over good fixtures on these two functions. Survivors show why: both tests use two coders, so mutant L7:78 (pair weight 1/(m-1) becomes m-1, identical at m=2) survives, yet the pipeline uses 4 voters; threshold boundary (20 votes) and rounding-digit mutants (3 to 4 digits, within the 0.0006 tolerance) survive the oracle. What the oracle did give: exact certified values for the fixtures (Lean theorems balanced_case, skewed_case) and a kill of the status bug where no fixture existed. Next (predicted before run): add an independent reference implementation of alpha by direct definition (all value pairs) over 2 to 4 coders, nominal and interval, as method R; predict it kills the multi-coder survivors (L7:78 and the m<2 boundary ones) and lifts alpha kills to 90 percent or more.

SCORE of L522 and MM3 leg of L521. R = independent reference alpha by direct definition (all value pairs, 2 to 4 coders, nominal and interval): killed 25 of 28 non-equivalent alpha mutants (89 percent; predicted 90 or more, missed by one mutant); survivors are two boundary cases (n < 2 changed to <= 2 and < 3, no test with exactly 2 values) and one rounding digit (3 to 4, inside tolerance, harmless). All three methods together on alpha: 25 of 28, same as R alone. MM3 quick class (MM3-0581 base to MM3-0591) on 10 random pair_stats mutants, rule fixed before reading: caught if goal not pass or any of Q1 to Q6 under 0.70; base MM3-0581 passes clean. Caught 1 of 10 (MM3-0586, chance-agreement product changed to division, Q4 0.52); prediction 'at most 2 of 10' HELD. Near misses not counted: MM3-0588 Q5 0.74, MM3-0591 Q2 0.71. Same 10 mutants: fixtures and oracle each killed 8 of 10 (both missed the rounding-digit one, MM3-0583, and /->* at L6:54, MM3-0585). SUMMARY across L520 to L523: hand fixtures 86 to 90 percent, independent reference 89 percent, Lean oracle 75 percent, MM3 reading code about 10 percent; the L520 statement 'Lean oracle is the strong verifier' is withdrawn. Lean's real contribution: certified expected values for fixtures (balanced_case, skewed_case, alpha_worked_case) and for-all-inputs properties. Learning recorded in knowledge_pipeline/LESSONS_LEARNED.md (intake line, not yet in the playbook). Open gaps: boundary fixtures (exactly 2 values; 20-vote threshold), 4-voter Lean model, rounding tolerance. Assumptions A1 to A7 as listed at L521.

AUDIT (owner asked to double check for errors, 2026-11-02). Found: (1) ERROR in sourced_checks_test.py pair_stats: PABAK used the two-answer form 2*Po-1 for all fields; with k answers PABAK is (k*Po-1)/(k-1); story type has 4 answers, so the saved 0.843 should be 0.896 (not quoted in chat; the JSON held it). Fixing and rerunning. (2) L520 said MM3 cost under 0.01 USD each; the budget display only shows 5.00 left after 21 runs, so the supportable claim is under one cent in total. (3) L520 gave 'about 25 s' for ten MM3 runs; that stamp covered my turn too, so treat it as an upper bound. (4) Replication table said MM3 'not run' on alpha: true only for the mechanical set; the hand-picked set did run (1 of 8). Predict non-equivalent kills: alpha union of methods 95 percent or more; pair_stats union 95 percent or more; pair_stats oracle alone still under 90 percent (binary only); every rounding-digit mutant now killed.

SCORE of L524 prediction, replication v2 (lean/replication_test.py; output runs/pulse/replication_FO.json, copied to replication_FO_v2.json; the v1 file of that name is overwritten, v1 numbers live only at L522/L523). RESULTS non-equivalent kills. alpha: fixtures 27 of 28 (96 percent), Lean oracle 22 (79), reference 26 (93), all three 28 (100). pair_stats: fixtures 45 of 51 (88), Lean oracle 46 (90), reference 51 (100), all three 51 (100). PREDICTIONS: union 95 percent or more on both HELD (100, 100); every rounding-digit mutant killed by some method HELD; 'pair_stats oracle alone under 90 percent' MISSED by one (90.2 percent). Survivors of single methods: alpha oracle misses multi-coder weight and n<2 boundaries (as predicted); pair_stats fixtures miss three rounding-digit and two division swaps. FIT (owner definition) shown as four tests: F1 subjective (reads alpha), F2 enough real cases (count per answer, bar ours), F3 truth source (none found, so 'agreement only'), F4 evidence in input (NOT measured; shown as not measured). engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: waiting for your yes (v5-leaf unchanged)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.title: Real conditions: counts
changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

changes.title: Traits: first results
changes.text: Sonnet graded 2,650 items on 51 questions (agrees with itself 87% on active answers). On the CPU reader, 24 of 51 questions work as present/absent flags; a 4B reader adds only a little (30 of 51). Next: build the flags into the engine, or label more graded examples.

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).
Sonnet and Haiku, two runs each, count as four voters.
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.
Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).
fitness.clef: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and with Haiku 63% on presence (a different question wording); on the 162 split items it matches majority 57%, so it cannot arbitrate them.

notes: Only items dated after the 2026-10-25 training cutoff are scored. The first run on all 395 items was contaminated (story type 98%) and was discarded.
86 items means wide ranges (story type v5-leaf 85 to 97%). This shows direction, not a verdict.
Set is 69% real conditions, so Condition present: right is judged against always-yes.
Direction and size have under 12 scorable items and are not scored.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: waiting for your yes (v5-leaf unchanged)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.title: Real conditions: counts
changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).
Sonnet and Haiku, two runs each, count as four voters.
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.
Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).
fitness.clef: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and with Haiku 63% on presence (a different question wording); on the 162 split items it matches majority 57%, so it cannot arbitrate them.

notes: Only items dated after the 2026-10-25 training cutoff are scored. The first run on all 395 items was contaminated (story type 98%) and was discarded.
86 items means wide ranges (story type v5-leaf 85 to 97%). This shows direction, not a verdict.
Set is 69% real conditions, so Condition present: right is judged against always-yes.
Direction and size have under 12 scorable items and are not scored.

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: waiting for your yes (v5-leaf unchanged)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).
Sonnet and Haiku, two runs each, count as four voters.
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.
Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).

PREDICTION (before run) STEP 1 of the proof plan: do the Fit checks predict stalls? Script projects/world-state/stall_test.py (CPU only, reuses score_end2end.py): run engine v6b-student and v5-leaf on DEVQ2 (1,593 natural items, Sonnet labels), per condition compute end-to-end recall (item found AND top condition equals the Sonnet condition) for conditions with 5 or more Sonnet positives; correlate (Spearman) with three case counts: (a) cases in the 395 four-vote sample, (b) training-period Sonnet labels p7b, (c) training-period Haiku labels p7. Predict: rho for (b) or (c) is 0.4 or more on v6b (more training cases, higher recall); rho for (a) is lower than for (b)/(c), because 395 items is a poor proxy for the training pool (a known weakness of the F2 count on the page); conditions with under 30 training cases have lower mean recall than those with 30 or more. If rho for (b) and (c) is under 0.2 the claim 'enough real cases predicts the stall' is not supported and F2 should be demoted on the page. Caveat in advance: about 10 to 15 conditions will qualify, so one correlation is noisy.

SCORE of L534 (stall_test.py -> runs/pulse/stall_test_v6b-student.json and _v5-leaf.json; DEVQ2 1,593 natural items; 11 conditions with 5 or more Sonnet positives). Spearman rho of per-condition end-to-end recall against case counts, v6b / v5-leaf: 395-sample consensus count 0.719 (p 0.013) / 0.775; training Sonnet labels 0.651 (p 0.03) / 0.698; training Haiku labels 0.478 (p 0.14) / 0.693. PREDICTION: 'b or c at least 0.4 on v6b' HELD; 'a (the 395-sample count) is lower than b and c' MISSED, it correlates best; 'under 30 training cases lower recall' UNTESTABLE (one condition, information_reliability 27 cases, recall 0.143 vs mean 0.254 for the ten others). Reading: enough real cases is weakly supported as a stall predictor, but alone it does not explain stalls: war_terror 335 training cases recall 0.083, cyber_insecurity 120 cases (27 positives) recall 0, prices 220 cases recall 0.125. EXPLORATORY (not pre-registered, n=11): per-condition agreement ratio (named by 3 or more of 4 voters / named by any voter in the 395 sample) rho 0.66 / 0.60 with recall; the five conditions under 0.45 agreement all have recall 0.2 or lower (information_reliability, civil_liberties, war_terror, biodiversity_loss, cyber_insecurity); five of six at 0.54 or above have recall 0.3 or more (prices 0.125 is the exception). Candidate rule to test out of sample on DEVQ (1,997 items) before any use: a condition with agreement under 0.45 stalls. Weakness: n=11, counts and agreement are correlated with each other, so they cannot be separated yet. Not changed on the page.

SCORE of the L535 out-of-sample test (stall_test.py devq -> runs/pulse/stall_test_v6b-student.json; DEVQ 1,997 natural items, 21 conditions with 5 or more Sonnet positives; agreement ratios come from the 395 voted items, not from DEVQ). Count correlations replicate, weaker: rho 0.58 (p 0.006) for the 395-sample consensus count, 0.47 (p 0.03) for Sonnet training cases, 0.31 (p 0.18) for Haiku. The candidate rule registered at L535, 'a condition with agreement under 0.45 stalls', HELD out of sample: of 11 such conditions (those named by 3 or more voters in the sample, 20 in total) 10 have recall 0.2 or lower, mean 0.063; the 9 at 0.45 or above have mean recall 0.316 and 5 of 9 reach 0.3 or more. Only exception under 0.45: water_stress 0.375. Caveats: the rule was formed on DEVQ2 and tested on DEVQ with the same engine (v6b-student) and the same 395-item agreement figures; engines other than v6b untested here beyond DEVQ2 (v5-leaf showed the same ordering); n=20. Use: per-condition agreement is a better stall flag than raw case counts; supports the condition-tier decision (L486, decision 2) and a stricter 'which condition' output, and should be added to the Consensus table. PREDICTION (before run) PRE-GATE TEST (owner 2026-11-03: rare answers need a pre-filter and a source that tells you something up front). Script projects/world-state/pregate_test.py, CPU only, free: on the 46,551 Haiku-labelled pool items (runs/p7), test cheap up-front signals against Haiku's story_type labels (a noisy target: Haiku and Sonnet agree on opinion only about 48 percent, so precision is read as an upper-bound proxy): URL section words for the 22,665 cc items (opinion, comment, editorial, analysis, column, blog...) and headline/text cues for all items (opinion: starts with Opinion/Analysis/Editorial, 'should', 'we need', question mark; forecast: will, expected to, forecast, could, set to). Predict: URL section cue has precision over 60 percent for opinion but recall under 15 percent (few items carry it); headline cues give lift of 2x or more at coverage 10 to 30 percent; the OR of all cues recovers 40 percent or more of Haiku-opinion at 2x or better precision than the 12.8 percent base rate (5,961 of 46,551), which would cut labelling cost for opinion at least 2x. If lift is under 1.5x the cues carry no usable up-front signal and the funnel needs the CPU model scores instead.

SCORE of L542 (pregate_test.py -> runs/pulse/pregate_test.json; 46,543 Haiku-labelled pool items; target is Haiku story_type, a noisy proxy). Base rates: opinion 12.8 percent, forecast 5.7, unclear 3.9. URL section words (22,568 cc items): opinion precision 88.1 percent, recall 12.0, coverage 1.8, lift 6.7 (prediction precision over 60 and recall under 15: HELD). Headline cues: opinion precision 46.8 recall 14.3 lift 3.7; forecast precision 32.2 recall 24.8 lift 5.6; coverage about 4 percent each (predicted lift 2x or more HELD, predicted coverage 10 to 30 percent MISSED). OR of all opinion cues: precision 52.9 (4.1x base) but recall 19.2 (predicted 40 or more: MISSED); cost cut if only flagged items are labelled about 21x but 81 percent of opinion items are never seen. Reading: cheap up-front cues find a clean, high-precision SUBSET of the rare answer, not the whole of it; they enrich a seed set but cannot enumerate or size the class, and a sample drawn from them is biased toward easy cases, so agreement measured on it overstates and a random calibration slice is needed. Script projects/world-state/tier_test.py, free, on the 395 four-vote items: sources S1 (Sonnet r1) and H1 (Haiku r1) define tiers per field; the reference is the OTHER pair (S2 and H2) when they agree with each other. Tier A = S1 and H1 agree; Tier C = they disagree. Measure how often the tier's label is reproduced by the independent reference. Predict: Tier A reproduces 95 percent or more for story type and topic and 85 percent or more for condition present; Tier C reproduces 60 percent or less on every field; Tier A covers 90 percent or more of items on story type, 85 percent on topic, 65 to 75 percent on presence. engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

layers.name: Area (drill into one thing)

fields.label: Agree, contradict, gap

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

items.outcome: Owner's logic holds (bigger window beats truncation); chunking a small model wins

BRIEF READ (owner: /workspace/_remove/rust_nlp_agent_brief.md, not to be built; techniques only). Read: decision and source table (lines 1 to 32), syntax and semantics incl. AMR-inspired schema (67 to 108), improvement loop (127 to 149); NOT read: shared evidence store, execution path, Rust/Lean job split, implementation sequence. USEFUL TECHNIQUES: (1) AMR-inspired frame with proposition scopes: a predicate with roles plus operators (negation, possibility or obligation, planning, quotation or reported claim) kept as scope, unknown values explicit; the brief warns it is AMR-inspired, not AMR-conformant, and that AMR-EAGER used learned classifiers, so it is vocabulary and design, not a training-free parser; I have not read the AMR guidelines (link in the brief). Our fit: the v3b presence rule (condition itself has already changed; plan, warning, reaction, intent or possible effect does not count) and story type (fact, forecast, opinion) are modality, polarity, time and attribution judgements, so a FRAME-FIRST labelling could split them into small closed attributes (polarity, actual vs planned vs possible vs required vs reported, time past, present, future, attribution) and DERIVE presence and story type by rule; hypothesis (not tested): attributes agree better across makers than the composite label and the derived labels are repeatable. To pre-register before any run: derived presence cross-maker alpha at least 0.10 above direct (Sonnet v3b vs Gemma 4 off direct 0.56), derived story type not worse than direct. Cost estimate small (Gemma local, about 0.1 USD hosted Haiku), not run. (2) Rule structure: guard, explicit exceptions, action, positive and negative examples, scoped constructions instead of word lists; matches our codebook with counterexamples. (3) Improvement loop: error signature, cluster by construction, bounded proposal with contrastive counterexamples, shadow evaluation on held-out data, promote only on predeclared gates, keep failures on the ledger; queue from unresolved cases, disagreements and conflicts plus a random audit of accepted high-confidence decisions; 'self-labels alone do not supply semantic truth' (same point as consistency is not correctness). (4) Three separate metrics: quality, selective coverage at a stated precision, cost; 85 percent does not locate the other 15 percent.

PRESENCE MINING (600 devq items, Gemma vs Sonnet v3b A; 57 Sonnet-yes/Gemma-no, 49 Sonnet-no/Gemma-yes): misses are judgment calls on SIZE OF THE REAL-WORLD CHANGE FOR PEOPLE, not wording. Sonnet says yes to market-wide sell-off, 3,500 deaths from smoke, election violence fears with armed attacks, oil majors on record prices, city-wide hunger, 70,000-police protest warning, closure of a national newspaper. Sonnet says no to a single exchange hack (Binance), 62 layoffs at one factory, a 2.2% budget cut, two helicopters colliding, a malicious browser extension, one Azure bug. Gemma says yes to these small, single-organisation events. So the field is 'did a society-level condition change', and what separates yes from no is scale/breadth, which a text-only student sees only through a few hundred examples. So the direction and size verdicts above are not clean verdicts on those fields. PRE-REGISTERED B3 (before any run): bundle B3 = the same 78 conditional items (chosen by the B1 presence answers, so blind to B3 answers), fields which_c, direction_c, size_c: the question says 'Assume this item reports that one listed condition has already changed' and the answer set has NO none option (38 conditions; up or down; five levels), instruction text sliced from the guideline as before, paraphrase variant P, same fixed verdict rule, unweighted, labelled conditional. Raters: Clef, Gemma, Qwen now; Jev needs the owner to raise the cumulative cap in xtest/budget_cap.json (estimate 0.12 USD for 78 items x 3 fields x 3 runs). Runner: run_bundle2.sh. Prediction: direction panel alpha at least 0.60 and size at least 0.50 if the none option was the main cause; if they stay under 0.50 the fields themselves are not reproducible across these raters.

B3 RESULT (pre-registered in L688; bundle B3 = 78 conditional items, no none option, Clef + Gemma + Qwen, lint passed, 1000 resamples; runs/xtest/B3/score_3.json; Jev not run because the cumulative cap in xtest/budget_cap.json refused it, so the run script ended BUNDLE-INCOMPLETE as designed). WHICH CONDITION (38 options): panel alpha 0.806 [0.733-0.875] = TENTATIVE (lower end under 0.80); pairs 0.737 to 0.847. DIRECTION (up or down): panel 0.478 [0.295-0.631] = REJECT; pairs 0.327, 0.597, 0.510; raw agreement 0.77 to 0.86 but the answers are skewed (up: Clef 0.73, Gemma 0.83, Qwen 0.82 of items), which is why alpha is low while raw agreement is high. SIZE (five levels): panel 0.457 [0.339-0.563] = REJECT; pairs 0.378, 0.450, 0.547; raw agreement 0.58 to 0.72; most answers are notable. PREDICTION MISSED: I expected direction at least 0.60 and size at least 0.50 if the none option was the main cause; both stayed under, so the none option was NOT the main cause. Same-rater paraphrase alpha: Clef 0.90 to 1.00, Qwen 0.87 to 0.97, Gemma 0.68 to 0.78 (Gemma again the least stable). READING, with limits: on items all four raters already see as a change, which condition is reproducible at the tentative level across three families; direction and size are not, with 78 items and intervals about 0.3 wide; direction's alpha is depressed by a one-sided answer split, so reject there means not shown reproducible at this sample size and skew, and does not mean shown irreproducible. A larger conditional set with more down items would be needed to say more. Open: Jev on B3 (0.12 USD estimate, needs the owner to raise the cap).

PRE-REGISTRATION M7, traits on the ONE structure (bundle B4). Questions: the 51 yes/no trait questions from the frozen spec specs/traits_v0.json, each asked as a noul question with the spec text as the instruction; no hand wording; the paraphrase control P is a mechanical statement form ('Consider this statement about the item: ... Answer yes if the statement is true of the item, no if it is not.'), built by rule and read in full before any run (one broken form, x050, was fixed by hand before the run). Items: 150 devq items chosen by sha256 of the id, so no rater's answer picks them (blind). Raters now: Clef, Gemma, Qwen (local); Jev waits for the owner to raise the cumulative cap (estimate 0.29 USD for 3 runs). Controls for every rater: order seed 1 and the paraphrase. Scoring: per question, panel alpha with a 1000-resample interval by the fixed rule (CLEAR lower end 0.80 or more, TENTATIVE 0.667 or more, REJECT upper end under 0.667, otherwise BORDERLINE). Declared before the result: a question whose pooled yes share is under 0.05 or over 0.95 is reported as SKEWED (alpha is unstable when one answer is almost the only one) and counted separately; the summary is the count per verdict and the list of CLEAR and TENTATIVE traits. PREDICTION: at least 10 of the 51 traits reach TENTATIVE or CLEAR (earlier readers reached Ready on 8 to 10 of 51 against Sonnet, L661, a different and harder test), and Gemma is the least stable rater. Run through run_bundle2.sh.

M7 RESULT, traits on the ONE structure (pre-registered L690; bundle B4: 150 blind items x 51 yes/no questions; Clef, Gemma, Qwen; lint passed; 1000 resamples; runs/xtest/B4/score_3.json; Jev not run, cap). Panel verdict counts by the fixed rule, with the declared SKEWED class (pooled yes share under 0.05 or over 0.95): CLEAR 0, TENTATIVE 1, BORDERLINE 12, REJECT 21, SKEWED 17 of 51. The one TENTATIVE trait is x025 (deaths or injuries): alpha 0.916 [0.796-1.000], yes share 0.09. PREDICTION MISSED: I expected at least 10 traits at TENTATIVE or CLEAR; got 1. Gemma the least stable rater: HIT (median same-rater paraphrase alpha 0.661 against Qwen 0.701 and Clef 0.744). THE LARGER FINDING: the traits are unstable under rewording even for one model. Only 5 of 51 questions have all three raters at same-rater paraphrase alpha 0.80 or more; the other 46 do not, and a cross-model alpha is not expected to exceed the same-model alpha, so most REJECT and BORDERLINE verdicts are bounded by the wording sensitivity before any model disagreement. The 5 stable questions are x022 and x023 (intent), x025 and x031 (risk), x034 (scale); their panel alphas are 0.652, 0.681, 0.916, 0.878, 0.767. By group: risk has the most SKEWED traits (6 of 8), scale has 5 of 6 at REJECT, certainty 4 of 5 at REJECT. LIMITS: one mechanical paraphrase (statement form) was used, and it may itself shift meaning for some questions, so the wording sensitivity mixes the instrument with that transformation; a second, independent paraphrase would separate them; 150 items and rare traits give wide intervals; the earlier 8 to 10 of 51 Ready (L658 to L661) was agreement with Sonnet on a different test and is not comparable. NEXT (not run): a second independent paraphrase on the 46 unstable questions, and Jev on B4 once the owner raises the cap.

PRE-REGISTRATION M8, is the traits wording sensitivity the instrument or my rewording (L691)? A second, independent control Q on bundle B4: the ORIGINAL spec question unchanged inside a different frame, 'Read the news item, then answer this question with yes or no only. Question: <original question>' (frame text only; no change to the question words, unlike the statement form P). Same 150 items, same three local raters (Clef, Gemma, Qwen), one main run each (order seed 0). For every question and rater: same-rater alpha between the original run (A seed 0) and Q, and between P and Q. READING, fixed now: if at least 35 of 51 questions again have the minimum over raters of the A-to-Q alpha under 0.80, the sensitivity belongs to the question forms or the models (the instrument); if fewer than 20 do, the statement form P was the main cause and the L691 wording finding is mostly an artifact of my rewording; between 20 and 34 is mixed. PREDICTION: mixed to instrument (at least 25). No threshold changes after the result. Jev not included (cap). Services voice and Clef stop for the local part and are restored by a trap.

OWNER YES (2026-11-04, 'yes raise it'): the cumulative hosted cap in xtest/budget_cap.json goes from 1.06 to 1.65 USD, which is 0.60 above the 1.054 already spent. It covers Jev on bundle B3 (estimate 0.12), bundle B4 traits (0.29) and the second wording control Q on B4 (0.10); total estimate 0.51, leaving about 0.09 spare. Nothing else is raised: the Sonnet typed pass (up to 3 USD) still needs its own yes. Hosted total since the 70 USD envelope: about 64.95 before this, about 65.5 after the planned Jev runs.

JEV ADDED TO B3 AND B4 (owner raised the cap, L693; lint passed; 1000 resamples; runs/xtest/B3/score_4.json and runs/xtest/B4/score_4.json; spend 1.588 of 1.65 USD). B3, 78 conditional items, no none option, four raters: WHICH 0.819 [0.753-0.883] TENTATIVE (was 0.806 with three); DIRECTION 0.591 [0.444-0.709] BORDERLINE (was 0.478 REJECT with three); SIZE 0.513 [0.409-0.597] REJECT (was 0.457). The L688 prediction (direction at least 0.60, size at least 0.50) was made for the panel that existed then, the three local raters, and that test stays MISSED; with Jev added direction is 0.591, just under 0.60, and size 0.513, just over 0.50, which is a different panel and is reported as such. Jev same-rater paraphrase alpha on B3: which 0.986, direction 1.000, size 0.897. B4 traits, four raters: CLEAR 1 (x025 deaths or injuries, 0.93 [0.83-1.00]), TENTATIVE 1 (x034 single city or smaller area, 0.806 [0.717-0.888]), BORDERLINE 12, REJECT 20, SKEWED 17 of 51; the L690 prediction of at least 10 at TENTATIVE or CLEAR stays MISSED (2). Same-rater paraphrase alpha, median over the 51 questions: Jev 0.878, Clef 0.744, Qwen 0.701, Gemma 0.661. READING: Jev holds a median of 0.878 under the same statement-form rewording that moves Gemma to 0.661, so the rewording by itself does not destroy the meaning of most questions; the instability in L691 is largely on the model side and the picture is rater-specific. The wording control Q (original question in a frame) is still running for Qwen; its comparison follows. Jev note: a more stable rater is not shown to be a more correct one.

Q CONTROL RESULT (pre-registered L692; original question words inside a different frame, Q seed 0, bundle B4, 150 items, Clef, Gemma, Qwen as registered, Jev also run). Questions with the minimum over the three registered local raters of the A-to-Q alpha under 0.80: 39 of 51 (with Jev also in the minimum: 39 of 51). The fixed reading was: at least 35 of 51 means the sensitivity belongs to the question forms or the models, not only to my rewording; it falls in that band, and the prediction (at least 25) is a HIT. Median A-to-Q alpha per rater: Jev 0.921, Clef 0.877, Qwen 0.825, Gemma 0.723 (against the statement form P: Jev 0.878, Clef 0.744, Qwen 0.701, Gemma 0.661), so the plain frame disturbs answers less than the statement form, and the ordering of raters is the same under both. 12 questions are stable for all four raters under Q: x001, x008, x010, x019, x022, x023, x024, x025, x030, x031, x034, x045; of the 5 stable under P (x022, x023, x025, x031, x034) all 5 are in that list. LIMITS: two controls so far; Jev being stable shows the instrument can be answered consistently, so the weakness is mostly in how the other models respond to wording, not a flaw that every reader shares; 150 items. This closes M7 and M8. Handoff written to GO.md; session context at about 80 percent.

PRE-REGISTRATION step 1 (GO.md Next 1): presence and direction need a better DEFINITION, not more readers. Plan: (a) write a narrow checkable-event definition for presence (one named event, one actor, one dated action in the text) and a larger conditional set with more down items for direction; (b) a second independent paraphrase for the unstable traits; (c) run through xtest on local raters only (no hosted, no new spend), with reshuffle and rewording controls and the lint. PREDICTION: narrower definition lifts panel alpha for presence above its current BORDERLINE band (lower end still under 0.80, so no CLEAR); direction stays BORDERLINE or REJECT until down items are added. SCORE AFTER: panel alpha with interval vs the playbook ch.12 verdict rule. This note is design only; no run yet, no GPU.
T21 engine card: BitMob Expert 1 v5-leaf

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: waiting for your yes (v5-leaf unchanged)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.title: Real conditions: counts
changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

changes.title: Traits: first results
changes.text: Sonnet graded 2,650 items on 51 questions (agrees with itself 87% on active answers). On the CPU reader, 24 of 51 questions work as present/absent flags; a 4B reader adds only a little (30 of 51). Next: build the flags into the engine, or label more graded examples.

fitness.name: Field checks v2
fitness.rule: Consensus verdict uses ONLY the sourced agreement score bands (Krippendorff 2004, p.241): 0.80 or more clear, 0.667 to 0.80 tentative, under 0.667 reject. Our own measures are flags and never decide.

measures.q: Do labellers agree beyond chance?
measures.m: Krippendorff's alpha: agreement beyond chance (1 = perfect, 0 = no better than guessing)

measures.q: Does agreement hold when a model from a different maker (Qwen3-14B) votes with Sonnet and Haiku?
measures.m: alpha over Sonnet, Haiku (one maker) and Qwen on the 395 items

text: T32 CHECK 5 SHARPENED (owner 2026-11-04): evidence must be DIRECTLY in the input, first-order, actionable; second or third tier inference and background knowledge do not count. Operational test in the pilot: each rater quotes the supporting span; a second reader checks that the span alone states the answer; report the share of positives with a valid span and the share that needed inference; pass line fixed before the pilot. Failing check 1 (definable and measurable) or check 5 means PARK, because a better reader does not address those two (to be confirmed on the first parked field); failing only 2 or 3 means REVISE the definition, at most two rounds. The presence rule already excludes effects inferred from background knowledge (frozen v3b guideline); the share has not been measured yet. Gate order: 1 definable, 2 reliable (agreement above line, yes-rates within a band), 3 enough real cases, 4 outside anchor, 5 directly in the input.
