It returns two topic guesses (its product contract) and may say unknown. Scores: top-1 lenient and strict, top-2 lenient (either guess in the accepted set), share unknown, ms per read. PREDICTION: top-1 lenient between 0.50 and 0.66, i.e. at or below the LLM raters (Gemma 0.660) because it was distilled from 2026 news labels and MN-DS is 2019 text with a different taxonomy; top-2 lenient lower end at least 0.70. If top-1 lands above Gemma the mapping is not the main cause of the raters gap. Output file runs/pulse/anchor_mnds_v6b-student.json.

T28 v6b-student SCORE (pre-registered L749; runs/pulse/anchor_mnds_v6b-student.json, script projects/world-state/score_anchor_v6b.py, 1676 clean MN-DS items, CPU one thread, 0 USD): top-1 lenient 1074 of 1676 = 0.641 (0.618 to 0.663), top-1 strict 0.442, top-2 lenient 1295 of 1676 = 0.773 (0.752 to 0.792), unknown share 0.0, 15.2 ms p50 and 17.1 ms p95 per read. Best constant guesses on the same items (own count): single 0.179 (sanctions_aid), best pair 0.357 (sanctions_aid with culture_leisure). PREDICTIONS: top-1 between 0.50 and 0.66 HELD (0.641); top-2 lower end at least 0.70 HELD (0.752), and it beats the best constant pair by 0.395. READING: against the human labels the 22.6M CPU reader matches the LLM raters on top-1 (Clef 0.640, Gemma 0.660 on the same clean items, ranges overlap), so on this anchor the reader is not worse than Clef or Gemma. All of them sit near 0.64, so this anchor cannot separate them and the shared ceiling comes from the mapping, the taxonomy or the shared view, not from reader size. Limits: lenient sets accept up to three categories per topic; mapping written by us; MN-DS is 2019 text with a different taxonomy; the licence line of the mirror is cc only.

T32 ROUND 1 PRE-REGISTRATION (before any rater runs the new text): presence definition v4a = frozen v3b guideline plus ONE edit inside the conditions rule, in specs/world_state_v4a_presence_timing.json: a change announced for a later date does not count, and a change still under way counts only for the part the item says has already happened. Basis: split items in runs/xtest/B1 are announced closings and events under way (ledger L698); MAVEN-FACT labels certain-to-have-happened separately from possible (arXiv 2407.15352). NOT changed this round: the scope question (single firm or outlet against a listed condition level), reported as an open check-1 gap. Test: same 600 items as B1 (runs/xtest/items600.jsonl), presence only, variant A, seed 0, raters Clef, Gemma, Qwen, local, 0 USD, paired with their B1 answers on the same items; Jev left out (hosted, cap). PREDICTION: (1) the spread of yes-rates across the three local raters shrinks from the B1 spread to within 10 points; (2) alpha over the three raters rises by at least 0.05 over their B1 alpha on the same items; (3) false-yes on the MAVEN-FACT negatives does not rise. Confirmation on fresh devq items only if (1) and (2) hold. Gate outcome applied after scoring per playbook 13.

T32 ROUND 1 SCORE (pre-registered L751; own computation with xtest/score.py alpha_nominal and boot_alpha, unweighted, 1000 resamples, from projects/world-state/runs/xtest/B1/runs/*_A_s0 and runs/xtest/B7/runs/*_A_s0, 597 paired items, Clef Gemma Qwen, 0 USD, B7 all 600 of 600 answered). Yes-rates old v3b: Clef 0.338, Gemma 0.156, Qwen 0.194, spread 0.182; new v4a: Clef 0.342, Gemma 0.154, Qwen 0.231, spread 0.188. Alpha over the three raters: old 0.580 (0.519 to 0.643), new 0.590 (0.527 to 0.652). Raters changed their answer on 26, 23 and 30 items, nearly symmetric for Clef and Gemma (yes to no 12 and 12, no to yes 14 and 11) and one-directional upward for Qwen (4 down, 26 up). PREDICTIONS: (1) spread within 10 points FAILED (0.188); (2) alpha up at least 0.05 FAILED (up 0.010, ranges overlap almost fully); (3) false-yes on the MAVEN-FACT negatives not rising: NOT TESTED this round (needs a rerun of B5 under v4a). READING: the timing lines did not move the strictness spread; the answer changes look like rewording noise, not a systematic shift. The spread looks like a stable disposition of each model, not a gap in the timing wording. Gate: round 1 of 2 used, outcome REVISE (playbook 13). Check 2 (reliable) fails on the pre-set line (lower end 0.527 against 0.667, spread 0.188 against 0.10). Round 2 candidate: require words in the item that state the change has already happened (check 5), same typed structure for every rater; or accept the spread and handle it by routing and per-rater calibration against an anchor (T27).
T32 step 3 done

T32 ROUND 2 PRE-REGISTRATION (1-3-1 pick: MM3-0604, memo projects/world-state/specs/presence_round2_options.md, Option A chosen at p 0.95, consensus STRONG, escalate false). Change control: the v4a timing lines are REVERTED (no gain, L752); round 2 = frozen v3b plus ONE edit, specs/world_state_v4b_presence_evidence.json: you may answer yes only if words in the item itself state that the change has already happened (check 5, playbook 13). Test: one combined bundle B8, 600 items from B1 plus the 952 MAVEN-FACT items of T29 (1552 tasks), presence, variant A, seed 0, Clef Gemma Qwen local, 0 USD. PREDICTIONS: (1) spread of yes-rates over the three raters on the 597 paired B1 items within 0.10; (2) alpha over the three up at least 0.05 over the v3b value 0.580 (L752), so at least 0.630; (3) false-yes on the 473 to 476 MAVEN-FACT negatives stays under 0.10 per rater and does not rise more than 0.02 over L730 (Clef 0.047, Gemma 0.002, Qwen 0.004). If (1) or (2) fail: revert the line, round 2 of 2 is used, outcome by the gate rule is PARK unless Option B (per-rater calibration with routing, T27) is taken, tried in that order.

T28 STEP 2 (v2 crosswalk): an EMPIRICAL crosswalk derived from the dev sample (items where Clef and Gemma agree; script projects/world-state/derive_map_v2.py) was built, inspected and REJECTED: it changes 17 topics and accepts categories such as labour_disputes to health and food_agriculture to lifestyle and health, i.e. it blesses rater confusions on small counts and would inflate scores; file kept as specs/topic_to_iptc_v2_empirical_REJECTED.json, not to be used. PRINCIPLED v2 = the a-priori v1 mapping unchanged, plus a scoring rule: gold human interest has no topic of ours by design (IPTC catch-all) and is excluded and reported separately. FRESH SAMPLE: data/anchors/mn_ds/items_T28b.jsonl, 1600 articles, 100 for each of the 16 other first-level categories, seed 20261105, drawn from rows not in the first sample and with a unique data_id, item ids keyed mn2:rowposition:data_id. PRE-REGISTRATION: (1) v6b-student top-2 lenient lower end of the 95 percent range at least 0.80 on the fresh sample (the Ready line, mapping v1, human interest excluded); (2) Clef top-1 lenient point estimate within 0.05 of 0.70, the post hoc value without human interest on the dev sample (L748 reading), as a reproducibility check; (3) best constant guess reported on the same items. A miss on (1) is a recorded result against the 0.80 line, not a reason to change the mapping.

T28 FRESH SAMPLE v6b-student SCORE (pre-registered L755; runs/pulse/anchor_mnds_fresh_v6b-student.json, items data/anchors/mn_ds/items_T28b.jsonl, 1600 articles, 16 categories without human interest, mapping v1, CPU one thread, 15.5 ms p50 and 17.0 ms p95, 0 USD): top-2 lenient 1279 of 1600 = 0.799 (0.779 to 0.818); top-1 lenient 1081 = 0.676 (0.652 to 0.698); top-1 strict 0.454; unknown share 0.0. Best constant guess on the same items: single 0.188, best pair 0.375 (own count). PREDICTION (1) top-2 lower end at least 0.80: MISSED, 0.779, the point estimate sits on the line (0.799) and the range straddles it; recorded as a result against the 0.80 line, mapping unchanged as pre-registered. Top-2 beats the best constant pair by 0.424. Dev sample top-2 including human interest was 0.773 (0.752 to 0.792), L750, so excluding human interest and drawing fresh articles moved the point estimate up by 0.026. Prediction (2) Clef top-1 reproducibility on the fresh sample is still to run (Clef is paused while the round 2 chain uses the GPU).

T32 ROUND 2 SCORE (pre-registered L754; scorer projects/world-state/score_t32_round.py, bundle runs/xtest/B8 against B1, 593 paired items, Clef Gemma Qwen, 0 USD, Qwen took 1061 s). Wording v4b (yes only if words in the item state the change has already happened): yes-rates Clef 0.314, Gemma 0.118, Qwen 0.199, spread 0.196 against 0.182 under v3b; alpha 0.553 (0.491 to 0.615) against 0.580 (0.519 to 0.641). False-yes on the MAVEN-FACT negatives: Clef 20 of 475 = 0.042 (0.027 to 0.064), Gemma 0 of 476 (0.000 to 0.008), Qwen 2 of 476 = 0.004 (0.001 to 0.015), all under 0.10 and not up. PREDICTIONS: (1) spread within 0.10 FAILED (0.196); (2) alpha up at least 0.05 FAILED (down 0.027); (3) false-yes held. Two wording rounds (L752, L754) left the strictness spread unchanged, so the spread is a property of each model and not a gap in our wording. GATE (playbook 13, lean/FieldGate.lean): check 2 failed after two REVISE rounds, so the rule gives PARK for presence as a single yes-no reader field; the evidence line is reverted (change control). Option B (per-rater handling with routing and soft targets, T27) stays as the follow-on and is tried as research, not as a blocker for the other Pulse fields. T32 engine card: BitMob Expert 1 v5-leaf

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

layers.asks: Pick something from the Pulse, such as a capability, and see what drives it, depends on it and is affected by it. Pilot done (L384): tags can be proposed on the CPU and verified by Clef, but agreement is only moderate, so the design is a hybrid.

fields.what: Find entities, places, concepts and capabilities in the item and link each to one stable identity. Pilot: about 5 tags per full article, 3 per headline item; reading the whole article adds 56% new tags.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.
next.ask: adopt v6b-student (sealed check first) · capability sources · tags at serving

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: waiting for your yes (v5-leaf unchanged)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.title: Real conditions: counts
changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

changes.title: Traits: first results
changes.text: Sonnet graded 2,650 items on 51 questions (agrees with itself 87% on active answers). On the CPU reader, 24 of 51 questions work as present/absent flags; a 4B reader adds only a little (30 of 51). Next: build the flags into the engine, or label more graded examples.

fitness.name: Field checks v2
fitness.rule: Consensus verdict uses ONLY the sourced agreement score bands (Krippendorff 2004, p.241): 0.80 or more clear, 0.667 to 0.80 tentative, under 0.667 reject. Our own measures are flags and never decide.

measures.q: Do labellers agree beyond chance?
measures.m: Krippendorff's alpha: agreement beyond chance (1 = perfect, 0 = no better than guessing)

measures.q: Does agreement hold when a model from a different maker (Qwen3-14B) votes with Sonnet and Haiku?
measures.m: alpha over Sonnet, Haiku (one maker) and Qwen on the 395 items
measures.bar: same bands as the agreement score; a flag only, it does not change the verdict

measures.q: Does each answer agree, the rare ones too?
Do Sonnet and Haiku agree, not just each with itself? Same maker, so this is not an independent check.
How many items have no 3-of-4 majority?
measures.bar: ours: 10% or less ok · over 20% fail

measures.q: Does one model repeat itself?
measures.cite: none found (stability is not correctness: arXiv 2609.15194)

fit_tests.m: the Agreement score above

fit_tests.cite: LESSONS #8 (our notes); Graham & Bull 1998 uses 200+ for intervals

fit_tests.bar: none = agreement only: the field can never be called correct

text: T31 engine card: BitMob Expert 1 v6b-student

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

changes.title: Adopted v6b-student
changes.text: Sealed set scored once (1,499 items, 2.19 USD hosted): story 91.5%, topic two guesses 92.2%, real conditions found 29.3%, all better than v5-leaf (87.1%, 90.1%, 22.0%). Ledger L771.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: waiting for your yes (v5-leaf unchanged)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring

text: T31 engine card: BitMob Expert 1 v6b-student

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

layers.name: Area (drill into one thing)

fields.label: Consolidated knowledge

fields.label: Agree, contradict, gap
fields.what: Check each new item against what we know and flag what is new or missing

fields.label: Claim, evidence, source
fields.what: Every statement traced to the source text it came from; the raw documents stay but are not the focus

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.
next.ask: adopt v6b-student (sealed check first) · capability sources · tags at serving

tried_groups.name: Swapping the trunk (Granite small R2)
tried_groups.summary: Ties with bge-small on every Pulse field (short items). On whole articles a bigger window beats truncating at 512, but chunking bge-small beats one long Granite pass and costs far less CPU. Plan for long articles: bge-small chunks feeding tag-level joins.

items.what: ibm-granite/granite-embedding-small-english-r2 as the shared encoder (47.7M, Apache-2.0, 8k, ModernBERT), same heads and items
items.result: Topic top-2 0.881 vs 0.877, which-condition 0.875 vs 0.863, all inside the noise; encoder alone 23 ms; engine p95 44.5 ms vs 36.2; memory 837 MB vs 732
items.outcome: bge-small stays; revisit when Area needs token-level heads

items.what: Long-term features: joining quality and long-input cost, Granite vs bge-small
items.result: Neighbour topic agreement 0.634 vs 0.648; cluster agreement (NMI) 0.383 vs 0.408; 8,192 tokens 22 s vs about 3.9 s chunked
items.outcome: Granite not ahead; one test left (token-level tagging head, needs the Area tag labels)

items.what: Whole-article test: can a passage from the late part find its article? (1,500 long articles, median 1,078 tokens)
items.result: bge truncated 0.50; Granite whole article 0.64; bge chunked mean 0.77; bge best chunk 0.87 (recall@1, late passages)
items.outcome: Owner's logic holds (bigger window beats truncation); chunking a small model wins

tried_groups.name: Bigger or tuned neural models
tried_groups.summary: Fine-tuning, int8 and distilling the encoder were not better, or not fast enough.

items.what: Fine-tuning the encoder
items.result: First try much worse (topic top-2 0.726); corrected try +0.014 on topic but worse on which-condition
items.outcome: Rejected: frozen features beat it

items.what: int8 encoder to make it fast enough
items.result: Topic top-2 drops 0.019 against a 0.01 limit
items.outcome: Rejected; cascade instead

items.what: Distilling the encoder into static vectors
items.result: Keeps none of the encoder's lift (topic top-2 0.813 vs 0.832)
items.outcome: Rejected

tried_groups.name: Outside language models (d1, LFM3)
tried_groups.summary: d1 is a strong second opinion (topic 0.926 when combined) but needs the GPU and its licence does not fit. LFM3 is unusable.

items.what: d1-2B decision model, zero-shot, on the GPU
items.result: Alone: topic top-2 0.852. Fused with our student: topic top-2 0.926, condition top-1 0.834
items.outcome: Pipeline test only: GPU, and a licence the owner called not commercially viable

items.what: LFM3-1.7B as a JSON reader
items.result: Only 28% valid JSON; as a yes/no scorer AUC 0.54 to 0.61
items.outcome: Rejected

tried_groups.name: Teaching tricks
tried_groups.summary: Training our student on d1's soft labels gave no gain.

items.what: Training the student on d1's soft labels
items.result: Topic top-2 -0.008, story -0.006, which-condition +0.009 to +0.02
items.outcome: No gain; d1 stays a live second opinion

tried_groups.name: Free-form tags (pilot: 100 articles, 100 headline items)
tried_groups.summary: CPU proposes, Clef verifies: about 3 tags per headline item, 5.4 per full article; wording agreement about 0.5; 77% of tags occur once. Capabilities are 7% of general-news tags and 23% of tech-news tags, and almost never recur across articles: news can propose capability candidates but cannot supply the capability layer. Design: a hybrid.

items.what: Tag pilot with spaCy proposer and local Clef verifier (5 narrow yes/no questions per candidate)
items.result: 41% of 2,762 candidates accepted; kappa 0.49 to 0.53; merge at cosine 0.80 cuts distinct tags by 33% but merges related, not only identical, tags; 56% of full-article tags are absent from the short version
items.outcome: Hybrid design; capability layer needs tech sources; a token-level tag head is the serving route (the proposer takes 0.7 s per item)

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

DOC 00 REVIEW, EVIDENCE TEST 1 (playbook/00-knowledge-pipeline-v1.md section 13 and test T07: syndicated copies must not sit in both training and test). PRE-REGISTRATION: projects/world-state/leakage_check.py compares each of the 1500 sealed and 2000 DEVQ items against the 46775 training pool texts (data/pool_train.jsonl) and against each other, near-duplicate = Jaccard of word 4-gram shingles at least 0.8, or equal headline. PREDICTION (under 2 percent each) HELD. Largest possible shift of the sealed scores of L771: 12 of 1499 = 0.8 points, so they stand; flagged ids kept in the file. EVIDENCE TEST 2 PRE-REGISTRATION (doc section 4: calibrated acceptance per head and abstention): projects/world-state/selective_check.py takes the v6b-student confidence for story type and for the two topic guesses, picks the lowest cutoff on DEVQ (1997 Sonnet labelled items) at which agreement among accepted items reaches 0.95, and applies that cutoff ONCE to the sealed set (1499) and to the fresh MN-DS articles (1600, topic two guesses against human labels, mapping v1). Also reports expected calibration error on DEVQ and sealed. PREDICTION: story type reaches 0.95 on DEVQ at coverage of at least 0.60, and on sealed the accepted share agrees at least 0.93; topic two guesses reaches 0.95 at coverage of at least 0.70, sealed accepted agreement at least 0.93; against human labels on MN-DS the accepted topic share is higher than the unfiltered 0.799 but below 0.95. No cutoff is chosen on sealed or MN-DS.

DOC 00 REVIEW, EVIDENCE TEST 2 RESULT (runs/pulse/selective_check.json, selective_check.py; cutoff from DEVQ only, applied once to sealed and MN-DS fresh). Story type: cutoff gives agreement 0.950 (0.939 to 0.959) at coverage 0.926 on DEVQ and 0.950 (0.937 to 0.960) at coverage 0.921 on sealed, against 0.919 and 0.916 unfiltered; calibration error 0.046 on both. Topic two guesses: cutoff 0.642 gives 0.950 at coverage 0.873 on DEVQ and 0.955 (0.942 to 0.965) at coverage 0.870 on sealed, against 0.915 and 0.922 unfiltered; calibration error 0.098 DEVQ and 0.093 sealed (the topic confidence is poorly calibrated). Against human labels (MN-DS fresh, mapping v1) the accepted 85.1 percent of articles agree 0.831 (0.810 to 0.850), against 0.799 for all. PREDICTIONS: all five HELD. READING under the Ready rule of L492 (a skipped item counts as a miss): abstention lowers the end to end rate (sealed topic 0.870 x 0.955 = 0.831 against 0.922 unfiltered; MN-DS 0.851 x 0.831 = 0.707), so it does not change any Ready verdict; what it adds is a CONFIDENT TIER the consumer can trust at 0.95 for about 87 to 92 percent of items, the same idea as the condition tiers of L486. DOC 00 REVIEW SUMMARY (playbook/00-knowledge-pipeline-v1.md, unchanged): it is a design for a larger system; Pulse maps to its G3 classification gate (heads Domain, Area, content function, conditions). Tools in it that our evidence reaches: (1) leakage check by group, tested, passes; (2) calibrated abstention, tested, gives a 0.95 tier, topic needs recalibration; (3) FACTUALITY as a separate label (Asserted, Reported, Planned, Predicted, Denied) on each fragment: our presence split items were announced and in progress events (L698) and MAVEN-FACT has human factuality labels, so presence can be split into a part with an outside anchor (did it happen) and a part without (is it a listed condition); not yet tested; (4) ADWIN style drift monitoring for per field agreement without halting, a gap noted at T27; (5) content function as multilabel instead of one story type, since opinion 0.61 and unclear 0.52 agree least (L744 era, Fit card), not yet tested. Out of scope for Pulse: Rust extractor and 1 ms scan, knowledge graph, ontology evolution, tenant isolation, answer engine.

title: Factuality head for presence (doc 00 fragments)
text: Factuality head for presence (doc 00 fragments)
why: Doc 00 splits an event from its factuality. Presence disagreements were announced and in-progress events (L698); MAVEN-FACT labels factuality by humans, so half of presence has an outside anchor.
acceptance: Factuality question scored two-sided against MAVEN-FACT human labels with n and 95 percent ranges per rater; alpha across raters compared with the combined presence alpha 0.580 (L752).
steps: Pre-register; ask the happened question on 952 MAVEN items
Score two-sided vs MAVEN-FACT gold, three local raters

text: T33 started

T33 PRE-REGISTRATION. HYPOTHESES: H1 the rater disagreement on presence (alpha 0.580, yes-rate spread 0.182, L752) comes from the factuality part (did the change already happen); H2 it comes from the scope part (is it one of the 38 listed conditions). TEST: a new question in xtest/bundle.py, additive (field happened, yes or no, variants A and P): does this item state that at least one event has already taken place; yes = the item states a completed or in effect event, no = announced, planned, predicted, possible, denied or only proposed. Items: runs/xtest/items_T32r2.jsonl, 1552 = the 600 news items of B1 plus the 952 MAVEN-FACT sentences of T29. Raters Clef, Gemma, Qwen, local, 0 USD, seed 0, frozen v3b intro. MAVEN gold (data/anchors/maven_fact/gold_T29.json): yes = a sentence with at least one CT+ event (476), no = none (476); this is the happened concept of lean/MavenFactFit.lean (hasCertainEvent), scored two sided. PREDICTIONS: (1) every rater balanced accuracy on the MAVEN sentences at least 0.90; (2) on the 597 paired news items alpha over the three raters for happened at least 0.68 (presence alpha 0.580 plus 0.10) and the spread of yes-rates at most 0.10. READING RULE: (2) holds means H1 is supported and presence should be rebuilt as happened AND listed-condition with the first part anchored; (2) fails means the disagreement lives in the scope part (H2) and the next test is a scope question against the 38 condition definitions. Scope part has no outside anchor either way.

T33 ROUND 1 SCORE (pre-registered L785; runs/xtest/B10/score_t33.json from projects/world-state/score_t33.py; 1552 items, Clef Gemma Qwen, 0 USD). Question: does this item state that at least one event has already taken place. MAVEN-FACT two sided, yes recall and no recall: Clef 344 of 476 (0.723) and 313 of 476 (0.658), balanced 0.690; Gemma 471 of 476 (0.989) and 36 of 476 (0.076), balanced 0.533; Qwen 453 of 476 (0.952) and 158 of 476 (0.332), balanced 0.642. News items (597 paired): happened yes-rates Clef 0.663, Gemma 0.982, Qwen 0.953, spread 0.319, alpha 0.072 (0.010 to 0.144) against presence 0.580. Consistency: presence yes but happened no on 23 of 202 for Clef and 0 for Gemma and Qwen. PREDICTIONS: (1) balanced accuracy at least 0.90 for every rater FAILED; (2) alpha at least 0.68 and spread at most 0.10 FAILED. READING: my design error, not evidence about H1 or H2: at least one event is true of almost any news text (a statement or an announcement is itself an event), and the gold marks one specific annotated event, so the question did not measure the concept the gold labels; by playbook 13 check 1 this question was not definable as written. Doc 00 puts factuality on a fragment with a predicate span, not on the whole item. H1 versus H2 is NOT decided by this round. ROUND 2: per-event question with the trigger word marked, two sided against MAVEN-FACT per-event human labels.

Question per event: in this item, has the event marked between « and » already taken place; yes or no, new field eventhappened in xtest/bundle.py (additive, 9 xtest tests still pass), frozen v3b intro. Items data/anchors/maven_fact/items_T33b.jsonl: 1818 marked events from the HUMAN annotated MAVEN-FACT validation file only (no model assisted labels): 909 not CT+ (CT- 384, PS+ 453, PS- 52, Uu 20) plus 909 random CT+, trigger tokens marked from the token offsets, sentences up to 600 characters; gold gold_T33b.json. READING RULE: both hold: factuality of a marked event is extractable and has an outside anchor, so presence can be rebuilt as listed-condition AND happened-event with the first part anchored, and the open question is the scope part; either fails: factuality itself is a hard sub-field and the gate result for presence stands for a deeper reason. title: Serve the CPU reader: wire v6b-student into a service
text: Serve the CPU reader: wire v6b-student into a service

T31 engine card: BitMob Expert 1 v6b-student

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

changes.title: Adopted v6b-student after one sealed-set scoring
changes.text: Sealed set scored once (1,499 items, 2.19 USD hosted): story 91.5%, topic two guesses 92.2%, real conditions found 29.3%, all better than v5-leaf (87.1%, 90.1%, 22.0%). Ledger L771.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: ADOPTED 2026-11-04 (was waiting for your yes)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

fitness.rule: Consensus verdict uses ONLY the sourced agreement score bands (Krippendorff 2004, p.241): 0.80 or more clear, 0.667 to 0.80 tentative, under 0.667 reject. Our own measures are flags and never decide.

measures.q: Do labellers agree beyond chance?

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).

Sonnet and Haiku come from one maker and share habits, so they count as one source; Qwen3-14B is the first independent maker (measured: same-maker agreement is higher than cross-maker on every field, L572).
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.

Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).

T33 ROUND 2 SCORE (pre-registered L788; runs/xtest/B11/score_t33b.json from projects/world-state/score_t33b.py; 1818 marked MAVEN-FACT validation events, 909 happened (CT+) and 909 not, human labels; Clef Gemma Qwen, 0 USD, no failures). Right when it happened: Clef 785 of 909 (0.864), Gemma 864 (0.950), Qwen 830 (0.913). Right when it did NOT happen: Clef 336 of 909 (0.370), Gemma 193 (0.212), Qwen 578 (0.636); by class Gemma CT- 54 of 384 (0.14), PS+ 128 of 453 (0.28); Qwen CT- 250 (0.65), PS+ 283 (0.62), PS- 40 of 52, Uu 5 of 20. Balanced accuracy Clef 0.617, Gemma 0.581, Qwen 0.774; majority vote of the three 0.643; alpha over the three 0.445 (0.409 to 0.479), all three agree on 0.689 of events. PREDICTIONS: (1) every rater balanced accuracy at least 0.85 FAILED; (2) alpha at least 0.70 FAILED. READING: factuality of a marked event is poorly judged zero shot by these three readers: they say it happened for most events and fail to say no for denied, planned or possible ones; the alpha of 0.445 is LOWER than combined presence (0.580, L752), so the disagreement does live at least partly in the factuality part (H1 supported in that sense, not decided against H2); the human labels the anchor provides are the way to train this part. Doc 00 puts factuality on a fragment: a supervised head is its route, not a better prompt. NEXT: feasibility of a small supervised factuality head on the human labelled validation events only (document grouped cross validation), internal research, no use of the train file whose licence and model assisted labels are unresolved.
T33 step 2 done

T33 STEP 3 PRE-REGISTRATION: supervised factuality head feasibility, projects/world-state/factuality_head_cv.py. Data: the 1818 marked human labelled validation events of T33 round 2 only (data/anchors/maven_fact/items_T33b.jsonl, gold_T33b.json), label happened = CT+. Features: the base leaf encoder embedding of the marked sentence (expert1_v5_leaf artefact, CPU), nothing else; classifier: balanced logistic regression, fixed C=1, no tuning; 5-fold cross validation GROUPED BY DOCUMENT so no sentence of a test document is seen in training. Internal feasibility research on CPU, 0 USD; the train file is not used (licence and model assisted labels unresolved). PREDICTION: pooled out-of-fold balanced accuracy between 0.70 and 0.85, above the best zero-shot reader on the same items (Qwen 0.774)? NO, expected at or below it; the question is whether a trained head on 1.8k examples gets near or above 0.85. PASS LINE: balanced accuracy at least 0.85 with the lower end of the 95 percent range at least 0.82. READING: pass means a CPU factuality head is feasible from human labels (anchored extractor without AI at serving); 0.70 to 0.85 means feasible only with more labels or a token-level feature (the train file, 70k events, after the licence is settled); below 0.70 means the encoder embedding alone does not carry the marked-event factuality.

T33 STEP 3 RESULT (pre-registered L805; runs/xtest/B11/factuality_head_cv.json, factuality_head_cv.py; 1818 human labelled validation events, 576 documents, 5 fold document grouped CV, base leaf embedding plus balanced logistic regression, CPU, 0 USD): recall happened 683 of 909 (0.751), recall not happened 619 of 909 (0.681), balanced accuracy 0.716 (0.696 to 0.737); by class CT+ 0.75, PS+ 0.59, CT- 0.77, PS- 0.90 (47 of 52), Uu 0.40 (8 of 20). Pass line 0.85 MISSED; prediction band 0.70 to 0.85 HELD. Above Clef 0.617 and Gemma 0.581 zero shot, below Qwen 0.774 zero shot on the same items. CHANGE-CONTROL ROUND 2 (one change): add sparse features of the words within 4 tokens either side of the marked trigger (word 1 and 2 grams, trigger replaced by a marker), the doc 00 predicate window idea; everything else identical. PREDICTION: balanced accuracy at least 0.78 and lower end of the range above 0.74; pass line unchanged at 0.85 with lower end 0.82. If it misses 0.78 the embedding plus window route is closed at this label count and the next lever is the 70k train events after the licence is settled by the owner.
T33 step 3 done
Factuality tested on CPU raters (alpha 0.445, balanced 0.58 to 0.77) and a supervised head (0.804); H1 supported, path recorded

T33 STEP 3 ROUND 2 RESULT (pre-registered L806; runs/xtest/B11/factuality_head_cv_window.json, factuality_head_cv.py with WINDOW=4; the no-window baseline reproduced 0.716 in the same run): adding word 1 and 2 grams of the 4 tokens either side of the marked trigger gives balanced accuracy 0.804 (0.786 to 0.822), recall happened 757 of 909 (0.833), recall not happened 705 of 909 (0.776); by class CT+ 0.83, PS+ 0.74, CT- 0.84, PS- 0.92 (48 of 52), Uu 0.15 (3 of 20). PREDICTION at least 0.78 with lower end above 0.74: HELD; pass line 0.85 with lower end 0.82: MISSED. A CPU head trained on 1818 human labelled events beats the best zero shot reader (Qwen 0.774) and Clef and Gemma (0.617, 0.581). CONCLUSIONS: (1) factuality of a marked event IS extractable on CPU from human labels without AI at serving, and has an outside anchor; (2) it needs the trigger: a free text item has no marked trigger, so presence from this route needs an event detector first (doc 00 G2 solver) and a listed-condition head, whose scope part has no outside anchor; (3) next lever for the head is more human labels: the 70k event train file of MAVEN-FACT, which has an unstated licence and GPT-3.5 pre-annotation, OWNER DECISION: may it be used for training (internal research) or only for scoring; (4) Uu stays weak (20 examples). Presence stays parked (L758); this is the research path from it, not a verdict change.

T30 ANCHOR FOUND AND PRE-REGISTRATION: CLEF 2025 CheckThat! Task 1 subjectivity, English, Hugging Face mirror AIWizards/clef2025_checkthat_task1_subjectivity, licence stated in the card and shipped as legal text: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial, share alike): INTERNAL SCORING ONLY, no training, no redistribution, folder data/anchors/checkthat_subj (git-ignored). 2076 labelled English sentences (train 830, dev 462, dev_test 484, test 300; OBJ 1331, SUBJ 745), annotator alpha 0.83 per the 2023 overview paper. Construct: objective versus subjective at SENTENCE level, which is not our four story types and not headline plus teaser. MAPPING (fixed now): primary SUBJ means v6b-student story type is opinion; secondary SUBJ means opinion or unclear; OBJ otherwise. Raters: v6b-student (CPU) and Clef. PREDICTIONS: OBJ recall at least 0.85; SUBJ recall between 0.20 and 0.60 (our opinion class is narrower than subjective: loaded wording is subjective but not an opinion); balanced accuracy between 0.58 and 0.75. READING: a balanced accuracy lower end of at least 0.70 means the fact versus opinion boundary has outside support; below that is expected because subjectivity is a wider construct, so a miss is reported as a construct gap and not as a failure of story type; forecast and unclear stay without an anchor.

T30 CHECKTHAT SCORE (pre-registered L810; runs/pulse/anchor_checkthat_v6b-student.json, score_checkthat.py; Clef via runs/xtest/B12; 2076 English sentences, internal scoring only, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). Primary mapping SUBJ means opinion: v6b-student subjective recall 468 of 745 (0.628), objective recall 985 of 1331 (0.740), balanced accuracy 0.684 (0.663 to 0.705); Clef 443 of 745 (0.595) and 997 of 1331 (0.749), balanced 0.672 (0.651 to 0.693). PREDICTIONS: objective recall at least 0.85 FAILED (0.740); subjective recall 0.20 to 0.60 narrowly MISSED for v6b-student (0.628) and held for Clef (0.595); balanced accuracy 0.58 to 0.75 HELD for both. Lower end 0.70 not reached by either, so the fact versus opinion boundary has only partial outside support; both readers behave alike (26 percent of objective sentences called opinion by v6b-student, 346 of 1331), so the ceiling here comes from the construct (subjective is wider than opinion) and the domain (sentences, opinion heavy sources), not from reader size. STEP 2 PRE-REGISTRATION, own checkable test for forecast (one sided, it can refute a forecast call and never confirm one, as in lean/MavenFactFit.lean): projects/world-state/forecast_cue_test.py counts, among the sealed items v6b-student calls forecast, the share whose text holds a future cue (will, would, expected to, forecast, projected, predicts, likely to, set to, plans to, poised to, could, may, might, a year in the future, next year or month or week, in the coming, outlook). PREDICTION: at least 0.90 of v6b-student forecast calls hold a cue; Sonnet forecast labels of the same items hold a cue at least 0.90 too; the share of cue-free forecast calls is listed in full.

T30 STEP 2 RESULT (pre-registered L811; runs/pulse/forecast_cue_test.json, forecast_cue_test.py; sealed items): v6b-student calls forecast on 36 of 1499 items, 30 hold a future cue (0.833); Sonnet labels forecast on 39 items, 34 hold a cue (0.872); 0.214 of all items hold a cue. PREDICTION (both at least 0.90) FAILED. Of the 6 cue free v6b-student calls, 4 read as real forecasts (a matchday preview, likely over most parts of India, a forecaster warning, storms looming and possible) that the word list lacks, 2 are unclear; the lexical cue list is too narrow to validate and was NOT widened afterwards to rescue the number. FINDINGS FOR STORY TYPE: fact versus opinion has partial outside support (CheckThat balanced 0.684 for v6b-student and 0.672 for Clef, both under the 0.70 line); forecast and unclear are rare (computed Sonnet shares on the sealed set 0.026 and 0.023) so playbook 13 check 3 (enough real cases) is not met for them and no anchor exists; story type is Ready overall by the Ready rule (L771) but forecast and unclear are NOT individually validated. T30 closes with that limit stated; a forecast anchor would need positive hunting plus a licensed source.

T39 PRE-REGISTRATION (topic confidence recalibration; engine NOT changed, a calibration map is produced and scored, wiring it in is an engine change for later). Method: isotonic regression from the v6b-student topic two guess confidence to hit or miss, fitted on DEVQ only (1997 Sonnet labelled items), applied once to sealed (1499); expected calibration error with 10 equal width bins, measured before and after. Script projects/world-state/calibrate_topic.py, map saved to runs/pulse/topic_calibration.json. PREDICTION: calibration error falls from 0.098 on DEVQ and 0.093 on sealed (L782) to under 0.05 on sealed; the accepted share at the DEVQ 0.95 cutoff changes by less than 0.03 coverage. If sealed stays at 0.05 or more the topic confidence stays flagged.

T39 RESULT (pre-registered L823; runs/pulse/topic_calibration.json, projects/world-state/calibrate_topic.py; isotonic map fitted on DEVQ only; engine NOT changed). Against Sonnet agreement: calibration error on sealed 0.093 before and 0.013 after (target under 0.05: HELD; DEVQ is in sample so its 0.0 is not evidence); mean confidence 0.829 against hit rate 0.922 before, 0.920 after, i.e. the raw topic confidence is underconfident against Sonnet. Coverage change at the 0.95 cutoff was not measured; the map is monotone so the order of items is unchanged. SAME MAP AGAINST HUMAN LABELS (MN-DS fresh, 1600 articles, lenient hit): raw confidence mean 0.808 against hit rate 0.799, calibration error 0.073; calibrated to Sonnet mean 0.907, error 0.113. READING: the raw topic confidence is already close to honest against the human labels and the Sonnet calibrated one overstates them by about 0.11; a calibration target must follow the governing bar, and Sonnet agreement runs higher than the outside check on the same items (0.922 sealed against 0.799 MN-DS, different samples and an unequal taxonomy). RECOMMENDATION recorded as default, the owner can change it: report two numbers to consumers, agreement with the teacher (Ready rule L492, governs Ready) and the outside check (caveat, topic sits at the 0.80 line, point 0.799, low end 0.779); do NOT ship the Sonnet calibrated map as a confidence. Steps 1 and 2 done; step 3 (which bar governs, an owner decision) stays open.

T36 STEP 3 (playbook 13 checks 2 and 3 on all 51 traits; runs/pulse/traits_gate_provisional.json from projects/world-state/traits_gate_provisional.py; xtest B4 panel Clef Jev Gemma Qwen, 150 items, variant A seed 0, alpha with 500 bootstrap resamples). Check 2 = alpha lower end at least 0.667 and yes-rate spread at most 0.10; check 3 measurable = at least 10 items where a majority of raters say yes. RESULT: PASS on measured checks 2 of 51 (x025 deaths or injuries: alpha 0.930, lower end 0.808, spread 0.013, 13 majority-yes items; x034 single city or smaller area: alpha 0.806, lower end 0.713, spread 0.080, 34 items); REVISE on reliability 30 of 51; HUNT positives 19 of 51 (fewer than 10 majority-yes items in 150, so reliability is not measurable at this sample size). By group: movement 6 revise and 2 hunt; direction_effect 4 and 4; intent 6 and 2; risk 1 pass, 1 revise, 6 hunt; scale 1 pass, 5 revise; time 2 revise, 2 hunt; certainty 4 revise and 1 hunt. Yes-rate spread alone is at most 0.10 for 28 traits while alpha lower end reaches 0.667 for only 2: unlike presence, most trait disagreement is item by item and not a strictness gap, so a threshold fix will not help. Checks 1 (definable) and 5 (directly in the input) are not measured for any trait, so no trait is GO yet; the 2 are GO candidates. T36 STEP 4 PRE-REGISTRATION (positive hunting for the 19 HUNT traits of L830, listed in runs/pulse/traits_gate_provisional.json). Method: per trait a logistic regression on the leaf pool embeddings (runs/embeds/leaf_64_fp32.npy, 46543 items) trained on the 1500 Sonnet graded items of runs/pulse/traits_main/train (present = any grade above not at all), its AUC checked on the 1000 held-out graded items of traits_main/eval; the pool is ranked, items already graded or already in the 150 item B4 panel set are excluded; per trait 40 top ranked plus 40 random items (seed 20261106), 80 items per trait, one bundle B13, variant A wording of specs/traits_v0.json unchanged, Clef Gemma Qwen local 0 USD (Jev hosted and capped), a trait is asked only on its own 80 items. The enriched sample is for measuring reliability only, it is not representative of the stream. PREDICTIONS: (1) the ranker has AUC at least 0.80 on the held-out graded items for at least 15 of the 19; (2) after hunting at least 15 of the 19 traits have 10 or more majority-yes items (measurable); (3) among the measurable ones at least 3 reach alpha lower end 0.667 or more with yes-rate spread 0.10 or less. If (3) fails the reading is that most traits are not reliable across families even with enough positives, and the gate outcome for them is REVISE then PARK per playbook 13.

T36 STEP 4 DEVIATION AND RANKER RESULT, recorded AFTER the run (my deviation note was blocked by the note guard and the script ran in the same command, so the order promised in L832 was not kept; the metric change affects only how the ranker is scored, not which items were selected). The 1000 held out graded items of traits_main/eval are queue items with no row in the pool embedding file, so the held out AUC was not computable (first run: no evaluation positives, no AUC for all 19). Metric used instead: AUC from 5 fold cross validation on the 1500 graded training items. RESULT (runs/xtest/B13_selection.json, projects/world-state/traits_hunt.py): AUC at least 0.80 for 17 of the 19 HUNT traits; the two below: x041 at 0.794 and x050 at 0.686 (only 13 positives); range 0.686 to 0.963. PREDICTION (1) at least 15 of 19: HELD. Selected 40 top ranked plus 40 random pool items per trait, 80 per trait, excluding graded items and the B4 panel items. Predictions (2) and (3) are still to be scored after the panel run.

T36 STEP 4 RUN INCIDENT: my B13 bundle file lacked the instruction_sha256 and guideline_sha256 fields that xtest/run.py writes into the run card, so the Clef run ended with KeyError at the final step AFTER writing all 1520 answers (runs/xtest/B13/runs/clef_A_s0/results.jsonl has 1520 lines, run_card.json missing). Bundle patched while the Gemma server was loading and xtest/bundle_traits_hunt.py now emits both fields; Gemma's runner started seconds earlier and may hit the same error at its last step with its answers already written. The answers are complete either way; the run cards for any rater that hit the error are missing and are reported here as missing, not reconstructed.

T36 STEP 4 SCORE (pre-registered L832, scorer projects/world-state/traits_hunt_score.py checked by MM3-0605 and MM3-0606 before it was run: rules and selection and alpha questions all pass, one output question at 0.13 was settled by running the script, which prints the counts; output runs/pulse/traits_hunt_result.json; bundle B13, 19 traits, 80 items each, Clef Gemma Qwen, 1520 answers each, 0 USD; run cards missing for Clef and Gemma per L834). Measurable (10 or more majority yes items): 17 of 19. Reliable (alpha lower end 0.667 or more and yes-rate spread 0.10 or less) among the measurable: 9 of 17, namely x012 (alpha 0.896, lower end 0.796), x013 (0.899, 0.816), x016 (0.850, 0.750), x018 (0.842, 0.734), x024 (0.915, 0.838), x026 (0.835, 0.721), x027 (1.000, 1.000), x028 (0.867, 0.766), x031 (0.900, 0.813). REVISE on reliability 8: x005, x006, x011, x029, x032, x042, x046, x048. HUNT more 2: x041 (7 majority yes) and x050 (1). Hunting worked: majority yes items in the 40 top ranked arms total 515 of 760, in the 40 random arms 22 of 760. PREDICTIONS (2) at least 15 of 19 measurable: HELD (17); (3) at least 3 reliable among the measurable: HELD (9). COMBINED PICTURE OF 51 (L830 plus this): 11 pass the measured checks (x025 and x034 on the natural panel, the 9 above on enriched samples), 38 REVISE, 2 HUNT more. LIMITS, stated before anyone reads 11 as ready: (a) the 9 were scored on an ENRICHED sample whose positives are items a classifier trained on Sonnet labels ranked high, so they are prototypical cases and agreement is likely higher than on natural positives; random arm positive rate is 22 of 760 = 0.029, so a natural confirmation needs about 1000 items per trait to see 30 positives; (b) panel is 3 raters here against 4 in B4, not paired; (c) checks 1 definable and 5 directly in the input are not measured for any trait, so no trait is GO. NEXT: natural prevalence confirmation of the 11 candidates on one shared sample of about 1000 natural items, then the quoted-span test for check 5.
T36 step 4 done

T36 NATURAL CONFIRMATION PRE-REGISTRATION. Bundle B14 (xtest/bundle_traits_natural.py, checked by MM3-0607: sample questions 0.93, 0.95, 0.96; its leakage doubt 0.74 and wording doubt 0.57 settled by data: B14 items overlap B13 hunted items 0, B4 panel 0, pool_train 0, embedding ids 0; 11 traits, 8800 tasks): the 11 candidate traits (x025 x034 x012 x013 x016 x018 x024 x026 x027 x028 x031) on ONE shared random sample of 800 natural DEVQ queue items, seed 20261107, variant A wording unchanged, Clef then Gemma and Qwen as two separate local jobs each under 1 hour (Clef about 45 minutes), 0 USD. PREDICTIONS: (1) the two natural controls x025 and x034 reproduce their B4 reliability (alpha lower end at least 0.667); (2) of the 9 enriched passers at least 5 keep alpha lower end 0.667 or more with spread 0.10 or less on this natural sample, counting only traits with at least 10 majority yes items; (3) at least 3 of the 9 are not measurable at 800 items (fewer than 10 majority yes items), consistent with the random arm positive rate of 0.029 (L835); (4) among the measurable ones the mean alpha is at least 0.05 lower than on the enriched sample (prototypical cases agree more). READING: (2) holds means reliability survives natural prevalence for those traits and they move to the check 5 test; (2) fails means the enriched result was prototype driven and the traits go REVISE; traits with too few natural positives need a larger sample before any verdict.
T35 started

T35 STEP 1 (read only; files probes/world-engine/world_service2.py, probes/cpu_engine.py, service.yaml, demo/models.json). FINDINGS: (1) the World engine service asks its reader typed yes or no questions (328 per story) through any TypeSafe /v1/systemone endpoint; its /reader route accepts such an address (world_service2.py line 601); (2) service cpu_engine.py on port 8020 is that kind of endpoint: BitMob, e5-small int8 plus one learned head per typed question, router by area, CPU only; (3) v6b-student (class ExpertS in expert1_runtime.py) answers the Pulse fields directly (story type, two topic guesses, condition presence, which, direction, size) and has no typed question interface, so it does not plug into the reader slot as it is. DECISION RECORDED (my pick, 1-3-1 style, owner can change): add a thin new CPU service pulse_reader with one route /v1/pulse (text in, Pulse fields out) as its own entry in service.yaml and demo/models.json, instead of grafting Pulse onto cpu_engine.py, because the contracts differ (typed questions against fixed Pulse fields). SIZE OF THE JOB: the Registered rule (memory: registered means all surfaces) asks for the add-model skill end to end: install, adapter, service, fact sheet, measurement, leaderboard, demo pages; models are chosen by registry name and no ids or addresses in code or pages (tools/check_models.py). That is larger than the one line I estimated at L796; steps 2 and 3 of T35 stay as written and the acceptance (endpoint, equal answers on the 1499 sealed items, p95 under 50 ms) stands.
T35 step 1 done

T36 NATURAL CONFIRMATION SCORE (pre-registered L837; scorer projects/world-state/traits_natural_score.py checked by MM3-0608 before it was run: predictions 0.80, 0.95, 0.73, comparison 0.92, 0.97, 0.95, overclaim all at or under 0.08, consensus STRONG; output runs/pulse/traits_natural_result.json; bundle B14, 11 traits on 800 natural DEVQ items, Clef Gemma Qwen, 8800 answers each, Clef 6 failed answers, 0 USD). Alpha and lower end of the interval, enriched sample alpha in brackets: x025 0.835 (0.779) reliable [control]; x034 0.697 (0.652), spread 0.120, not reliable [control]; x013 0.802 (0.699) reliable [0.899]; x031 0.796 (0.691) reliable [0.900]; x012 0.756 (0.582) [0.896]; x024 0.732 (0.620) [0.915]; x026 0.739 (0.532) [0.835]; x028 0.657 (0.546) [0.867]; x018 0.618 (0.479) [0.842]; x016 0.519 (0.418) [0.850]; x027 0.561 (0.398) [1.000]. Majority yes items per trait 11 to 38 of 800 for the nine, 88 for x025, 201 for x034. PREDICTIONS: (1) both controls alpha lower end at least 0.667: FAILED (x034 0.652, spread 0.12); (2) at least 5 of the 9 enriched passers stay reliable: FAILED (2: x013 and x031); (3) at least 3 of the 9 not measurable at 800 items: FAILED (all 9 had 10 or more majority yes items, natural rates 0.014 to 0.048); (4) mean alpha drop from enriched to natural at least 0.05: HELD (0.203). READING per the rule written in L837: the enriched result was prototype driven. After the natural test 3 of 51 traits clear the reliability rule with outside-sample evidence (x025 deaths or injuries, x013 a cost grew for ordinary people, x031 a threat to the natural environment); x034 is borderline (lower end 0.652 here, 0.713 on the 4 rater panel); the other 8 hunted passers go REVISE. Checks 1 definable and 5 directly in the input are still not measured for any trait, so no trait is GO. Rater set differs (3 here, 4 in B4), not paired.

text: T40 started

T40 STEP 1 (gate check 1, definable, MM3 reading specs/traits_candidates_wording.md; MM3-0609 x025, MM3-0610 x013, MM3-0611 x031, MM3-0612 x034; the later three reused cached decision answers of MM3-0609, so their gap and reach lines repeat; the PASS LINE was not pre-registered, I use MM3 own goal gate as the reading and say so). x025 deaths or injuries: goal gate pass (p 0.86); ambiguity of a word 0.41, more than one thing at once 0.51 (deaths OR injuries), a yes needs the fact stated outright 0.38; borderline case left open 0.19; consensus SPLIT, escalate true, recorded and not resolved. x013 a cost grew for ordinary people: goal unsure (p 0.63); ambiguous word 0.46; answerable from text 0.77; stated outright 0.35; consensus STRONG. x031 threat to the natural environment: goal unsure (p 0.64); ambiguous word 0.40; answerable from text 0.84; stated outright 0.40; borderline case 0.38; consensus STRONG. x034 single city or smaller area: goal FAIL (p 0.24); threshold word without a rule 0.67; needs extra definition text 0.71; stated outright 0.21; consensus SPLIT, escalate true. READING: check 1 is established for x025 only; not established for x013 and x031 (unsure); fails for x034, which also had the weakest natural reliability (alpha lower end 0.652, spread 0.12, L841): by playbook 13 and lean/FieldGate.lean a failing check 1 means PARK, with a written definition as a new trait version being the way back in. For all four, the question whether a yes needs the fact stated outright scores low (0.21 to 0.40), which is the thing the check 5 span test measures next.
T40 step 1 done

T40 STEP 2 PRE-REGISTRATION (gate check 5, directly in the input). Test: for the positives (at least 2 of 3 raters said yes in the natural bundle B14) of x025 (88), x013 (28), x031 (25) and a seeded sample of 60 of x034 (201), Qwen (local) copies word for word the shortest part of the item that states the answer (projects/world-state/span_quotes.py); a quote counts only if it is an exact substring of the item and at most 40 words; all three raters then answer the same trait question on the quote alone (bundle B15, xtest/bundle_span.py) and on a same length random word window of the same item as control. PASS LINE (fixed now): directly in the input rate, i.e. positives with a valid quote AND 2 of 3 yes on the quote, divided by ALL positives, at least 0.90, and control majority yes rate at most 0.30. Scripts checked by MM3-0613: quote rules 0.97, 0.89, 0.95 and overclaim 0.02, 0.04, 0.09 pass; its denominator doubt (0.23 that the score divides by all positives) is a misreading settled by a planted fixture: 10 positives, 5 valid, 5 span yes, 2 control yes gives 0.5 and 0.4 and pass false as expected (score_t40_span.py with argument paths). PREDICTIONS: x025 reaches 0.90; x013 and x031 fall between 0.70 and 0.90 (loose words ordinary and threat, MM3-0610 and MM3-0611); x034 lowest and fails; control rate at most 0.30 for all. Local, 0 USD, Qwen quote step then Clef then Gemma and Qwen verification, voice and Clef paused and restored by the scripts, one wrapper under 1 hour.

T40 STEPS 2 AND 3. CHECK 5 SCORE (pre-registered L846; scorers checked by MM3-0613 and a planted fixture; runs/pulse/traits_check5_result.json; Qwen quotes, Clef Gemma Qwen answer on the quote alone, 398 tasks, 0 USD; invalid quotes 2 of 201: one answer 'The answer is no.' for x013 and the single word 'injuries' for x025). Directly in the input rate over ALL positives, control rate on a same length random window: x013 27 of 28 = 0.964, control 0.259 PASS; x025 81 of 88 = 0.920, control 0.149 PASS; x031 25 of 25 = 1.000, control 0.200 PASS; x034 48 of 60 = 0.800, control 0.333 FAIL. PREDICTIONS: x025 at least 0.90 HELD; x013 and x031 between 0.70 and 0.90 NOT HELD, both higher; x034 lowest and fails HELD; control at most 0.30 for all FAILED for x034 only (0.333). POST HOC ROBUSTNESS (not pre-registered, runs/pulse/traits_check5_robustness.json): Qwen both chose the quotes and is a judge; requiring Clef AND Gemma both yes on the quote gives x013 0.929, x031 0.880, x025 0.750, x034 0.667, with both-yes control rates 0.259, 0.120, 0.092, 0.017; Clef alone accepts only 0.761 of the x025 quotes. Read: the check is sensitive to the judge, x025 passes by the pre-registered majority rule and not by the stricter both-yes rule. GATE OUTCOMES (projects/world-state/traits_gate_outcomes.py, rule of lean/FieldGate.lean, four examples decided by Lean in lean/TraitsGate.lean): GO 1 = x025 deaths or injuries (c1 MM3-0609 pass, c2 natural alpha lower end 0.779, c3 88 majority yes of 800, c4 partial anchor via event types, c5 0.920); PARK 3 = x013 and x031 (c2 and c5 pass, c1 NOT established: MM3-0610 and MM3-0611 unsure, p 0.63 and 0.64; the pass line for c1 was not pre-registered, I used the MM3 goal gate) and x034 (c1 fail MM3-0612, c2 0.652, c5 0.800); HUNT 2 = x041, x050; REVISE provisional 45 (reliability fails on the latest sample; c1 and c5 not measured). x013 and x031 are the closest to GO: tightening their wording is a new trait version and the re-gate is cheap because reliability and the text check already pass.

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

changes.text: Sealed set scored once (1,499 items, 2.19 USD hosted): story 91.5%, topic two guesses 92.2%, real conditions found 29.3%, all better than v5-leaf (87.1%, 90.1%, 22.0%). Ledger L771.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: ADOPTED 2026-11-04 (was waiting for your yes)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.
