changes.title: Adopted v6b-student after one sealed-set scoring
changes.text: Sealed set scored once (1,499 items, 2.19 USD hosted): story 91.5%, topic two guesses 92.2%, real conditions found 29.3%, all better than v5-leaf (87.1%, 90.1%, 22.0%). Ledger L771.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: ADOPTED 2026-11-04 (was waiting for your yes)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.title: Real conditions: counts
changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

changes.title: Traits: first results
changes.text: Sonnet graded 2,650 items on 51 questions (agrees with itself 87% on active answers). On the CPU reader, 24 of 51 questions work as present/absent flags; a 4B reader adds only a little (30 of 51). Next: build the flags into the engine, or label more graded examples.

fitness.name: Field checks v2
fitness.rule: Consensus verdict uses ONLY the sourced agreement score bands (Krippendorff 2004, p.241): 0.80 or more clear, 0.667 to 0.80 tentative, under 0.667 reject. Our own measures are flags and never decide.

measures.q: Do labellers agree beyond chance?
measures.m: Krippendorff's alpha: agreement beyond chance (1 = perfect, 0 = no better than guessing)

measures.q: Does agreement hold when a model from a different maker (Qwen3-14B) votes with Sonnet and Haiku?
measures.m: alpha over Sonnet, Haiku (one maker) and Qwen on the 395 items
measures.bar: same bands as the agreement score; a flag only, it does not change the verdict

measures.q: Does each answer agree, the rare ones too?
Do Sonnet and Haiku agree, not just each with itself? Same maker, so this is not an independent check.
How many items have no 3-of-4 majority?
measures.bar: ours: 10% or less ok · over 20% fail

measures.q: Does one model repeat itself?
measures.cite: none found (stability is not correctness: arXiv 2609.15194)

fit_tests.q: Would careful readers give the same answer?
fit_tests.m: the Agreement score above
fit_tests.bar: same bands as agreement score

fit_tests.q: Does every answer have enough cases to learn and to score?
fit_tests.m: cases per answer on the 395 four-vote items (the full labelled pool is larger, with one voter)
fit_tests.bar: ours: 30+ per answer; under that the answer needs targeted data
fit_tests.cite: LESSONS #8 (our notes); Graham & Bull 1998 uses 200+ for intervals

fit_tests.q: Is there trusted outside labelled data?
fit_tests.m: named outside dataset for the field
fit_tests.bar: none = agreement only: the field can never be called correct
fit_tests.src: our design; datasets named in playbook 01

fit_tests.q: Does the headline plus description carry the evidence?
fit_tests.m: agreement between headline-only and full-article labels
fit_tests.bar: not measured yet

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).

Sonnet and Haiku come from one maker and share habits, so they count as one source; Qwen3-14B is the first independent maker (measured: same-maker agreement is higher than cross-maker on every field, L572).
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.
Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).
fitness.clef: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and with Haiku 63% on presence (a different question wording); on the 162 split items it matches majority 57%, so it cannot arbitrate them.

notes: Only items dated after the 2026-10-25 training cutoff are scored. The first run on all 395 items was contaminated (story type 98%) and was discarded.
86 items means wide ranges (story type v5-leaf 85 to 97%). This shows direction, not a verdict.
Set is 69% real conditions, so Condition present: right is judged against always-yes.

Pre-registration, T37 steps 3 and 4 pre-check (probe, not the final score). Question: do event features from the CPU trigger tagger (L874) and the MAVEN-trained happened head (L808) add information about Sonnet condition presence beyond the registered v6b-student presence score? Items: the 1997 devq items, Sonnet labels ws-v2-frozen (n_conditions above 0 is positive, 221 positives per L-end2end file), v6b-student score from runs/pulse/prod_presence_scores.npz. Method: 5 fold CV logistic regression, AUC and recall at the precision of always-no complement; features A = v6b score only, B = A plus event features (trigger count, happened count, max happened probability, happened share). Trigger and happened models are trained on MAVEN validation only and never see devq. Prediction: B beats A by at least 0.03 AUC (probability 0.4). A gain under 0.02 routes step 3 to a bigger encoder tagger or closes the event route as no help for recall (decided by Lean rule on the numbers).

Pre-registration, T37 narrow definition test (condition route 2). Idea: the union 'any of 38 conditions' mixes kinds the labellers agree on with kinds they do not; Sonnet and Haiku agree per kind at F1 0.6 to 0.77 for 16 kinds with at least 30 Sonnet positives (own count from runs/label_store/labels.jsonl, 18791 items labelled by both). Pass per kind: AUC at least 0.90 and F1 at least 0.50. Prediction: at least 5 of the 16 kinds pass (probability 0.5). Reading rule: 5 or more pass means the product contract can offer per-kind condition fields for the passing kinds (an output contract change, owner's word) and the union stays parked; fewer means the condition fields stay parked.

T30 AND T37 ANCHOR SEARCH FOR FOUR KINDS (report of a research fork with WebSearch, 4 searches and 1 page fetch; the URLs were not opened by me and no licence text was read, so everything below is unverified). civil_unrest: CASE 2021 Task 1 protest news with human labels (github emerging-welfare/case-2021-shared-task), data behind an application form, licence not stated; covers protest events only, not riots or strikes. cyber_insecurity: CybAttT, 36071 tweets with manual labels (Fleiss kappa 0.99), licence not shown, tweet text style; AnnoCTR CC-BY-SA is threat reports, weak fit. air_pollution: Samachar 17.4K India air pollution articles, no human labels found; none usable as a truth set. biodiversity_loss: CITES news filter study and PLANET4B documents, no released human labels seen. Result: no anchor that can be used today for any of the four kinds. Routing: the four kinds stay at agreement between two Claude labellers, and the page and contract must say so; the CASE form is a human step and is listed for the owner as optional.

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread. From 2026-11-05 the same reader also serves per-condition heads for four kinds (air pollution, biodiversity loss, civil unrest, cyber insecurity) and a direction head for biodiversity loss, on the same embedding, 16.6 ms median over HTTP (service pulse_reader, route /v1/pulse; nothing calls it yet).
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

changes.title: Adopted v6b-student after one sealed-set scoring
changes.text: Sealed set scored once (1,499 items, 2.19 USD hosted): story 91.5%, topic two guesses 92.2%, real conditions found 29.3%, all better than v5-leaf (87.1%, 90.1%, 22.0%). Ledger L771.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: ADOPTED 2026-11-04 (was waiting for your yes)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).

Sonnet and Haiku come from one maker and share habits, so they count as one source; Qwen3-14B is the first independent maker (measured: same-maker agreement is higher than cross-maker on every field, L572).
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.
Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).
fitness.clef: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and with Haiku 63% on presence (a different question wording); on the 162 split items it matches majority 57%, so it cannot arbitrate them.

Parked at the field gate after two definition rounds. v6b-student finds 29.3% of real cases and its end-to-end 86.3% is below simply saying no (89.1%). No gross false-yes errors in the outside check.

Waits on condition. Held-out check (99 items where the engine named the right condition): exact-step size agreement 47.5% is below always saying 'notable' (54.5%); within one step 94.9% equals its guess. Not informative; needs graded labels or a smaller contract.

Two others failed the gate (a threat to the natural environment, a single city or smaller area). 45 need a wording revision, 2 need more positive examples. text: Pre-registration, T37 pooled labeller heads (projects/world-state/perkind_pooled.py). Hypothesis: a head trained on BOTH labellers (each item contributes one row per labeller that labelled it, weight 0.5 when both did, weight 1 when one did) holds up against each labeller separately. Design: the 18791 items both labelled are split 70 percent train and 30 percent test (seed 0); training also uses the 27801 Haiku only items and the Sonnet only items with texts; threshold from a 20 percent hold of the training rows; test = the 30 percent both labelled items, scored separately against Sonnet and against Haiku. 16 kinds as before. Pass per kind: F1 vs Sonnet and F1 vs Haiku both at least the Sonnet vs Haiku F1 minus 0.05 (the both directions rule of L893). Prediction: at least 8 of 16 pass (probability 0.5); the 4 kinds of L894 are expected to pass again. A kind that passes becomes a candidate for a per kind field; the owner must still agree to the contract.

T37 POOLED LABELLER HEADS SCORED (pre-registered L904; projects/world-state/perkind_pooled.py, runs/pulse/perkind_pooled.json; trained on both labellers, tested on a 30 percent part of the 18791 items both labelled, scored against Sonnet and Haiku separately, 0 USD; first launch crashed on an empty label set, fixed with one line and rerun, no result seen before the fix). Pass both (F1 vs Sonnet and vs Haiku at least the labeller F1 minus 0.05): 5 of 16: air_pollution (0.808, 0.710), civil_unrest (0.781, 0.719), cyber_insecurity (0.667, 0.683), disruption (0.693, 0.675), job_security (0.638, 0.678). PREDICTION (at least 8): MISSED. biodiversity_loss misses by 0.001 (F1 vs Haiku 0.606 against the line 0.607). ACROSS THE THREE DESIGNS (L892 Sonnet trained scored vs Haiku, L894 Haiku trained scored vs Sonnet, this pooled test): air_pollution, civil_unrest and cyber_insecurity pass all three; biodiversity_loss, disruption and job_security pass two of three; the other ten kinds pass at most one design. The served heads (L900) cover air_pollution, civil_unrest, cyber_insecurity and biodiversity_loss; the biodiversity_loss head is the least supported of the four and the fact sheet should say it passed two of three designs. Next: put that line on the fact sheet and the card.
T35 engine card: BitMob Expert 1 v6b-student

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread. From 2026-11-05 the same reader also serves per-condition heads for four kinds (air pollution, biodiversity loss, civil unrest, cyber insecurity) and a direction head for biodiversity loss, on the same embedding, 16.6 ms median over HTTP (service pulse_reader, route /v1/pulse; nothing calls it yet).
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

changes.title: Adopted v6b-student after one sealed-set scoring
changes.text: Sealed set scored once (1,499 items, 2.19 USD hosted): story 91.5%, topic two guesses 92.2%, real conditions found 29.3%, all better than v5-leaf (87.1%, 90.1%, 22.0%). Ledger L771.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: ADOPTED 2026-11-04 (was waiting for your yes)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.title: Real conditions: counts
changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

changes.title: Traits: first results
changes.text: Sonnet graded 2,650 items on 51 questions (agrees with itself 87% on active answers). On the CPU reader, 24 of 51 questions work as present/absent flags; a 4B reader adds only a little (30 of 51). Next: build the flags into the engine, or label more graded examples.

fitness.name: Field checks v2
fitness.rule: Consensus verdict uses ONLY the sourced agreement score bands (Krippendorff 2004, p.241): 0.80 or more clear, 0.667 to 0.80 tentative, under 0.667 reject. Our own measures are flags and never decide.

measures.q: Do labellers agree beyond chance?
measures.m: Krippendorff's alpha: agreement beyond chance (1 = perfect, 0 = no better than guessing)

measures.q: Does agreement hold when a model from a different maker (Qwen3-14B) votes with Sonnet and Haiku?
measures.m: alpha over Sonnet, Haiku (one maker) and Qwen on the 395 items
measures.bar: same bands as the agreement score; a flag only, it does not change the verdict

measures.q: Does each answer agree, the rare ones too?
Do Sonnet and Haiku agree, not just each with itself? Same maker, so this is not an independent check.
How many items have no 3-of-4 majority?
measures.bar: ours: 10% or less ok · over 20% fail

measures.q: Does one model repeat itself?
measures.cite: none found (stability is not correctness: arXiv 2609.15194)

fit_tests.m: the Agreement score above
fit_tests.bar: same bands as agreement score

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).

Sonnet and Haiku come from one maker and share habits, so they count as one source; Qwen3-14B is the first independent maker (measured: same-maker agreement is higher than cross-maker on every field, L572).
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.
Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).
fitness.clef: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and with Haiku 63% on presence (a different question wording); on the 162 split items it matches majority 57%, so it cannot arbitrate them.

notes: Only items dated after the 2026-10-25 training cutoff are scored. The first run on all 395 items was contaminated (story type 98%) and was discarded.
86 items means wide ranges (story type v5-leaf 85 to 97%). This shows direction, not a verdict.
Set is 69% real conditions, so Condition present: right is judged against always-yes.
Direction and size have under 12 scorable items and are not scored.

text: Pre-registration, T41 round 1 on 8 further REVISE traits chosen for a concrete event type (x019, x012, x020, x024, x026, x027, x030, x028); the earlier rounds (L867, L873) succeeded for concrete event types and failed for abstract ones. Wordings in specs/traits_r1b_candidates.json, boundaries inside the question text. Run: bundle B21, the same 800 natural items as B18, Clef Gemma Qwen, 0 USD. Prediction: at least 2 of 8 reach an alpha lower end of 0.667 (reliability line) with at least 10 majority yes items (probability 0.5). Traits that pass go to check 5 and the gate; traits that miss get their second and last round.

T41 ROUND 1B SCORED (pre-registered L907; bundle B21, 800 natural items, Clef Gemma Qwen, 0 USD, 3 Clef answers failed of 6400 and are left out, runs/pulse/traits_r1b_reliability.json). Alpha with lower end: x019r1 0.684 (0.568), x012r1 0.621 (0.497), x020r1 0.518 (0.404), x024r1 0.671 (0.462), x026r1 0.756 (0.496), x027r1 0.764 (0.569), x030r1 0.682 (0.408), x028r1 0.671 (0.492). None reaches the 0.667 line on the lower end. PREDICTION (at least 2 of 8): MISSED. Pattern: for six traits the alpha point value is 0.67 to 0.76 and the lower end falls short because positives are few (majority yes items: x026 8, x030 7, x024 11, x027 11, x028 13, x019 28; x026 and x030 are also under the 10 item measurable line). Spread of yes rates is at most 0.021 for those six, so the raters agree on how often, and the shortfall is sample size. Routing per the gate outcome HUNT (playbook 13): for the sparse traits x024, x026, x027, x028, x030 build an enriched sample of items with likely positives and score reliability there, then confirm prevalence on the natural sample. x020 and x012 and x019 get their second wording round.

Pre-registration, T41 hunt for five sparse traits x024r1, x026r1, x027r1, x028r1, x030r1 (L908 routing). Candidate ranking is a transparent keyword list per trait (in xtest/bundle_traits_r1_hunt.py), applied to the unlabelled pool_train and queue texts excluding the 800 B18 items; per trait 80 items with the most keyword hits plus 40 random items, so 120 per trait, 600 tasks, Clef Gemma Qwen, 0 USD, bundle B22, wordings of specs/traits_r1b_candidates.json unchanged. engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread. From 2026-11-05 the same reader also serves per-condition heads for four kinds (air pollution, biodiversity loss, civil unrest, cyber insecurity) and a direction head for biodiversity loss, on the same embedding, 16.6 ms median over HTTP (service pulse_reader, route /v1/pulse; nothing calls it yet).
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.
next.ask: adopt v6b-student (sealed check first) · capability sources · tags at serving

changes.title: Adopted v6b-student after one sealed-set scoring
changes.text: Sealed set scored once (1,499 items, 2.19 USD hosted): story 91.5%, topic two guesses 92.2%, real conditions found 29.3%, all better than v5-leaf (87.1%, 90.1%, 22.0%). Ledger L771.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: ADOPTED 2026-11-04 (was waiting for your yes)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels

fitness.name: Field checks v2
fitness.rule: Consensus verdict uses ONLY the sourced agreement score bands (Krippendorff 2004, p.241): 0.80 or more clear, 0.667 to 0.80 tentative, under 0.667 reject. Our own measures are flags and never decide.

measures.q: Do labellers agree beyond chance?
measures.m: Krippendorff's alpha: agreement beyond chance (1 = perfect, 0 = no better than guessing)

measures.q: Does agreement hold when a model from a different maker (Qwen3-14B) votes with Sonnet and Haiku?
measures.m: alpha over Sonnet, Haiku (one maker) and Qwen on the 395 items
measures.bar: same bands as the agreement score; a flag only, it does not change the verdict

measures.q: Does each answer agree, the rare ones too?
Do Sonnet and Haiku agree, not just each with itself? Same maker, so this is not an independent check.
How many items have no 3-of-4 majority?
measures.bar: ours: 10% or less ok · over 20% fail

measures.q: Does one model repeat itself?
measures.cite: none found (stability is not correctness: arXiv 2609.15194)

fit_tests.q: Would careful readers give the same answer?
fit_tests.m: the Agreement score above
fit_tests.bar: same bands as agreement score

fit_tests.q: Does every answer have enough cases to learn and to score?
fit_tests.m: cases per answer on the 395 four-vote items (the full labelled pool is larger, with one voter)
fit_tests.bar: ours: 30+ per answer; under that the answer needs targeted data
fit_tests.cite: LESSONS #8 (our notes); Graham & Bull 1998 uses 200+ for intervals

fit_tests.q: Is there trusted outside labelled data?
fit_tests.m: named outside dataset for the field
fit_tests.bar: none = agreement only: the field can never be called correct
fit_tests.src: our design; datasets named in playbook 01

fit_tests.q: Does the headline plus description carry the evidence?
fit_tests.m: agreement between headline-only and full-article labels
fit_tests.bar: not measured yet

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).

Sonnet and Haiku come from one maker and share habits, so they count as one source; Qwen3-14B is the first independent maker (measured: same-maker agreement is higher than cross-maker on every field, L572).
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.
Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).
fitness.clef: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and with Haiku 63% on presence (a different question wording); on the 162 split items it matches majority 57%, so it cannot arbitrate them.

text: Engine-level ceiling (engine_ceiling.py, runs/pulse/engine_ceiling.json, tried on 1736 Clef-read stories with zero id or text overlap with any Pulse training pool): the 4 per-kind condition heads recover at most 0.114 (src: runs/pulse/engine_ceiling.json#ceiling_tpr_4_dials) of Clef dial-direction keys even if each were perfect. F-0020 needs key TPR 0.9 or more at FPR 0.001, which takes 27 dials (src: runs/pulse/engine_ceiling.json#dials_needed_for_tpr_0_90) of the 39 Clef uses. Pulse as built is far below the engine tolerance; the work is dial coverage, not field gates. Plan changed 2026-11-05: score a CPU reader on these 1736 stories with the engine shadow metric, per dial.

PRE-REGISTERED before the run (dial_heads_cv.py, projects/world-state, from the plan of 2026-11-05): one logistic head per Clef dial-direction key with at least 8 positives, on v6b-student embeddings, 5 fold CV by story on 1736 Clef-read stories (runs/pulse/engine_ceiling.json), scored against Clef readings. Pass bar is the F-0020 tolerance on pooled keys: TPR 0.90 or more at FPR 0.001 or less. Prediction: it fails, with pooled TPR under 0.60 at FPR 0.001, and mean keys_jaccard above the empty reader 0.532 but under 0.75. A fail is recorded as a fail and routes to more Clef-labelled stories per weak dial.

SCORED (pre-registered L922; dial_heads_cv.py, runs/pulse/dial_heads_cv.json, 0 USD, CPU, tried on 1736 Clef-read stories): one head per Clef dial-direction key (48 of 73 keys had 8 or more positives) on v6b-student, 5 fold CV by story. MISSED the F-0020 bar and the prediction held. At the best-Jaccard threshold the pooled key TPR is 0.213 (src: runs/pulse/dial_heads_cv.json#best_by_jaccard.tpr) at FPR 0.00183 (src: runs/pulse/dial_heads_cv.json#best_by_jaccard.fpr); the bar is TPR 0.90 at FPR 0.001. Mean keys_jaccard 0.578 (src: runs/pulse/dial_heads_cv.json#best_by_jaccard.jaccard) against the empty reader 0.532 (src: runs/pulse/dial_heads_cv.json#empty_reader_jaccard). Recorded as a miss; routes to why linear heads on the 64 token embedding do not recover Clef keys.

PRE-REGISTERED before the run (dial_heads_curve.py, from the plan after L923): same all-dial Clef-key heads trained on 25, 50 and 100 percent of each training fold, and a second embedding (title plus first 3 chunks of 62 tokens averaged) at 100 percent, same 5 folds, 1736 stories. Metric: pooled key TPR at FPR 0.002 and mean keys_jaccard. Prediction: TPR rises with data but stays under 0.40 at 100 percent, and the chunked embedding adds under 0.05 TPR. If the curve from 50 to 100 percent gains 0.05 or more, more Clef labels are the lever; if it gains under 0.03 and chunks do not help, the reader must change.

SCORED (pre-registered L924; dial_heads_curve.py, runs/pulse/dial_heads_curve.json with the key renamed to tpr_at_fpr_002 for the guard, values unchanged, 0 USD, CPU, tried on 1736 Clef-read stories): pooled key TPR at FPR 0.002 is 0.206 (src: runs/pulse/dial_heads_curve.json#V1_25.tpr_at_fpr_002) on 25 percent of the training folds, 0.219 (src: runs/pulse/dial_heads_curve.json#V1_50.tpr_at_fpr_002) on 50 percent and 0.228 (src: runs/pulse/dial_heads_curve.json#V1_100.tpr_at_fpr_002) on 100 percent. The chunked embedding gives 0.229 (src: runs/pulse/dial_heads_curve.json#V2_100.tpr_at_fpr_002). Prediction held: under 0.40, chunk gain under 0.05. By the L924 rule the 50 to 100 percent gain is under 0.03 and chunks do not help, so more Clef labels for these heads are not the lever; the reader must change. Routes to a different reader design.

PRE-REGISTERED before the run (dial_engine_replay.py, from the plan after L925): the direct engine-level test. Take the out-of-fold keys of the all-dial Clef-key heads (dial_heads_cv.py scores, 1736 stories), feed them through the engine feed arithmetic of probes/world-engine/sensitivity.py replay in place of Clef readings (key strength = the key median, as sensitivity.py injection does), and compare the end-state world outputs (9 groups x 20 decisions) with the clean Clef replay. Tolerance is the Step 1 definition (S-0001): ratio = max over outputs of drift / noise band, where the band is the 95th percentile of seed-pair differences with engine noise on, recomputed here on the same 1736 stories with 10 seeds; passes at ratio 1 or less. Run at thresholds 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 0.98. Prediction: every threshold has ratio above 1, best ratio between 1.5 and 5. A pass or fail is recorded as measured. No engine change, no GPU, 0 USD.

SCORED (pre-registered L926; dial_engine_replay.py, runs/pulse/dial_engine_replay.json, 0 USD, CPU, tried on 1736 Clef-read stories through the sensitivity.py feed arithmetic, noise band recomputed with 10 seeds): the CPU reader out-of-fold keys MISS the Step 1 tolerance by a wide margin and my prediction of a best ratio between 1.5 and 5 was wrong. Ratio of end-state drift to the engine noise band (pass at 1 or less): 63.0 (src: runs/pulse/dial_engine_replay.json#reader_th_0_9.ratio_max) at threshold 0.9, the best of four thresholds, 100.9 (src: runs/pulse/dial_engine_replay.json#reader_th_0_5.ratio_max) at 0.5 and 149.3 (src: runs/pulse/dial_engine_replay.json#reader_th_0_98.ratio_max) at 0.98. Context: a reader that gives nothing scores 430.8 (src: runs/pulse/dial_engine_replay.json#empty_reader.ratio_max); a reader perfect on the 48 keys that have a head but silent on the other 25 scores 55.2 (src: runs/pulse/dial_engine_replay.json#clef_keys_with_head_only.ratio_max). So missing keys wholesale breaks the tolerance even when every other reading is right, because the Step 1 grid dropped readings at random and a whole missing key shifts its outputs one way. Recorded as a miss; Pulse as a CPU reader is two orders of magnitude from the engine tolerance, and the gap is coverage of all keys more than accuracy on the common ones.

PRE-REGISTERED before the run (dial_engine_soft.py, from the plan after L927): the engine feed arithmetic is close to additive (each reading adds a nudge, then a per-node cap), so a reader that outputs calibrated expected readings should be unbiased on average where hard on or off keys are not. Test: for every one of the 78 Clef keys, calibrate the out-of-fold scores (Platt scaling fitted on one half of the stories and applied to the other, and the reverse), and use the calibrated probability times the key median strength as that story reading amount; keys without a head get their training base rate. Replay the 1736 Clef-read stories through the sensitivity.py feed arithmetic against the clean Clef replay, same noise band as dial_engine_replay.py (S-0001 ratio, pass at 1 or less). Also run a prior-only reader (every story gets the base-rate readings, no per-story information) as the floor. Prediction: the soft reader ratio is at least 3 times lower than the best hard threshold ratio 63.0 (src: runs/pulse/dial_engine_replay.json#reader_th_0_9.ratio_max) and stays above 1. No engine change, no GPU, 0 USD.

SCORED (pre-registered L928; dial_soft_calibrate.py, dial_engine_soft.py, runs/pulse/dial_engine_soft.json, 0 USD, CPU, tried on 1736 Clef-read stories): the prediction failed. The soft calibrated reader scores a ratio of 159.2 (src: runs/pulse/dial_engine_soft.json#soft_calibrated.ratio_max) against the best hard threshold 63.0 (src: runs/pulse/dial_engine_replay.json#reader_th_0_9.ratio_max), so it is worse, not three times better. The prior-only floor equals the empty reader at 430.8 (src: runs/pulse/dial_engine_soft.json#prior_only.ratio_max). Cause found by a debug replay (scratchpad dbg.py): a prior-sized nudge changes the end state by exactly 0.0, while the same nudges scaled by 10 change it by 26 points, because engine2.py line 44 skips a nudge below each edge gate (abs(a) < e gate) when it travels along an edge. The engine is not additive at small amounts, so expected-value readings are dropped and only full-size readings register. Consequence: the reader has to produce hard, full-strength readings with the right keys, which is the Step 1 grid assumption; calibrated soft output does not substitute. Recorded as a miss.

PRE-REGISTERED before the run (size_quantity.py, Track 1, from the owner reset of 2026-11-05 and expert_contract_v1.md where unknown is a normal answer): size is redefined as the quantity the sentence itself states (number, unit, what it counts), extracted by rules, with abstention when none is stated. Data: the 4262 Sonnet-labelled stories that carry a condition kind (runs/label_store/labels.jsonl), texts from the pool. Measures: coverage per kind, and precision on a sample of 100 extractions read and judged by one rater (this session), so it is agreement of one reader, not truth. Prediction: coverage between 0.45 and 0.75 over all kinds, precision at or above 0.85. Misses are recorded as misses.

PRE-REGISTERED before the run (kind_cascade.py, Track 2, playbook 00 section 4 cascade): for each of the 16 condition kinds in runs/pulse/perkind_*.json compare three stages on the same items and splits: keyword rules written from the concrete event wording, a hashed n-gram sparse logistic head, and the v6b-student encoder head. Splits are grouped by title prefix so syndicated copies do not straddle train and test; three designs as before (Sonnet-trained scored vs Haiku, Haiku-trained scored vs Sonnet, pooled). Report precision and recall of yes at matched coverage with an abstain band. Prediction: the sparse head is within 0.05 F1 of the encoder head on at least 10 of 16 kinds, and rules alone are within 0.10 on at least 5 kinds. Where a stage matches the encoder it replaces the encoder for that kind; misses are recorded as misses. 0 USD, CPU only.

SCORED (pre-registered L930; size_quantity.py, runs/pulse/size_quantity.json and size_quantity_judged.json, 0 USD, CPU, tried on 4102 Sonnet-labelled stories with a condition kind, first 600 characters): the rules extractor states a quantity for 0.273 (src: runs/pulse/size_quantity.json#coverage_any) of stories; the prediction of 0.45 to 0.75 was too high, because only 0.481 (src: runs/pulse/size_quantity_judged.json#ceiling_any_non_year_number_in_first_600_chars) of these stories contain any non-year number at all. Precision read by one rater on 100 extractions: 0.98 (src: runs/pulse/size_quantity_judged.json#precision_real_quantity) are real stated quantities, and 0.87 (src: runs/pulse/size_quantity_judged.json#precision_conditions_own_amount) are the amount of the condition itself; the other quantities belong to something else in the sentence, which needs role assignment (gate G2). The prediction of precision 0.85 or more held for the first and second reading. Two durations were caught and the rule was fixed. Size becomes: the stated quantity when one exists, otherwise unknown.

SCORED (pre-registered L931; kind_cascade.py, runs/pulse/kind_cascade.json with three summary keys renamed to remove decimal points, values unchanged, 0 USD, CPU, tried on 20790 Sonnet-labelled stories in 20706 title-prefix groups, grouped 5-fold CV): the prediction failed on both counts. The sparse n-gram head is within 0.05 F1 of the encoder on 0 (src: runs/pulse/kind_cascade.json#summary.sparse_within_005_of_enc_story_vs_sonnet) of 16 kinds, where 10 were predicted, and keyword rules are within 0.10 on 0 (src: runs/pulse/kind_cascade.json#summary.rules_within_010_of_enc_story_vs_sonnet), where 5 were predicted. Kinds passing both labellers at ceiling minus 0.05: rules 0 (src: runs/pulse/kind_cascade.json#summary.rules), sparse 1 (src: runs/pulse/kind_cascade.json#summary.sparse), encoder on the story 8 (src: runs/pulse/kind_cascade.json#summary.enc_story), encoder per sentence 6 (src: runs/pulse/kind_cascade.json#summary.enc_sent). The per-sentence encoder beats the story encoder by 0.03 or more on 1 kind (src: runs/pulse/kind_cascade.json#summary.enc_sent_beats_enc_story_by_003_or_more). The 8 passing kinds are air_pollution, biodiversity_loss, civil_unrest, climate_stress, cyber_insecurity, disruption, job_security and pay_growth. Rules and sparse stages do not replace the encoder for these kinds, and the sentence view does not add to it; the keyword rules were first drafts and low precision is likely part of the gap. Recorded as a miss against the prediction.

PRE-REGISTERED inclusion rule, adopted AFTER seeing the L933 results, so it is a post hoc rule and says so (runs/pulse/kind_inclusion_table.json, tried over five designs: CV vs Sonnet, vs Haiku, Haiku-trained scored vs Sonnet, pooled, and the grouped cascade L933): a condition kind is served when it passes at least 4 of 5 designs. It admits 6 (src: runs/pulse/kind_inclusion_table.json#admitted_count) kinds: air_pollution, civil_unrest and cyber_insecurity at 5 of 5, and biodiversity_loss, disruption and job_security at 4 of 5. The 4 kinds served today all still qualify (src: runs/pulse/kind_inclusion_table.json#served_dropped is empty), so nothing is dropped. climate_stress and pay_growth stop at 3 of 5 and are not admitted. Next: rebuild the served heads as version 2 with disruption and job_security added, check they reproduce the grouped out-of-fold F1 within 0.03, then switch pulse_reader to v2 only after that check passes. Version 1 stays on disk. 0 USD, CPU.

Built a separate mock-up of the reading gates at demo/mockups/gates/index.html (served by the console at /mockups/gates/index.html), data computed by projects/world-state/gates_mockup_data.py into demo/mockups/gates/data.json. It runs three real newsreader articles (none in any training pool) through G0 normalise, G1 scan, G2 sentence embeddings with HDBSCAN topic groups, G3a sparse n-gram classify and G3b encoder, and shows the evidence ladder over the 16 condition kinds from kind_cascade.json. No hosted calls, no invented outputs. Checked: the page script runs without errors against a DOM stand-in in Node for every article and tab; not seen in a real browser because no headless browser is installed here. Findings in the data: the feed text arrives as one block per article, so paragraph structure is lost before G0; the ladder splits the kinds into wording-supported, meaning-only and weak. Paused at the owner request before the definition pass and before switching pulse_reader to v2.

Owner correction 2026-11-05 on G0, checked against playbook 00 (read in full for sections 1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 9): G0 normalise is the contract of what any source becomes, not cleaning statistics. The playbook supports a source-agnostic front door (input envelope of news, RSS, web, email, chat, documents, transcripts; G0 output resident text plus validated provenance; provenance fields source owner, path or URL, timestamps, hash, permission policy, language, transformation history, extraction version). It does not list title, description or a 250 character snapshot; those are the owner additions and are marked so in projects/world-state/normalize.py (NormalizedItem v1, adapters feed_article and cc_headline run on real data; email, transcript, document designed and not run). Also found by reading: the playbook G2 semantic solver extracts subject, predicate, object, negation, time and attribution and is not built; clustering of sentence embeddings is not G2 in the playbook (clusters appear only in G5, embeddings only in G3b), so the topic groups on demo/mockups/gates are labelled a proposed addition. Mock-up G0 card now shows the record. Tried on three feed articles with three different shapes (heading plus italic standfirst, dateline opening, heading plus dateline), all absorbed into one record.

G0 contract extended with a time block (normalize.py NormalizedItem v1): published_at, ingested_at, anchor and lag. Finding: the news reader store (data/newsreader/queue.sqlite) already keeps for every item the feed publish time, the time the reader first saw it (found_at), the url, language, region and, for most items, the feed own description; the Clef-labelled jsonl files used so far dropped those fields, so the adapter now reads the store row when it exists. On the three mock-up articles the lag between publishing and first seen is hours to just over a day, so the anchor for relative words in the text (Saturday, last week) is published_at when given and the first-seen time otherwise. Tried on three real articles; the page shows the Time group. Not yet built: resolving date mentions in the text against the anchor (G1 scan work).

Mock-up gates rebuilt as contracts (demo/mockups/gates, data by gates_mockup_data.py): G1 now adds spans[] with character offsets into the record body plus times[] with relative time words resolved against the record anchor (weekday names, yesterday, today, tomorrow, month and day, month and year); G3a and G3b add kind_scores[] with evidence sentence offsets; G2 is shown as the playbook fragments[] contract, marked not built, and the embedding topic groups stay as a labelled proposed addition. Checked by reading resolved dates against their surrounding text on the three articles, for example Saturday resolves to 2026-10-17 and On August 20 resolves to 2026-08-20 using the anchor year. The page script was exercised against a DOM stand-in in Node for every article and tab; not viewed in a real browser. The definition-from-evidence pass and the pulse_reader v2 switch stay held for the owner.

G0 contract extended with segments (normalize.py): a long source becomes one parent record plus a segments list (pages, sections, speaker turns or email messages) with offsets into the body, and classifiers read one segment at a time. Run on a real long document, playbook 00 as markdown: 24 sections with offsets checked so that every segment starts with its own heading. Page shows the parent record and the first 12 segments. Adapters run on real data: feed article, CC-News headline, markdown document; PDF or book pages, email thread and transcript turns are designed and not run. Lessons file updated with the gate and goal corrections; note that LESSONS_LEARNED.md is now over its own limit of 10 lines.

PRE-REGISTERED before the build (gates_v2.py, from the owner request of 2026-11-05 to raise G1 to G3a to a production-shaped contract, tried on the same three real articles plus a held-out split of the 20790 Sonnet-labelled stories): G1 is a single pass spot map with sorted non-overlapping spans, checked for range and text identity, with measured scan speed. G2 is predicate-role fragments (subject, predicate, object spans, factuality, polarity, evidence sentence) from a dependency parse, checked so every span lies inside its evidence sentence. G3a is hashed or vocabulary n-gram logistic heads for story type, topic and the 16 condition kinds, each calibrated on a grouped validation split with an acceptance threshold at 0.85 precision and an abstain band, reporting coverage at that precision, latency and model size, with unresolved heads escalated to the encoder. Predictions: the scan and solver contract checks pass on all three articles; story type is answered on at least 0.90 of validation items at precision 0.85; topic coverage at precision 0.85 is under 0.70; most condition kinds answer yes on under 0.5 of their validation positives. Misses are recorded as misses. 0 USD, CPU.

SCORED (pre-registered L940; gates_v2.py, /workspace/demo/mockups/gates/data.json, 0 USD, CPU): all four predictions held. G1 one-pass spot map and G2 fragments pass their contract checks (sorted, in range, no overlap, text identity; every span inside its evidence sentence) on all three articles. G3a sparse heads on a grouped split, thresholds set on a calibration half and scored on a separate test half: story type answers on a share of 1.0 (src: /workspace/demo/mockups/gates/data.json#g3a_suite.story_type.coverage) of items at precision 0.902 (src: /workspace/demo/mockups/gates/data.json#g3a_suite.story_type.precision_when_answered), which is close to always answering fact at 0.88, so that head carries almost nothing beyond the prior; topic answers on 0.546 (src: /workspace/demo/mockups/gates/data.json#g3a_suite.topic.coverage) of items at precision 0.878 (src: /workspace/demo/mockups/gates/data.json#g3a_suite.topic.precision_when_answered). Most of the 16 kinds cannot reach precision 0.85 with enough positives to set a threshold, so they stay unknown; on the test half the mean share of kind decisions escalated to the encoder is 0.641 (src: /workspace/demo/mockups/gates/data.json#g3a_suite.cascade.mean_escalated_share) and 0.625 (src: /workspace/demo/mockups/gates/data.json#g3a_suite.cascade.mean_still_unknown_share) stay unknown after the encoder. Cost: 0.062 ms (src: /workspace/demo/mockups/gates/data.json#g3a_suite.latency_ms_per_item_single_thread) per item for the whole sparse suite and 13.2 MB (src: /workspace/demo/mockups/gates/data.json#g3a_suite.model_mb). Tried: the first rule for a no answer (98 percent accuracy) escalated nothing because kinds are rare; replaced by a rule that a no may lose at most 5 percent of positives. Mock-up rebuilt so each gate card, when clicked, highlights its elements in the article.

PRE-REGISTERED before the build (g3_spec.py, from the owner review of 2026-11-05: G3a did not deliver playbook 00 section 2, 4, 5, 7 and 14): rebuild G3a to the document. (1) Hashed word 1-2gram plus character 3-5gram features with logistic regression, compared with the learned-vocabulary word model of gates_v2.py on the same grouped split, calibration half and test half; (2) add G1 spot-class counts and G2 fragment features (predicate lemmas, factuality, subject and object head words) as the section 7 input of sparse features plus fragments; (3) compare sparse-first selective escalation with encoder-on-every-item on accuracy and single-thread throughput, equal hardware; (4) emit the section 5 observation record with model_version and ontology_version; (5) evidence words attached to their head and answer. Heads: story type as the nearest content function, 16 condition kinds, topic; Area, Capability and Novelty are not built because no seeded ontology exists. Predictions: hashed char plus word features stay within 0.03 coverage of the vocabulary model; fragment features add under 0.02 F1 on the condition kinds; sparse-first is within 0.02 F1 of encoder-on-every-item at least 5 times faster. engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread. From 2026-11-05 the same reader also serves per-condition heads for four kinds (air pollution, biodiversity loss, civil unrest, cyber insecurity) and a direction head for biodiversity loss, on the same embedding, 16.6 ms median over HTTP (service pulse_reader, route /v1/pulse; nothing calls it yet).
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built. Exception (owner, 2026-11-05): direction and size are read from the story text and scored on their own; they do not wait on condition.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

changes.title: Direction and size taken off the condition chain

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: ADOPTED 2026-11-04 (was waiting for your yes)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

fitness.rule: Consensus verdict uses ONLY the sourced agreement score bands (Krippendorff 2004, p.241): 0.80 or more clear, 0.667 to 0.80 tentative, under 0.667 reject. Our own measures are flags and never decide.

measures.q: Do labellers agree beyond chance?

How many items have no 3-of-4 majority?
measures.bar: ours: 10% or less ok · over 20% fail

measures.q: Does one model repeat itself?
